at sagsøge.explanation: "At sagsøge" means "to sue", to take a person or a company to court to demand money or a ruling: sagsøge en virksomhed (to sue a company). The one who sues is called sagsøgeren (the plaintiff).

sentence.da: Hun vil **sagsøge** firmaet, fordi det ikke betalte hende.
sentence.en: She wants to sue the firm because it did not pay her.

at samarbejde.explanation: "At samarbejde" means "to cooperate", built from sam (together) and arbejde (work). The person you work with comes after med (with): Jeg samarbejder med naboen (I cooperate with the neighbor).

sentence.da: Vi skal **samarbejde** for at løse opgaven.
sentence.en: We have to work together to solve the task.

at samle.explanation: "At samle" means "to gather" or "to collect": Læreren samler børnene (The teacher gathers the children). For a hobby, add på: Jeg samler på frimærker (I collect stamps). It can also mean to put together: Jeg samler en reol (I am putting together a bookcase).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **samle** på gamle mønter.
sentence.en: My brother wants to collect old coins.

at samle på.explanation: "At samle på" means "to collect" as a hobby, like stamps or coins. Without på, at samle means "to gather" or "to pick up": Hun samler blomster (She picks flowers).

sentence.da: Min søn vil **samle på** frimærker.
sentence.en: My son wants to collect stamps.

at sammenfatte.explanation: "At sammenfatte" means "to summarize", to gather the main points of a long text or talk into a short form: sammenfatte rapporten (to summarize the report). Sammen means "together", so you put the points together.

sentence.da: Kan du **sammenfatte** mødet i tre linjer?
sentence.en: Can you summarize the meeting in three lines?

at sammenkalde.explanation: "At sammenkalde" means "to convene", to call people together for a meeting. It is used when someone with authority, such as a boss, a board or a government, makes the call: sammenkalde et møde (to call a meeting).

sentence.da: Formanden vil **sammenkalde** bestyrelsen til et møde i morgen.
sentence.en: The chairman will convene the board for a meeting tomorrow.

at sammenligne.explanation: "At sammenligne" means "to compare" and is used with med (with): Jeg sammenligner prisen med prisen i går (I compare the price with yesterday's price). It is built from sammen (together) and ligne (to look like).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sammenligne** priserne i to butikker.
sentence.en: I want to compare the prices in two stores.

at sammensætte.explanation: "At sammensætte" means "to put together", to join separate parts into one whole, such as a team, a menu or a piece of furniture. A word made of two words is et sammensat ord (a compound word).

sentence.da: Træneren skal **sammensætte** et hold til næste kamp.
sentence.en: The coach has to put together a team for the next match.

at sanse.explanation: "At sanse" means "to sense", to notice something through your eyes, ears, nose, skin or tongue. It is also used for noticing a mood without being told: Hun sanser, at han er nervøs (She senses that he is nervous).

sentence.da: Hun kan **sanse**, når nogen er ked af det.
sentence.en: She can sense when someone is sad.

at satse.explanation: "At satse" means "to bet" and "to go for". With på (on), it means to put your hope or effort on one choice: Hun satser på en karriere som musiker (She is going for a career as a musician). To put money on a game or race is also at satse: Han satsede hundrede kroner på hesten (He bet a hundred kroner on the horse).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **satse** på en uddannelse i stedet for et job.
sentence.en: I want to go for an education instead of a job.

at savne.explanation: "At savne" means "to miss" someone or something that is not here. It is not used for a missed bus. For that, Danes say Jeg nåede ikke bussen (I did not catch the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **savne** min familie meget.
sentence.en: I will miss my family a lot.

at scanne.explanation: "At scanne" means "to scan", either to copy a paper into a computer or to read a barcode with a phone camera. Danish uses the same word for both.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **scanne** brevet og sende det.
sentence.en: I want to scan the letter and send it.

at score.explanation: "At score" means "to score" in sports, when a player puts the ball in the net or over the line.

sentence.da: Han vil **score** et mål i kampen.
sentence.en: He wants to score a goal in the match.

at scrolle.explanation: "At scrolle" means "to scroll", to move up or down a page on a screen. Use ned (down) or op (up) to say which way: scrolle ned (scroll down), scrolle op (scroll up).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **scrolle** i timevis på min telefon.
sentence.en: I can scroll for hours on my phone.

at se.explanation: "At se" means "to see", and also "to watch": Jeg ser en film (I am watching a movie). Jeg kan se, hvad du mener means "I can see what you mean". Vi ses! means "See you!". At kigge (to look) is for looking on purpose: Kig her! (Look here!).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **se** dit hus fra her.
sentence.en: I can see your house from here.

at se bort fra.explanation: "At se bort fra" means "to disregard", to leave something out of account on purpose: Hvis vi ser bort fra prisen, er den en god bil (If we disregard the price, it is a good car). Bort means "away", so it is like looking away from it.

sentence.da: Du kan ikke bare **se bort fra** reglerne.
sentence.en: You cannot just disregard the rules.

at se efter.explanation: "At se efter" means "to look for" and "to check": Jeg ser efter bussen (I am looking out for the bus). It also means checking: Se efter, om døren er låst (Check whether the door is locked).

sentence.da: Kan du **se efter** mine nøgler?
sentence.en: Can you look for my keys?

at se frem til.explanation: "At se frem til" means "to look forward to". It is common at the end of a letter: Jeg ser frem til at høre fra dig (I look forward to hearing from you).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **se frem til** en lang sommerferie.
sentence.en: The children can look forward to a long summer break.

at se ned på.explanation: "At se ned på" means "to look down on", to think a person is worth less than you. It also works for looking down from a high place: Jeg ser ned på gaden (I look down at the street). The opposite is at se op til (to look up to).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **se ned på** folk, bare fordi de er fattige.
sentence.en: You must not look down on people just because they are poor.

at se op til.explanation: "At se op til" means "to look up to", to think highly of someone and want to be like them: Jeg ser op til min lærer (I look up to my teacher).

sentence.da: Børn har ofte brug for nogen at **se op til**.
sentence.en: Children often need someone to look up to.

at se på.explanation: "At se på" means "to look at", with your eyes on something. Do not mix it up with at se (to see) or at lede efter (to look for): Jeg leder efter min nøgle (I am looking for my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **se på** billedet.
sentence.en: I want to look at the picture.

at se tilbage.explanation: "At se tilbage" means "to look back", with your eyes or in your memory. For looking back at the past, add på: se tilbage på sommeren (look back on the summer).

sentence.da: Hun vil **se tilbage** på sin barndom.
sentence.en: She wants to look back on her childhood.

at se tv.explanation: "At se tv" means "to watch TV". Danish uses se (to see) where English says "watch", as in se en film (to watch a movie). At se fjernsyn (to watch television) means the same. Tv is said as two letters, te-ve.

sentence.da: Vi vil **se tv** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to watch TV tonight.

at se ud.explanation: "At se ud" means "to look", in the sense of how something appears: Du ser træt ud (You look tired). Hvordan ser det ud? (What does it look like?) Looking at something with your eyes is at se på (to look at).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **se ud** som en pirat til festen.
sentence.en: My brother has to look like a pirate at the party.

at sejle.explanation: "At sejle" means "to sail", and it covers any trip on water, with or without sails, even by engine. Rowing is a different word, at ro.

sentence.da: Om sommeren vil vi **sejle** til en lille ø.
sentence.en: In the summer, we want to sail to a small island.

at sende.explanation: "At sende" means "to send", for example a letter, a parcel or an email. The person who gets it comes right after sender (send), with no word for "to": Jeg sender dig en besked (I send you a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to send a letter to Mom.

at sende en sms.explanation: "At sende en sms" means "to text", or literally to send an SMS. To say who gets it, put them after sende (send): Jeg sender dig en sms (I send you a text).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende en sms** til min ven.
sentence.en: I want to send a text to my friend.

at servere.explanation: "At servere" means "to serve" food or drinks, for example in a restaurant or for guests at home: Maden bliver serveret klokken 18 (The food is served at 6 pm).

sentence.da: Tjeneren vil **servere** maden nu.
sentence.en: The waiter will serve the food now.

at shoppe.explanation: "At shoppe" means "to shop", mostly for fun, like looking for clothes. For groceries, use at købe ind (to buy groceries): Jeg køber ind til aftensmad (I am buying groceries for dinner).

sentence.da: Vi skal **shoppe** i byen i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going shopping in town this weekend.

at sidde.explanation: "At sidde" means "to sit", the state of already being in a chair. Use ved (at) for the place: Jeg sidder ved computeren (I am sitting at the computer). To sit down is at sætte sig (literally to put oneself).

sentence.da: Du kan **sidde** på stolen.
sentence.en: You can sit on the chair.

at sidde fast.explanation: "At sidde fast" means "to be stuck", the state of not moving: Bilen sidder fast (The car is stuck). It fits a person who cannot go on: Jeg sidder fast med opgaven (I am stuck on the task).

sentence.da: Lastbilen kan **sidde fast** i mudderet.
sentence.en: The truck can end up stuck in the mud.

at sige.explanation: "At sige" means "to say": Hvad siger du? (What are you saying?). At sige hej means "to say hi". To tell a story, use at fortælle (to tell) instead.

sentence.da: Børnene skal **sige** tak.
sentence.en: The children must say thank you.

at sige farvel.explanation: "At sige farvel" means "to say goodbye". Farvel (goodbye) can sound a little final, as if you will not meet again. Among friends, Danes more often say hej hej (bye bye) or vi ses (see you).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sige farvel** til vores gæster.
sentence.en: We have to say goodbye to our guests.

at sige goddag.explanation: "At sige goddag" means "to say hello", literally to say good day. Like "good day" in English, goddag sounds formal or old-fashioned. With friends, you would normally say hej (hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige goddag** til min mor.
sentence.en: You must say hello to my mother.

at sige op.explanation: "At sige op" means "to resign / quit": Han sagde op i går (He quit yesterday). It is also used to cancel something, like a subscription: Jeg sagde mit abonnement op (I canceled my subscription).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sige op** og finde et nyt job.
sentence.en: I want to quit and find a new job.

at sige til.explanation: "At sige til" means "to tell" or "to let know": you speak up so that someone can act. Sig til, hvis du har brug for hjælp (Tell me if you need help). Without til, at sige only means "to say": Hun sagde hej (She said hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige til**, når du er sulten.
sentence.en: You have to let me know when you are hungry.

at sige undskyld.explanation: "At sige undskyld" means "to say sorry". Undskyld alone also gets someone's attention: Undskyld, ved du, hvor stationen er? (Excuse me, do you know where the station is?)

sentence.da: Du skal **sige undskyld** til din bror.
sentence.en: You have to say sorry to your brother.

at signere.explanation: "At signere" means "to sign". For a form or contract, Danes more often say at underskrive (to sign a paper). Signere is common for autographs and for players or artists who sign with a club or label: Spilleren har signeret med klubben (The player has signed with the club).

sentence.da: Forfatteren vil **signere** bøger i boghandlen på lørdag.
sentence.en: The author will sign books in the bookstore on Saturday.

at sigte.explanation: "At sigte" means "to aim" and "to charge". To aim is to point at something you want to hit: Han sigter på dåsen (He aims at the can). To charge is when the police say officially that someone is suspected of a crime: Han er sigtet for tyveri (He is charged with theft).

sentence.da: Skytten skal **sigte**, før hun trykker på aftrækkeren.
sentence.en: The shooter has to aim before she pulls the trigger.

at sikre.explanation: "At sikre" means "to secure" and "to ensure": to fasten or guard something so it cannot get hurt or lost, or to make sure it happens. For example, Vi sikrer, at alle får mad (We make sure everyone gets food). Do not mix it up with at forsikre (to insure).

sentence.da: Du skal **sikre** lasten med stropper, så den ikke falder af.
sentence.en: You must secure the load with straps so that it does not fall off.

at simulere.explanation: "At simulere" means "to simulate", to copy a real situation, usually on a computer, to try it out or practice it. It can also mean to fake: Han simulerer sygdom (He is faking an illness).

sentence.da: Piloterne kan **simulere** en nødlanding i en flysimulator.
sentence.en: The pilots can simulate an emergency landing in a flight simulator.

at sjuske.explanation: "At sjuske" means "to be sloppy", to do something carelessly and too fast, so it is not done well. Add med for the thing: sjuske med lektierne (to be sloppy with the homework).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **sjuske**, når du skriver en vigtig mail.
sentence.en: You must not be sloppy when you write an important email.

at skabe.explanation: "At skabe" means "to create", to bring something new into being. It sounds bigger than at lave (to make). Use lave for everyday things, like lave mad (make food), and skabe for something new, like skabe nye job (create new jobs).

sentence.da: Vi vil **skabe** en ny hjemmeside sammen.
sentence.en: We want to create a new website together.

at skabe sig.explanation: "At skabe sig" means "to make a fuss", to act in an over-the-top way, often to get attention: Barnet skaber sig i butikken (The child is making a scene in the store). It is not the same as at skabe (to create).

sentence.da: Han kan **skabe sig**, når han ikke får sin vilje.
sentence.en: He can make a fuss when he does not get his way.

at skade.explanation: "At skade" means "to harm" or "to damage": Det skader ikke (It does no harm). Regnen skadede huset (The rain damaged the house). To hurt yourself, add sig: Jeg skadede mig (I hurt myself).

sentence.da: For meget sukker kan **skade** dine tænder.
sentence.en: Too much sugar can harm your teeth.

at skaffe.explanation: "At skaffe" means "to get" or "to obtain", often with some effort: Kan du skaffe mad til alle? (Can you get food for everyone?) Just receiving something is at få: Jeg fik en gave (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi kan **skaffe** billetter til dig.
sentence.en: We can get tickets for you.

at skamme sig.explanation: "At skamme sig" means "to be ashamed", to feel bad because you did something wrong or foolish. To tell someone off, Danes say Skam dig! (Shame on you!).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **skamme sig** over at bede om hjælp.
sentence.en: You should not be ashamed of asking for help.

at skele.explanation: "At skele" means "to be cross-eyed", to have eyes that do not point the same way. With til it means "to glance", often with interest or envy: Han skeler til naboens bil (He eyes the neighbor's car).

sentence.da: Drengen skal have briller, fordi han kan **skele**.
sentence.en: The boy needs glasses because he can be cross-eyed.

at skelne.explanation: "At skelne" means "to distinguish", to see or hear that two things are not the same: Jeg kan ikke skelne mellem tvillingerne (I cannot tell the twins apart). It is only about noticing, not about taking things apart, which is at adskille (to separate).

sentence.da: Farveblinde kan have svært ved at **skelne** rød fra grøn.
sentence.en: Colorblind people can have trouble telling red from green.

at skifte.explanation: "At skifte" means "to change" by swapping one thing for another: Jeg skifter dæk (I change tires). To make something different, use at ændre: Jeg ændrer planen (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skifte** tøj, når vi kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I want to change clothes when we get home.

at skifte mening.explanation: "At skifte mening" means "to change one's mind" about an opinion or a decision. For a thing, like a shirt, use plain skifte (change): skifte skjorte (change a shirt).

sentence.da: Du kan **skifte mening**, når du vil.
sentence.en: You can change your mind whenever you want.

at skifte tøj.explanation: "At skifte tøj" means "to change clothes". At skifte on its own means "to change" or "to switch" something, such as skifte job (to change jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg er våd og vil **skifte tøj**.
sentence.en: I am wet and want to change clothes.

at skifte ud.explanation: "At skifte ud" means "to replace": you swap an old thing for a new one. Ud (out) shows the old thing going out: Jeg skifter pæren ud (I replace the light bulb). In sports it means to substitute a player, taking one out and putting another in.

sentence.da: Træneren vil **skifte ud** midt i kampen.
sentence.en: The coach wants to substitute in the middle of the game.

at skildre.explanation: "At skildre" means "to depict", to show a person, a place or an event in words or pictures, in a book, a film or a painting: Filmen skildrer krigen (The film depicts the war).

sentence.da: Maleren vil **skildre** havnen i et stort maleri.
sentence.en: The painter wants to depict the harbor in a large painting.

at skille.explanation: "At skille" means "to separate", to pull two things apart: Jeg skiller sort tøj fra hvidt (I separate black clothes from white). It is also used for divorce: De blev skilt (They got divorced).

sentence.da: Du skal **skille** æggeblommen fra hviden.
sentence.en: You have to separate the yolk from the white.

at skilles.explanation: "At skilles" means "to separate", and for a couple "to divorce". It also means parting ways: Vi skilles ved stationen (We part at the station).

sentence.da: Mine forældre vil **skilles**, men de er venner.
sentence.en: My parents want to get divorced, but they are friends.

at skinne.explanation: "At skinne" means "to shine", like the sun or a lamp. It also works for people who look happy: Hun skinner af glæde (She glows with joy).

sentence.da: Solen vil **skinne** hele weekenden.
sentence.en: The sun will shine all weekend.

at skjule.explanation: "At skjule" means "to hide", so others cannot see or find something. It also works for feelings: Hun skjuler sin vrede (She is hiding her anger).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skjule** pakken under sengen.
sentence.en: I will hide the package under the bed.

at skrabe.explanation: "At skrabe" means "to scrape", to pull a hard edge across a surface to remove something from it: Han skrabede malingen af væggen (He scraped the paint off the wall). Danes also use it for carrots: at skrabe gulerødder (to peel carrots).

sentence.da: Jeg må **skrabe** isen af forruden, før jeg kan køre.
sentence.en: I have to scrape the ice off the windshield before I can drive.

at skraldgrine.explanation: "At skraldgrine" means "to roar with laughter", to laugh very loudly at something funny. It is a much stronger version of at grine (to laugh), and af shows what is funny: Vi skraldgrinede af filmen (We roared with laughter at the movie).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **skraldgrine**, når klovnen falder i vandet.
sentence.en: The children will roar with laughter when the clown falls into the water.

at skrige.explanation: "At skrige" means "to scream", often from fear, pain or anger: Hun skreg af smerte (She screamed in pain). For loud but normal calling, use at råbe (to shout).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **skrige** højt, når jeg er bange.
sentence.en: I can scream loudly when I am scared.

at skrive.explanation: "At skrive" means "to write". It also covers typing and texting: skrive en besked (to write a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to write a letter to Mom.

at skrive af.explanation: "At skrive af" means "to copy", to write out text that someone else wrote. In school it also means to take answers from a neighbor's paper, which is not allowed on a test.

sentence.da: Munkene plejede at **skrive af** gamle bøger i hånden.
sentence.en: The monks used to copy old books by hand.

at skrive ned.explanation: "At skrive ned" means "to write down", to keep something on paper so you remember it: Skriv det ned, så du ikke glemmer det (Write it down so you do not forget it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive ned**, hvad han siger.
sentence.en: I want to write down what he says.

at skrive til.explanation: "At skrive til" means "to write to" a person, with til (to) naming who gets it. It also covers texting: Skriv til mig! (Text me!).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive til** min lærer i dag.
sentence.en: I want to write to my teacher today.

at skrubbe.explanation: "At skrubbe" means "to scrub", to clean something by pressing and moving a stiff brush over it. Skrub af! (Get lost!) is a rude way to tell someone to leave.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrubbe** gulvet, fordi det er blevet meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to scrub the floor because it has gotten very dirty.

at skrue.explanation: "At skrue" means "to screw", to turn a screw in or out: Han skruer låget af (He unscrews the lid). With op (up) or ned (down) it means to turn something up or down: Skru ned for musikken (Turn down the music).

sentence.da: Kan du **skrue** hylden fast på væggen?
sentence.en: Can you screw the shelf onto the wall?

at skrælle.explanation: "At skrælle" means "to peel", for potatoes, carrots and fruit. The skin you take off is en skræl (a peel).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrælle** fem kartofler.
sentence.en: I have to peel five potatoes.

at skræmme.explanation: "At skræmme" means "to scare": Du skræmte mig! (You scared me!) To be scared yourself, say at være bange: Jeg er bange for edderkopper (I am scared of spiders).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **skræmme** katten.
sentence.en: You must not scare the cat.

at skubbe.explanation: "At skubbe" means "to push", for things and for people: Han skubbede mig (He pushed me). On a door, the sign says Skub (Push).

sentence.da: Kan du **skubbe** bilen sammen med mig?
sentence.en: Can you push the car together with me?

at skuffe.explanation: "At skuffe" means "to disappoint": Filmen skuffede mig (The movie disappointed me).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skuffe** dig igen.
sentence.en: I do not want to disappoint you again.

at skulle.explanation: "At skulle" means "to have to" or "should": Jeg skal arbejde (I have to work). It is also used for plans: Jeg skal i skole (I am going to school).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skulle** arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I don't want to have to work tomorrow.

at skumme.explanation: "At skumme" means "to foam" and "to skim". To foam is to form a white layer of tiny air pockets on top: Sæben skummer (The soap is foaming). To skim is to read something quickly without taking in every word: skumme en artikel (to skim an article).

sentence.da: Mælken begynder at **skumme**, når du varmer den op.
sentence.en: The milk starts to foam when you heat it up.

at skyde.explanation: "At skyde" means "to shoot": Jægeren skyder en hare (The hunter shoots a hare). It is also used in sports: Han skød bolden i mål (He shot the ball into the goal).

sentence.da: Hun kan **skyde** med bue og pil.
sentence.en: She can shoot with a bow and arrow.

at skylde.explanation: "At skylde" means "to owe": Jeg skylder dig hundrede kroner (I owe you a hundred kroner). With på (on) it means "to blame": Han skylder på mig (He blames me).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skylde** nogen penge.
sentence.en: I do not want to owe anyone money.

at skyldes.explanation: "At skyldes" means "to be due to", and it names the reason for something: Problemet skyldes en fejl i systemet (The problem is due to an error in the system). Do not mix it up with at skylde (to owe).

sentence.da: Togets forsinkelse **skyldes** sne på skinnerne.
sentence.en: The train's delay is due to snow on the tracks.

at skylle.explanation: "At skylle" means "to rinse", to run clean water over something to get soap or dirt off. With ud (out), it means to rinse out: Skyl munden ud (Rinse your mouth out).

sentence.da: Du skal **skylle** grøntsagerne, før du skærer dem.
sentence.en: You should rinse the vegetables before you cut them.

at skynde sig.explanation: "At skynde sig" means "to hurry". The little word after it matches who hurries: Jeg skynder mig (I hurry), Han skynder sig (He hurries). Skynd dig! means "Hurry up!"

sentence.da: Hun må **skynde sig**, fordi toget kører snart.
sentence.en: She has to hurry because the train leaves soon.

at skåle.explanation: "At skåle" means "to toast", raising your glass and drinking together: Vi skåler for dig (We toast you). The little word for (for) says who or what you toast.

sentence.da: Nu skal vi alle **skåle** for fødselaren.
sentence.en: Now we are all going to toast the birthday person.

at skåne.explanation: "At skåne" means "to spare", to treat someone or something gently so it is not hurt or worn out: skåne sit knæ (to go easy on your knee). It can also mean to keep someone from something unpleasant, with for: Jeg skåner dig for detaljerne (I spare you the details).

sentence.da: Du bør **skåne** din ryg og ikke løfte tungt.
sentence.en: You should go easy on your back and not lift heavy things.

at skælve.explanation: "At skælve" means "to tremble", to shake from fear, cold or strong feeling: Hendes stemme skælvede (Her voice trembled). The ground can do it too, and a jordskælv (earthquake) is literally an earth that trembles.

sentence.da: Mine hænder kan **skælve**, når jeg er meget bange.
sentence.en: My hands can tremble when I am very scared.

at skændes.explanation: "At skændes" means "to argue", and it takes two or more people: Vi skændes aldrig (We never argue). To say who with, add med: Jeg skændes med min bror (I am arguing with my brother).

sentence.da: Børnene **skændes** hele tiden om legetøjet.
sentence.en: The children argue all the time about the toy.

at skænke.explanation: "At skænke" means "to pour" a drink into a glass or cup for someone: Må jeg skænke en kop kaffe til dig? (May I pour you a cup of coffee?). It can also mean "to donate" or "to give as a gift": skænke et beløb til en god sag (to donate an amount to a good cause).

sentence.da: Tjeneren vil **skænke** vin til alle gæsterne.
sentence.en: The waiter will pour wine for all the guests.

at skære.explanation: "At skære" means "to cut" with a knife: Jeg skærer brødet i stykker (I cut the bread into pieces). Cutting hair with scissors is a different word, at klippe (to cut with scissors).

sentence.da: Kan du **skære** løget for mig?
sentence.en: Can you cut the onion for me?

at skærpe.explanation: "At skærpe" means "to sharpen" and "to tighten": to make a knife or tool sharper, or to make a rule or a check stricter, as in skærpe reglerne (to make the rules stricter). It can also mean to make your attention more alert.

sentence.da: Politiet vil **skærpe** kontrollen i weekenden.
sentence.en: The police will tighten the checks over the weekend.

at sladre.explanation: "At sladre" means "to tell on" and "to gossip". To tell on someone is to report what they did wrong to an adult in charge. A child who does it is called en sladrehank (a tattletale). To gossip is to talk about other people's private lives: Naboerne sladrer om alt (The neighbors gossip about everything).

sentence.da: Hun ville ikke **sladre** til læreren om sin bedste veninde.
sentence.en: She did not want to tattle to the teacher about her best friend.

at slanke sig.explanation: "At slanke sig" means "to diet", to eat less or differently in order to get thinner. It always needs sig (yourself): Hun slanker sig (She is dieting).

sentence.da: Hun vil **slanke sig** og spiser derfor mindre brød og sukker.
sentence.en: She wants to diet and therefore eats less bread and sugar.

at slappe af.explanation: "At slappe af" means "to relax" or "to take it easy", like resting on the sofa after a long day. Slap af! (Relax!) can also tell someone to calm down. The little word af (off) stays in every form.

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **slappe af**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to relax.

at slentre.explanation: "At slentre" means "to stroll", to go slowly and without hurry, just for the pleasure of it: slentre rundt i byen (to stroll around town). It is often used with rundt (around).

sentence.da: Vi vil **slentre** langs havnen og kigge på bådene.
sentence.en: We will stroll along the harbor and look at the boats.

at slette.explanation: "At slette" means "to delete", to remove something from a device, like a file or a message: Jeg sletter den gamle fil (I delete the old file).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **slette** alle de gamle billeder.
sentence.en: I want to delete all the old photos.

at slibe.explanation: "At slibe" means "to sharpen" and "to sand". For a knife, it is to drag the edge over a hard stone until it is sharp: Jeg sliber knivene (I am sharpening the knives). For wood or walls, it is to wear away rough spots.

sentence.da: Du skal **slibe** bordet med sandpapir, før du maler det.
sentence.en: You have to sand the table with sandpaper before you paint it.

at slide.explanation: "At slide" means "to wear out" and "to toil". Things wear out from use: Sko slides, når man går meget i dem (Shoes wear out when you walk a lot in them). A person toils by working very hard for a long time, often for a family or a living.

sentence.da: Han må **slide** hårdt for at brødføde sin store familie.
sentence.en: He has to toil hard to feed his large family.

at slikke.explanation: "At slikke" means "to lick", to pass your tongue over something: at slikke en is (to lick an ice cream). Danes also say slikke sol (to soak up the sun) for lying in the sun.

sentence.da: Katte bruger tungen til at **slikke** sig rene.
sentence.en: Cats use their tongues to lick themselves clean.

at slippe.explanation: "At slippe" means "to let go" and "to escape": Slip mig! (Let go of me!) Han slap væk (He got away). Slippe for means "to be spared from": Jeg slap for at vaske op (I got out of doing the dishes).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **slippe** snoren nu.
sentence.en: You must not let go of the string now.

at slippe af med.explanation: "At slippe af med" means "to get rid of": Hun slap af med sin forkølelse (She got rid of her cold). It is built from slippe (to let go) and af med (off with), so what you lose comes at the end.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **slippe af med** min gamle sofa.
sentence.en: I would like to get rid of my old sofa.

at sludre.explanation: "At sludre" means "to chat", to talk in a relaxed way about nothing important: sludre med naboen (to chat with the neighbor). Sludder (nonsense) is closely related, as in Det er sludder! (That is nonsense!).

sentence.da: Vi kan **sludre** over en kop kaffe i dag.
sentence.en: We can chat over a cup of coffee today.

at sluge.explanation: "At sluge" means "to swallow", to send food or a pill down your throat: Hun slugte tabletten uden vand (She swallowed the pill without water). It can also mean "to gulp down": Han slugte maden på to minutter (He gulped the food down in two minutes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **sluge** den store tablet.
sentence.en: I cannot swallow the big pill.

at slukke.explanation: "At slukke" means "to turn off" a light or "to put out" a fire: slukke lyset (turn off the light) and slukke en brand (put out a fire). For a TV or the radio, use slukke for (turn off): slukke for fjernsynet (turn off the TV).

sentence.da: Husk at **slukke** lyset.
sentence.en: Remember to turn off the light.

at slukke for.explanation: "At slukke for" means "to turn off" something like the TV, the radio or the heating: Jeg slukker for radioen (I turn off the radio). For a light, slukke lyset (turn off the light) is the usual choice. A fire is put out with plain slukke: slukke en brand (to put out a fire).

sentence.da: Husk at **slukke for** fjernsynet.
sentence.en: Remember to turn off the TV.

at slutte.explanation: "At slutte" means "to end" or "to finish": Skolen slutter klokken tre (School ends at three). With med (with) it means "to stop doing something": Jeg slutter med at ryge (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **slutte** om en time.
sentence.en: The movie is going to end in an hour.

at slutte fred.explanation: "At slutte fred" means "to make peace", to end a conflict between people or countries. With med (with), it names the other side: Jeg har sluttet fred med min bror (I have made peace with my brother). It also fits an inner struggle: slutte fred med fortiden (to make peace with the past).

sentence.da: Efter mange års krig vil landene endelig **slutte fred**.
sentence.en: After many years of war the countries finally want to make peace.

at slå.explanation: "At slå" means "to hit" and "to beat", so it covers hitting with your hand or a tool and winning over someone: Hun slog mig i skak (She beat me at chess). Slå græsset means "mow the lawn".

sentence.da: Jeg kan **slå** et søm i væggen med en hammer.
sentence.en: I can hit a nail into the wall with a hammer.

at slå et smut forbi.explanation: "At slå et smut forbi" means "to drop by", to stop at a place for a short time, often on your way somewhere else. Danes add lige (just) to sound casual: Vi slår lige et smut forbi bageren (We will just stop by the bakery).

forms.da: jeg har slået et smut forbi

sentence.da: Jeg kan **slå et smut forbi** dig på vej hjem.
sentence.en: I can drop by your place on my way home.

at slå græs.explanation: "At slå græs" means "to mow the lawn". It is built from slå (hit) and græs (grass), so it literally means to hit grass. The same slå is used for hitting a ball: at slå en bold (to hit a ball).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **slå græs**, fordi græsset er blevet langt.
sentence.en: I have to mow the lawn because the grass has gotten long.

at slå igennem.explanation: "At slå igennem" means "to break through", to become known and successful, for example as an artist or an athlete: Hun slog igennem som sangerinde (She became a star as a singer). It is also used for the sun coming out of the clouds: Solen slår igennem (The sun breaks through).

sentence.da: Mange unge musikere drømmer om at **slå igennem**.
sentence.en: Many young musicians dream of breaking through.

at slå op.explanation: "At slå op" means "to look up" a word: Jeg slår ordet op (I look up the word). It can also mean to break up: Hun slog op med ham (She broke up with him).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **slå op** i ordbogen.
sentence.en: I have to look it up in the dictionary.

at slå sig ned.explanation: "At slå sig ned" means "to settle down", to make a place your home or to stop moving around: Familien slog sig ned i Aarhus (The family settled in Aarhus). It can also mean to take a seat for a while: Vi slog os ned på en bænk (We took a seat on a bench).

sentence.da: Efter mange år i udlandet ville de **slå sig ned** i Danmark.
sentence.en: After many years abroad they wanted to settle down in Denmark.

at slå to fluer med et smæk.explanation: "At slå to fluer med et smæk" means "to kill two birds with one stone", to solve two problems with one action. The Danish picture is two flies hit with one smack, not birds and a stone.

forms.da: Jeg vil slå to fluer med et smæk
forms.en: I want to kill two birds with one stone

forms.da: Her slår vi to fluer med et smæk
forms.en: Here we kill two birds with one stone

forms.da: at slå to fluer med et smæk
forms.en: to kill two birds with one stone

sentence.da: Du kan **slå to fluer med et smæk** ved at cykle på arbejde.
sentence.en: You can kill two birds with one stone by cycling to work.

at slå ud.explanation: "At slå ud" means "to knock out". In sport, it means to beat a team so that it leaves the competition: Danmark slog Tyskland ud (Denmark knocked Germany out). Trees and flowers also slå ud when they come into leaf or bloom: Træerne slår ud i maj (The trees come into leaf in May). A fuse that cuts the power also slår ud (trips).

sentence.da: Hvis strømmen bliver for stærk, kan sikringen **slå ud**.
sentence.en: If the current gets too strong, the fuse can trip.

at slæbe.explanation: "At slæbe" means "to drag" or "to haul" something heavy with effort. It also fits a tired person: Jeg slæber mig hjem (I drag myself home).

sentence.da: Vi skal **slæbe** de tunge kasser op ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to haul the heavy boxes up the stairs.

at smadre.explanation: "At smadre" means "to smash", to break something into pieces with force. It is also used for a heavy defeat: Holdet smadrede modstanderen (The team beat the opponent badly).

sentence.da: Glas kan **smadre**, når det rammer gulvet.
sentence.en: Glass can smash when it hits the floor.

at smage.explanation: "At smage" means "to taste", both for trying food and for having a flavor. Det smager godt (It tastes good) and Det smager af citron (It tastes like lemon).

sentence.da: Må jeg **smage** din suppe?
sentence.en: May I taste your soup?

at smelte.explanation: "At smelte" means "to melt", when something solid turns to liquid: Isen smelter i solen (The ice melts in the sun). You can also melt something yourself: Jeg smelter smør (I melt butter).

sentence.da: Sneen vil **smelte**, når det bliver varmt.
sentence.en: The snow will melt when it gets warm.

at smide.explanation: "At smide" means "to throw", and also "to throw away": Jeg smider papiret i skraldespanden (I throw the paper in the trash can). For throwing a ball, kaste (throw) is more usual.

sentence.da: Du må ikke **smide** affald på gaden.
sentence.en: You must not throw trash on the street.

at smide ud.explanation: "At smide ud" means "to throw out", like old food or things you no longer need: Jeg smider maden ud (I throw the food out). It also means "to kick out" of a place: De smed ham ud af baren (They threw him out of the bar).

sentence.da: Vi skal **smide ud**, hvad vi ikke bruger.
sentence.en: We have to throw out what we do not use.

at smile.explanation: "At smile" means "to smile". Hun smilede til mig means "She smiled at me": you smile til (to) someone.

sentence.da: Hun er glad og kan **smile** til alle.
sentence.en: She is happy and can smile at everyone.

at sminke sig.explanation: "At sminke sig" means "to put on makeup". The little word sig (oneself) changes with the person: Hun sminker sig (She puts on makeup), but Du sminker dig (You put on makeup).

sentence.da: Hun vil **sminke sig** og tage en kjole på.
sentence.en: She wants to put on makeup and put on a dress.

at smitte.explanation: "At smitte" means "to infect", to pass an illness on to someone. It also works for moods: Hendes latter smitter (Her laughter is catching).

sentence.da: Du kan **smitte** andre, når du er syg.
sentence.en: You can infect others when you are sick.

at smugle.explanation: "At smugle" means "to smuggle", to bring goods across a border secretly and against the law. It also fits a small sneaky act: Han smuglede slik ind i biografen (He smuggled candy into the movie theater).

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at **smugle** varer over grænsen.
sentence.en: It is illegal to smuggle goods across the border.

at smuldre.explanation: "At smuldre" means "to crumble", to come apart in small pieces, like dry bread, a cake or an old wall: Kagen smuldrer (The cake crumbles). It is also used for hopes: Hans håb smuldrede (His hopes crumbled).

sentence.da: Murstenene i den gamle mur begynder at **smuldre**.
sentence.en: The bricks in the old wall begin to crumble.

at smutte.explanation: "At smutte" means "to pop out" or "to slip away" quickly: Jeg smutter lige ud (I'll just pop out). It can also mean "to slip" by accident: Kniven smuttede (The knife slipped).

forms.en: I have slipped away / popped out

sentence.da: Jeg vil lige **smutte** ned i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I'll just pop down to the supermarket.

at smøre.explanation: "At smøre" means "to spread", for example butter on bread: Jeg smører brødet med smør (I spread butter on the bread). Danes also say at smøre en madpakke (to make a packed lunch).

sentence.da: Kan du **smøre** et stykke brød til mig?
sentence.en: Can you butter a slice of bread for me?

at snakke.explanation: "At snakke" means "to talk" or "to chat", and it is the everyday word for speaking. At tale (to speak) sounds more formal and fits a speech or a meeting: Han taler på mødet (He speaks at the meeting).

sentence.da: Jeg har tid og kan **snakke** nu.
sentence.en: I have time and can talk now.

at snakke om.explanation: "At snakke om" means "to talk about": Vi snakker om mad (We are talking about food). To talk with a person, use med (with): Jeg snakker med min mor (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi vil **snakke om** vores ferie i aften.
sentence.en: We want to talk about our vacation tonight.

at snakke om vejret.explanation: "At snakke om vejret" means "to make small talk", literally "to talk about the weather": Vi snakkede om vejret i elevatoren (We made small talk in the elevator). It is chat where nothing important is said.

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke bare **snakke om vejret** med dig.
sentence.en: I don't just want to make small talk with you.

at sne.explanation: "At sne" means "to snow": Det sner (It is snowing). The word for snow itself is also "sne", as in Der er sne (There is snow), so the sentence shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: I vinter kan det **sne** meget.
sentence.en: In winter it can snow a lot.

at snige sig.explanation: "At snige sig" means "to sneak", to move quietly so nobody notices. Add a direction to say where: at snige sig ind (to sneak in), at snige sig ud (to sneak out).

sentence.da: Katten vil **snige sig** hen til fuglen uden en lyd.
sentence.en: The cat wants to sneak over to the bird without a sound.

at snooze.explanation: "At snooze" means "to snooze", to press the button on your alarm for a few more minutes of sleep: Jeg snoozer to gange hver morgen (I hit snooze twice every morning). To sleep late on purpose, say at sove længe (to sleep in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **snooze** i fem minutter mere.
sentence.en: I want to snooze for five more minutes.

at snorke.explanation: "At snorke" means "to snore": Han snorker højt om natten (He snores loudly at night). To tell someone to stop, say Hold op med at snorke! (Stop snoring!)

sentence.da: Min far plejer at **snorke** meget højt.
sentence.en: My dad usually snores very loudly.

at snuble.explanation: "At snuble" means "to stumble" or "to trip", to knock your foot on something and nearly fall. The thing you hit comes after over: snuble over en kabel (trip over a cable). It also fits words: snuble over et svært ord (stumble over a hard word).

sentence.da: Det er nemt at **snuble** på en våd trappe.
sentence.en: It is easy to stumble on a wet staircase.

at snuppe.explanation: "At snuppe" means "to grab", to take something quickly, often without asking: Han snuppede min kuglepen (He grabbed my pen). It is also an everyday word for doing something small and quick: Skal vi snuppe en kop kaffe? (Shall we grab a cup of coffee?).

sentence.da: Du kan lige **snuppe** en kage, og så går vi.
sentence.en: You can quickly grab a cake, and then we go.

at snyde.explanation: "At snyde" means "to cheat", to break the rules to win or to trick someone. When you trick someone out of something, use for: Han snød mig for hundrede kroner (He cheated me out of a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **snyde** til en eksamen.
sentence.en: You must not cheat on an exam.

at snøfte.explanation: "At snøfte" means "to sniffle", to breathe in noisily through the nose, for example with a cold or after tears: Barnet snøftede længe bagefter (The child sniffled for a long time afterward).

sentence.da: Han vil **snøfte** hele dagen, fordi han er forkølet.
sentence.en: He will sniffle all day because he has a cold.

at sortere.explanation: "At sortere" means "to sort", to put things into groups or an order, like trash into bins or mail into piles: Jeg sorterer affaldet (I sort the trash).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sortere** tøjet efter farve.
sentence.en: We have to sort the clothes by color.

at sove.explanation: "At sove" means "to sleep": Jeg sover godt (I sleep well). Going to bed is a different phrase: at gå i seng (to go to bed).

sentence.da: Børnene er trætte og vil **sove**.
sentence.en: The children are tired and want to sleep.

at sove længe.explanation: "At sove længe" means "to sleep in": Vi sover længe i weekenden (We sleep in on the weekend). Længe means "a long time", so Hun sov længe (She slept for a long time) works too.

sentence.da: I morgen er det lørdag, og jeg vil **sove længe**.
sentence.en: Tomorrow is Saturday, and I want to sleep in.

at sove over sig.explanation: "At sove over sig" means "to oversleep", to sleep past the time you meant to get up: Jeg sov over mig og kom for sent (I overslept and was late). To sleep late on purpose, say at sove længe (to sleep in).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **sove over sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: She does not want to oversleep tomorrow.

at spadsere.explanation: "At spadsere" means "to stroll", to walk slowly for pleasure, not to get somewhere. For a plain walk, Danes often say at gå en tur (to go for a walk).

sentence.da: Vi vil **spadsere** langs havnen og nyde solen.
sentence.en: We want to stroll along the harbor and enjoy the sun.

at spare.explanation: "At spare" means "to save", mostly money: Vi sparer penge til en rejse (We are saving money for a trip). It also works for time: Det sparer tid (That saves time).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spare** penge til en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I want to save money for a new bike.

at spare op.explanation: "At spare op" means "to save up", to put money aside bit by bit for something: Jeg sparer op til en cykel (I am saving up for a bike). Without op (up), at spare is the general word for saving, as in at spare tid (to save time).

sentence.da: Vi vil **spare op**, så vi kan købe et hus.
sentence.en: We want to save up so we can buy a house.

at spare på.explanation: "At spare på" means "to save on", as in using less of something: Vi sparer på varmen (We are saving on heat). It also means "to be careful with": Hun sparer på pengene (She is careful with the money).

sentence.da: Vi skal **spare på** strømmen i vinter.
sentence.en: We have to save on electricity this winter.

at sparke.explanation: "At sparke" means "to kick": Han sparkede bolden over hegnet (He kicked the ball over the fence). With til (to), you give something a kick: Hun sparkede til døren (She gave the door a kick).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **sparke** bolden i mål.
sentence.en: The kids want to kick the ball into the goal.

at specialisere sig.explanation: "At specialisere sig" means "to specialize", to concentrate on one area. The area comes after i (in): at specialisere sig i hjertekirurgi (to specialize in heart surgery).

sentence.da: Efter studiet vil lægen **specialisere sig** i hjertesygdomme.
sentence.en: After university, the doctor wants to specialize in heart disease.

at spejle.explanation: "At spejle" means "to mirror", to send back an image the way a smooth surface does. With sig, the thing is seen in the surface: Hun spejler sig i vinduet (She sees herself in the window).

sentence.da: Bjergene kan **spejle** sig i den stille sø.
sentence.en: The mountains can be mirrored in the quiet lake.

at spekulere.explanation: "At spekulere" means "to speculate" and, more often, "to wonder", to think hard about something. The thing you wonder about comes after på: Jeg spekulerer på det (I wonder about it). With i it is about money: spekulere i aktier (to speculate in shares).

sentence.da: Hun begyndte at **spekulere** på, hvorfor han var så stille.
sentence.en: She began to wonder why he was so quiet.

at spilde.explanation: "At spilde" means "to spill" and "to waste": Jeg spildte vand på bordet (I spilled water on the table). Vi må ikke spilde mad (We must not waste food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **spilde** min tid på det.
sentence.en: I do not want to waste my time on that.

at spilde tid.explanation: "At spilde tid" means "to waste time": Jeg spilder tid på telefonen (I waste time on the phone). At spilde on its own also means "to spill": Jeg spildte kaffe (I spilled coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **spilde tid** på det her.
sentence.en: I do not want to waste time on this.

at spille.explanation: "At spille" means "to play" a game, a sport or an instrument: Vi spiller fodbold (We play soccer). It also means "to act" a part: Hun spiller en prinsesse (She plays a princess). For children playing for fun, Danes say at lege (to play).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **spille** guitar og synge.
sentence.en: My brother can play the guitar and sing.

at spille en rolle.explanation: "At spille en rolle" means "to play a role", on stage or in real life: Hun spiller en rolle i skolens teater (She plays a role in the school theater). It also means "to matter": Prisen spiller ikke nogen rolle (The price does not matter).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **spille en rolle** i filmen.
sentence.en: He would like to play a role in the movie.

at spille fodbold.explanation: "At spille fodbold" means "to play soccer" ("football" in Britain). Spille (to play) is used for most games and sports. The word fodbold is built from fod (foot) and bold (ball).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **spille fodbold** i dag.
sentence.en: The children want to play soccer today.

at spise.explanation: "At spise" means "to eat": Vi spiser aftensmad (We eat dinner). At spise ude means "to eat out". For drinking, use at drikke (to drink).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spise** brød, ost og æbler.
sentence.en: I want to eat bread, cheese and apples.

at sponsorere.explanation: "At sponsorere" means "to sponsor", to pay for an event, a team or a person, usually in return for advertising: Banken sponsorerer festivalen (The bank sponsors the festival).

sentence.da: Et lokalt firma vil **sponsorere** fodboldholdets nye trøjer.
sentence.en: A local company wants to sponsor the soccer team's new shirts.

at spore.explanation: "At spore" means "to track" or "to trace", to follow signs back to where something is or came from: Politiet sporer telefonen (The police trace the phone). It is built on et spor (a trail or footprint).

sentence.da: Med et nummer kan du **spore** din pakke på nettet.
sentence.en: With a number you can track your package online.

at sprede.explanation: "At sprede" means "to spread", to make something cover a bigger area or reach more people. With sig (itself) it happens by itself: Rygtet spreder sig (The rumor spreads). Without sig someone does it: Han spreder rygtet (He spreads the rumor).

sentence.da: Vinden kan **sprede** frøene over hele marken.
sentence.en: The wind can spread the seeds over the whole field.

at springe.explanation: "At springe" means "to jump": Børn springer i vandet (Children jump into the water). With over added, it means "to skip": Jeg springer en side over (I skip a page).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **springe** over hegnet.
sentence.en: The dog can jump over the fence.

at springe over.explanation: "At springe over" means "to skip", to leave something out: Jeg springer frokosten over (I skip lunch). It can also mean "to jump over": Hunden sprang over hegnet (The dog jumped over the fence).

sentence.da: Jeg vil aldrig **springe over** morgenmaden.
sentence.en: I will never skip breakfast.

at sprænge.explanation: "At sprænge" means "to blow up", to break something apart with explosives: at sprænge en bro (to blow up a bridge). It also means to go beyond a limit: at sprænge budgettet (to blow the budget).

sentence.da: Arbejderne bruger dynamit til at **sprænge** klippen.
sentence.en: The workers use dynamite to blow up the rock.

at sprøjte.explanation: "At sprøjte" means "to spray" or "to squirt": Han sprøjter vand på blomsterne (He sprays water on the flowers). A doctor's needle is en sprøjte (a syringe), the same word.

sentence.da: Børnene vil **sprøjte** vand på hinanden.
sentence.en: The children want to spray water on each other.

at spytte.explanation: "At spytte" means "to spit", to force saliva or food out of the mouth. With på it is aimed at something: spytte på gulvet (spit on the floor). It also fits things that shoot out: Dragen spytter ild (The dragon spits fire).

sentence.da: Barnet kan ikke lide smagen og vil **spytte** den ud.
sentence.en: The child does not like the taste and wants to spit it out.

at spænde.explanation: "At spænde" means "to tighten" and "to fasten": Spænd remmen (Tighten the strap). It also means to tense up: Jeg spænder musklerne (I tense my muscles).

sentence.da: Du skal altid **spænde** sikkerhedsbæltet i bilen.
sentence.en: You must always fasten the seat belt in the car.

at spøge.explanation: "At spøge" means "to joke", to say something for fun that is not meant for real: Jeg spøger kun (I am only joking). The same word is used for ghosts: Det spøger i huset (The house is haunted).

sentence.da: Han kan godt **spøge** med sin egen fejl, og alle griner.
sentence.en: He can joke about his own mistake, and everyone laughs.

at spørge.explanation: "At spørge" means "to ask" a question: Jeg spørger ham om vejen (I ask him for directions). To ask for something you want, use at bede om (to ask for): Jeg beder om en kop kaffe (I ask for a cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge** læreren.
sentence.en: I want to ask the teacher.

at spørge om.explanation: "At spørge om" means "to ask about" or "to ask for". Om (about) comes right after spørge and is followed by the topic or thing you want: spørge om prisen (ask about the price), spørge om vej (ask for directions).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om** hjælp.
sentence.en: I want to ask for help.

at spørge om vej.explanation: "At spørge om vej" means "to ask for directions", word for word "to ask about way": Undskyld, må jeg spørge om vej? (Excuse me, may I ask for directions?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om vej** til banegården.
sentence.en: I want to ask for directions to the station.

at stabilisere.explanation: "At stabilisere" means "to stabilize", to make something steady so it stops changing or shaking: Lægerne stabiliserer patienten (The doctors stabilize the patient). With sig it happens by itself: Priserne stabiliserer sig (Prices settle).

sentence.da: Vi bruger en stang til at **stabilisere** det høje telt.
sentence.en: We use a pole to stabilize the tall tent.

at stadfæste.explanation: "At stadfæste" means "to confirm" or "to uphold", to make a decision or a law official so that it stands: Retten stadfæstede dommen (The court upheld the verdict). It is used in law and government, not in everyday talk.

sentence.da: Kongen kan **stadfæste** en ny lov, og så gælder den.
sentence.en: The king can formally approve a new law, and then it applies.

at stamme.explanation: "At stamme" means "to stutter" and also "to come from". For speech, it stands alone: Han stammer, når han er nervøs (He stutters when he is nervous). For origin, it takes fra: Min familie stammer fra Jylland (My family comes from Jutland).

sentence.da: Mange danske ord kan **stamme** fra tysk.
sentence.en: Many Danish words can come from German.

at standse.explanation: "At standse" means "to stop", when something moving comes to a halt or you make it halt: Bilen standsede foran huset (The car stopped in front of the house). To quit doing something, say at holde op (to quit): Jeg holder op med at ryge (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: Bussen skal **standse** ved stationen.
sentence.en: The bus has to stop at the station.

at starte.explanation: "At starte" means "to start", for people and for machines: Bilen starter ikke (The car won't start) and Vi starter i morgen (We start tomorrow). At begynde (to begin) means almost the same.

sentence.da: Filmen skal **starte** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The movie is going to start at eight.

at starte på.explanation: "At starte på" means "to start on" something, like a task: Jeg starter på opgaven (I start on the assignment). Without på (on), starte (to start) is for things that get going: Bilen starter ikke (The car won't start).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **starte på** et nyt projekt i dag.
sentence.en: I want to start on a new project today.

at stave.explanation: "At stave" means "to spell", saying the letters of a word one at a time. It is common when you give a name or an address on the phone: Hvordan staver man det? (How do you spell that?)

sentence.da: Kan du **stave** dit navn?
sentence.en: Can you spell your name?

at stege.explanation: "At stege" means "to fry" and "to roast": Jeg steger kød i panden (I fry meat in the pan) and Vi steger en and i ovnen (We roast a duck in the oven). Cooking in water is at koge (to boil).

forms.en: I have fried, I have roasted

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stege** æggene i panden.
sentence.en: I am going to fry the eggs in the pan.

at stemme.explanation: "At stemme" means "to vote": Jeg stemmer på ham (I vote for him). It also means "to be correct": Det stemmer! (That is right!)

sentence.da: Alle over atten år kan **stemme** ved valget.
sentence.en: Everyone over eighteen can vote in the election.

at stemme på.explanation: "At stemme på" means "to vote for" the person or party you choose. Danish uses på (on) where English says for: Vi stemte på Peter (We voted for Peter). Without på, stemme (to vote) just means casting a vote.

sentence.da: Til valget vil jeg **stemme på** Anna.
sentence.en: At the election, I want to vote for Anna.

at stige.explanation: "At stige" means "to rise" and "to climb": Prisen stiger (The price is rising). Han stiger op ad trappen (He climbs up the stairs). With vehicles, it means "to get in": Hun steg ind i bilen (She got into the car).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **stige** til tredive grader.
sentence.en: The temperature can rise to thirty degrees.

at stige af.explanation: "At stige af" means "to get off", used for a bus, a train or a bike: Hun stiger af cyklen (She gets off the bike). The opposite is at stige på (to get on).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stige af** bussen ved torvet.
sentence.en: I will get off the bus at the square.

at stige på.explanation: "At stige på" means "to get on", used for a bus, a train or a bike: Vi stiger på toget i Odense (We get on the train in Odense). The opposite is at stige af (to get off).

sentence.da: Vi må **stige på** bussen nu.
sentence.en: We have to get on the bus now.

at stikke.explanation: "At stikke" means "to sting" and "to stick": Bien stak mig (The bee stung me). It also means to put something in: Jeg stikker pengene i lommen (I stick the money in my pocket).

sentence.da: Du skal **stikke** nøglen i døren.
sentence.en: You have to stick the key in the door.

at stikke af.explanation: "At stikke af" means "to run off": you get away quickly, often from trouble. Tyven stak af (The thief ran off).

sentence.da: Drengen ville **stikke af**, men læreren så ham.
sentence.en: The boy wanted to run off, but the teacher saw him.

at stikke en finger i jorden.explanation: "At stikke en finger i jorden" means "to take stock", to stop and check where things really stand before you go on. Literally it is "to stick a finger in the ground", like feeling what the soil is like.

forms.da: Vi må stikke en finger i jorden
Hun stak en finger i jorden
Lad os stikke en finger i jorden

sentence.da: Vi må **stikke en finger i jorden** og se, hvor vi står.
sentence.en: We must take stock and see where we stand.

at stikke en kæp i hjulet.explanation: "At stikke en kæp i hjulet" means "to throw a wrench in the works", to spoil or block someone's plan, often on purpose. Literally it is to stick a stick in the wheel. The person you spoil things for comes after for: stikke en kæp i hjulet for nogen (to spoil things for someone).

forms.da: Han stikker en kæp i hjulet
forms.en: He throws a wrench in the works

forms.da: Hun stak en kæp i hjulet for os
Stik ikke en kæp i hjulet for dem
forms.en: Do not spoil things for them

sentence.da: Naboen vil **stikke en kæp i hjulet** for vores byggeplan.
sentence.en: The neighbor wants to throw a wrench in the works of our building plan.

at stille.explanation: "At stille" means "to put / place (upright)": Jeg stiller cyklen i skuret (I put the bike in the shed). For something lying flat, use at lægge (to lay): Jeg lægger bogen på bordet (I put the book on the table).

sentence.da: Kan du **stille** flasken på bordet?
sentence.en: Can you put the bottle on the table?

at stille et spørgsmål.explanation: "At stille et spørgsmål" means "to ask a question": Læreren stillede et spørgsmål (The teacher asked a question). The short word at spørge (to ask) is also common: Jeg vil spørge dig om noget (I want to ask you something).

sentence.da: Må jeg **stille et spørgsmål** om lektien?
sentence.en: May I ask a question about the homework?

at stille op.explanation: "At stille op" means "to run for office", to put your name forward in a vote: Han stiller op for partiet (He runs for the party). It also means to show up and play for a team: Holdet stiller op til kampen (The team turns out for the match). To line up, add sig: Børnene stiller sig op i en række (The children line up in a row).

sentence.da: Hun vil **stille op** til valget som borgmester.
sentence.en: She wants to run for mayor in the election.

at stille uret.explanation: "At stille uret" means "to set the clock". You can say which way: stille uret en time frem (set the clock an hour forward) or stille uret en time tilbage (set the clock an hour back).

sentence.da: Vi skal **stille uret** en time tilbage.
sentence.en: We have to set the clock back an hour.

at stimulere.explanation: "At stimulere" means "to stimulate", to wake up or support an activity: Musik stimulerer hjernen (Music stimulates the brain). It is also used for the economy: at stimulere økonomien (to boost the economy).

sentence.da: Leg kan **stimulere** børns fantasi og nysgerrighed.
sentence.en: Play can stimulate children's imagination and curiosity.

at stirre.explanation: "At stirre" means "to stare", to keep your eyes on something without turning away. The thing you stare at comes after på: stirre på skærmen (stare at the screen). Without a thing it can mean empty staring: Han stirrer ud i luften (He stares into space).

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **stirre** på fremmede mennesker.
sentence.en: It is rude to stare at strangers.

at stjæle.explanation: "At stjæle" means "to steal": Han stjal min cykel (He stole my bike). Robbing a bank or a person is different: at røve (to rob).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **stjæle** fra andre.
sentence.en: You must not steal from others.

at stole på.explanation: "At stole på" means "to trust", and på always stays with it: Jeg stoler på min læge (I trust my doctor). Even with ikke (not), på stays at the end: Jeg stoler ikke på ham (I do not trust him).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **stole på** min bedste ven.
sentence.en: I can trust my best friend.

at stoppe.explanation: "At stoppe" means "to stop": Bussen stopper her (The bus stops here). With med (with) it means "to quit doing something": Jeg stopper med at spise slik (I am going to stop eating candy).

sentence.da: Bilen skal **stoppe** ved det røde lys.
sentence.en: The car has to stop at the red light.

at straffe.explanation: "At straffe" means "to punish", to give someone a consequence for doing wrong. It also fits mistakes, where the result hurts you: Fejlen blev straffet med et mål (The mistake was punished with a goal).

sentence.da: Dommeren kan **straffe** en spiller med et rødt kort.
sentence.en: The referee can punish a player with a red card.

at stramme.explanation: "At stramme" means "to tighten", to pull something until it sits firmly: at stramme en skrue (to tighten a screw). It is also used for rules: at stramme reglerne (to make the rules stricter).

sentence.da: Man kan **stramme** et bælte, når det sidder løst.
sentence.en: You can tighten a belt when it is loose.

at streame.explanation: "At streame" means "to stream", to watch or listen online without saving the file: Vi streamer en serie hver aften (We stream a series every evening).

sentence.da: Vi vil **streame** en film i aften.
sentence.en: We want to stream a movie tonight.

at strejke.explanation: "At strejke" means "to strike", to stop work together to demand better conditions. Everyone in the group does it at once: Buschaufførerne strejker (The bus drivers are on strike).

sentence.da: Lærerne vil **strejke**, fordi de ønsker højere løn.
sentence.en: The teachers want to strike because they want higher pay.

at strikke.explanation: "At strikke" means "to knit": Min mor strikker en hue (My mother is knitting a hat). Crocheting is a different word: at hækle (to crochet).

sentence.da: Min mormor kan **strikke** en varm trøje.
sentence.en: My grandmother can knit a warm sweater.

at stryge.explanation: "At stryge" means "to iron" clothes: Jeg stryger en skjorte (I iron a shirt). It also means "to stroke" something gently: Hun stryger katten (She strokes the cat).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stryge** en skjorte før mødet.
sentence.en: I have to iron a shirt before the meeting.

at stræbe.explanation: "At stræbe" means "to strive", to work hard over a long time toward something you want. The goal comes after efter: stræbe efter succes (to strive for success). Stræbsom (ambitious) is the same word family.

sentence.da: Han vil **stræbe** efter at blive den bedste i klassen.
sentence.en: He wants to strive to become the best in the class.

at strække.explanation: "At strække" means "to stretch": Jeg strækker armene (I stretch my arms). To stretch your own body, add sig (oneself): Katten strækker sig (The cat stretches).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **strække** benene efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: It is important to stretch your legs after the run.

at strække sig.explanation: "At strække sig" means "to stretch" your own body: Han strækker sig efter træning (He stretches after exercise). The little word sig changes with who stretches: jeg strækker mig (I stretch), vi strækker os (we stretch).

sentence.da: Katten vil **strække sig** i solen.
sentence.en: The cat wants to stretch in the sun.

at strø.explanation: "At strø" means "to sprinkle", to scatter small bits over a surface: strø sukker på kagen (to sprinkle sugar on the cake). It is also used for scattering things around: strø om sig med penge (to throw money around).

sentence.da: Vi må **strø** sand foran døren, når der er is.
sentence.en: We must sprinkle sand in front of the door when there is ice.

at studere.explanation: "At studere" means "to study", especially at a university: Jeg studerer historie (I study history). For studying at home for a test, Danes often say at læse til en eksamen (literally to read for an exam).

related.en: a study, a course of study

sentence.da: Hun vil **studere** medicin på universitetet.
sentence.en: She wants to study medicine at the university.

at styre.explanation: "At styre" means "to steer" and "to control": Hun styrer bilen (She steers the car). It also means "to run" something: Han styrer firmaet (He runs the company).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **styre** båden selv.
sentence.en: I can steer the boat myself.

at styrke.explanation: "At styrke" means "to strengthen", to make something stronger or better able to resist: at styrke musklerne (to strengthen the muscles). It also fits relationships: Turen styrkede venskabet (The trip strengthened the friendship).

sentence.da: Daglig motion kan **styrke** hjertet og musklerne.
sentence.en: Daily exercise can strengthen the heart and the muscles.

at styrte.explanation: "At styrte" means "to rush" and "to crash", both a fast movement that is hard to control. Flyet styrtede ned (The plane crashed down). Without ned, it is about speed: Jeg styrtede hjem (I rushed home).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **styrte** ud af døren, når klokken ringer.
sentence.en: The children will rush out the door when the bell rings.

at stå.explanation: "At stå" means "to stand", but Danish uses it more widely than English: Flasken står på bordet (The bottle stands on the table). It also covers writing: Der står et navn på døren (A name is written on the door).

sentence.da: Man kan **stå** eller sidde i bussen.
sentence.en: You can stand or sit on the bus.

at stå af.explanation: "At stå af" means "to get off", used for a bus, a train or the metro: Hvor skal vi stå af? (Where do we get off?) For a bike or a horse, use at stige af (to get off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå af** ved næste stop.
sentence.en: I will get off at the next stop.

at stå for.explanation: "At stå for" means "to be in charge of", a job or a task: Hvem står for festen? (Who is in charge of the party?)

forms.en: I have been in charge of

sentence.da: Min bror vil **stå for** maden til festen.
sentence.en: My brother will be in charge of the food for the party.

at stå i kø.explanation: "At stå i kø" means "to stand in line". The word kø means "line" (a queue of people): Jeg står i kø i supermarkedet (I am standing in line at the supermarket).

sentence.da: Vi må **stå i kø** for billetter.
sentence.en: We have to stand in line for tickets.

at stå op.explanation: "At stå op" means "to get up" out of bed, literally to stand up. When saying what you have done, Danish uses er (am) instead of har (have): Jeg er stået op (I have gotten up). To stand up from a chair, Danes say at rejse sig (to stand up).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå op** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I want to get up at seven.

at stå på ski.explanation: "At stå på ski" means "to ski", literally to stand on skis. Water skiing works the same way: at stå på vandski (to water ski). There is no en or et (a) before ski.

sentence.da: Vi vil **stå på ski** i Norge.
sentence.en: We want to ski in Norway.

at støde på.explanation: "At støde på" means "to come across", to see or notice something by chance, often without looking for it: Jeg stødte på min gamle lærer i byen (I ran into my old teacher in town). It also works for difficulties: støde på modstand (face resistance).

sentence.da: Vi kan **støde på** problemer, når vi bygger huset.
sentence.en: We may come across problems when we build the house.

at stønne.explanation: "At stønne" means "to groan", to make a deep sound from pain, effort or annoyance. With over it names what bothers you: stønne over varmen (to groan about the heat).

sentence.da: Man kan **stønne**, når man løfter noget meget tungt.
sentence.en: You can groan when you lift something very heavy.

at støtte.explanation: "At støtte" means "to support" a person or a cause: Mine forældre støtter mig (My parents support me). It also means "to lean on": Han støttede sig til væggen (He leaned on the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **støtte** dig.
sentence.en: I will always support you.

at støve af.explanation: "At støve af" means "to dust", to wipe dust off furniture and things. The thing goes between: Jeg støver hylderne af (I dust the shelves). It also fits old skills: støve sit fransk af (dust off your French).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **støve af** i stuen, når gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: I will dust in the living room when the guests come.

at støvsuge.explanation: "At støvsuge" means "to vacuum". It is built from støv (dust) and suge (suck): Han støvsuger trappen (He vacuums the stairs). The machine is en støvsuger (a vacuum cleaner).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **støvsuge** stuen i dag.
sentence.en: I have to vacuum the living room today.

at suge.explanation: "At suge" means "to suck", pulling something in with your mouth or a machine: Babyen suger på sutten (The baby sucks on the pacifier).

sentence.da: Barnet kan **suge** saften op med et sugerør.
sentence.en: The child can suck the juice up with a straw.

at sukke.explanation: "At sukke" means "to sigh", letting out a deep breath when you are tired, sad or annoyed: Hun sukkede dybt (She sighed deeply). A sigh is et suk.

sentence.da: Min bror kan **sukke** højt, når han keder sig.
sentence.en: My brother can sigh loudly when he is bored.

at sulte.explanation: "At sulte" means "to starve", to suffer from having too little food: Børnene sulter (The children are starving). To say you are simply hungry, use Jeg er sulten (I am hungry), not sulte.

sentence.da: Ingen skal **sulte**, når der er mad nok til alle.
sentence.en: Nobody should starve when there is enough food for everyone.

at summe.explanation: "At summe" means "to buzz", to make the soft, steady sound of a bee, a fly or a machine: Bierne summer i haven (The bees buzz in the garden). A place can buzz too: Byen summer af liv (The city buzzes with life). To hum a tune is at nynne, not at summe.

sentence.da: Om sommeren kan man høre fluer **summe** i vinduet.
sentence.en: In summer you can hear flies buzz in the window.

at supplere.explanation: "At supplere" means "to supplement", to add something to what you already have so that it is enough: Han supplerer sin løn med et deltidsjob (He supplements his salary with a part-time job). With hinanden (each other), it means they fill in what the other lacks: De supplerer hinanden (They complement each other).

sentence.da: Du kan **supplere** din kost med frugt og grønt.
sentence.en: You can supplement your diet with fruit and vegetables.

at sutte.explanation: "At sutte" means "to suck", to take something into the mouth and keep it there. The thing comes after på: Babyen sutter på flasken (The baby sucks on the bottle).

sentence.da: Barnet kan lide at **sutte** på tommelfingeren.
sentence.en: The child likes to suck on the thumb.

at svare.explanation: "At svare" means "to answer" or "to reply". To answer a question, add på (on): svare på et spørgsmål (to answer a question).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **svare** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: I can answer the question.

at svare igen.explanation: "At svare igen" means "to talk back", to reply to someone in a rude or cheeky way, usually a child to a parent or teacher: Svar ikke igen! (Do not talk back!). Igen usually means "again", but here it means "back".

sentence.da: Drengen må ikke **svare igen**, når mor skælder ud.
sentence.en: The boy must not talk back when mom scolds him.

at svare på.explanation: "At svare på" means "to answer" or "to reply to", and på always follows the thing you answer: Jeg svarer på din besked (I reply to your message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **svare på** din mail i morgen.
sentence.en: I will reply to your email tomorrow.

at svede.explanation: "At svede" means "to sweat": Jeg sveder, når jeg løber (I sweat when I run). It also fits nerves: Hun sveder over eksamen (She is sweating over the exam).

sentence.da: Når det er varmt, kan jeg **svede** meget.
sentence.en: When it is hot, I can sweat a lot.

at svigte.explanation: "At svigte" means "to let down" or "to fail", to go back on someone who trusted you: Han svigtede sine børn (He let his children down). It also describes things that stop working when needed: Bremserne svigtede (The brakes failed).

sentence.da: En ven må aldrig **svigte** en anden, når det går galt.
sentence.en: A friend must never let another down when things go wrong.

at svinge.explanation: "At svinge" means "to swing", to move back and forth or in an arc: Pendulet svinger (The pendulum swings). It is also the everyday verb for turning while driving or biking.

sentence.da: Du skal **svinge** til venstre ved lyskrydset.
sentence.en: You must turn left at the traffic light.

at svække.explanation: "At svække" means "to weaken", to make something less strong, often little by little: at svække immunforsvaret (to weaken the immune system).

sentence.da: Lange nætter uden søvn kan **svække** kroppen.
sentence.en: Long nights without sleep can weaken the body.

at sværge.explanation: "At sværge" means "to swear", to promise something very seriously: Jeg sværger, jeg har ikke gjort det (I swear I did not do it). It is not the word for bad language. For that, Danes use at bande (to curse).

sentence.da: Vidnet skal **sværge** at sige sandheden i retten.
sentence.en: The witness must swear to tell the truth in court.

at svømme.explanation: "At svømme" means "to swim": Jeg svømmer i havet (I swim in the sea). For a quick dip, Danes also say at bade (to go for a swim): Vi bader i søen (We are going for a swim in the lake).

sentence.da: Fisk kan **svømme** i vandet.
sentence.en: Fish can swim in the water.

at sy.explanation: "At sy" means "to sew": Jeg syr en knap på (I am sewing on a button). It also covers closing a cut with stitches: Lægen syede såret (The doctor stitched the wound).

sentence.da: Min mor kan **sy** sine egne kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother can sew her own dresses.

at sygemelde sig.explanation: "At sygemelde sig" means "to call in sick", telling your employer that you are ill: Jeg sygemelder mig i dag (I am calling in sick today).

sentence.da: Hun må **sygemelde sig**, fordi hun har feber.
sentence.en: She has to call in sick because she has a fever.

at symbolisere.explanation: "At symbolisere" means "to symbolize", to stand for an idea or feeling. The symbol comes first, then the idea: Duen symboliserer fred (The dove symbolizes peace), not the other way around.

sentence.da: Et rødt hjerte kan **symbolisere** kærlighed.
sentence.en: A red heart can symbolize love.

at synes.explanation: "At synes" means "to think", in the sense of having an opinion: Jeg synes, det er godt (I think it is good). For a guess about a fact, use at tro (to believe, to guess): Jeg tror, han kommer (I think he is coming). Hvad synes du? means "What do you think?".

sentence.da: Hvad **synes** du om maden?
sentence.en: What do you think about the food?

at synge.explanation: "At synge" means "to sing". To sing along with others or with a recording, add med (with): Jeg synger med (I sing along).

sentence.da: Hun kan **synge** en smuk sang.
sentence.en: She can sing a beautiful song.

at synke.explanation: "At synke" means "to sink" and also "to swallow": Skibet synker (The ship sinks). Jeg kan ikke synke (I can't swallow).

sentence.da: Den tunge sten vil **synke** i vandet.
sentence.en: The heavy stone will sink in the water.

at såre.explanation: "At såre" means "to hurt" or "to wound", mostly someone's feelings: Dine ord sårede mig (Your words hurt me). For pain in the body, Danes say at gøre ondt: Det gør ondt (It hurts).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **såre** dig, men jeg må sige sandheden.
sentence.en: I do not want to hurt you, but I must tell the truth.

at sælge.explanation: "At sælge" means "to sell". Til salg means "for sale", as on a sign: Bilen er til salg (The car is for sale).

sentence.da: Bageren vil **sælge** brød i butikken.
sentence.en: The baker wants to sell bread in the store.

at sænke.explanation: "At sænke" means "to lower", to make something go down: at sænke stemmen (to lower your voice). Compare at synke (to sink), which happens by itself: Skibet synker (The ship sinks). With sænke, someone does it: Piraterne sænker skibet (The pirates sink the ship).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **sænke** priserne, fordi der er for få kunder.
