sentence.en: My big brother is ten years older than me.

en storesøster.explanation: "En storesøster" means "a big sister": any sister who is older than you, whatever the age gap.

sentence.da: Min **storesøster** er tre år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big sister is three years older than me.

en storfamilie.explanation: "En storfamilie" means "an extended family", a family that includes grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins, not only parents and children.

sentence.da: Til jul samles hele min **storfamilie** hos mormor.
sentence.en: At Christmas my whole extended family gathers at Grandma's.

en stork.explanation: "En stork" means "a stork", a large white bird with black wing tips that builds big nests on roofs and flies south for the winter.

sentence.da: En **stork** har meget lange ben og et langt næb.
sentence.en: A stork has very long legs and a long beak.

en storm.explanation: "En storm" means "a storm" with very strong wind. It is stronger than blæst (windy weather) and weaker than en orkan (a hurricane).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **storm** med meget vind.
sentence.en: A storm is coming with a lot of wind.

en stormflod.explanation: "En stormflod" means "a storm surge", a sudden rise of the sea when strong wind pushes water toward the coast and covers low land. The word is used in weather warnings along the coast.

sentence.da: Ved en **stormflod** presser vinden havet ind over kysten.
sentence.en: In a storm surge, the wind pushes the sea in over the coast.

en straf.explanation: "En straf" means "a punishment". You get one with at få en straf (to get a punishment), and you give one with at give en straf (to give a punishment).

sentence.da: Børn får en **straf**, når de gør noget forkert.
sentence.en: Children get a punishment when they do something wrong.

en straffeattest.explanation: "En straffeattest" means "a criminal record", an official paper that shows whether you have been found guilty of anything. Some employers ask to see one before they hire someone.

sentence.da: Til jobbet skal du aflevere en **straffeattest** fra politiet.
sentence.en: For the job you have to hand in a criminal record from the police.

en strand.explanation: "En strand" means "a beach", the sandy edge of the sea or a lake. You say på stranden (at the beach), using på (on), not i (in).

sentence.da: Der er sand og hav ved en **strand**.
sentence.en: There is sand and sea at a beach.

en strandpromenade.explanation: "En strandpromenade" means "a beach promenade", a wide walkway for strolling along the beach.

sentence.da: Vi går langs havet på en lang **strandpromenade**.
sentence.en: We walk along the sea on a long beach promenade.

en strandtur.explanation: "En strandtur" means "a trip to the beach", usually for a day. It is built from strand (beach) and tur (trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **strandtur**, hvis det bliver pænt vejr.
sentence.en: We will go on a beach trip if the weather is nice.

en strategi.explanation: "En strategi" means "a strategy", a clever overall approach for winning or succeeding over a long time. A taktik (tactic) is smaller: the way you act in one moment.

sentence.da: Firmaet har en klar **strategi** for de næste fem år.
sentence.en: The firm has a clear strategy for the next five years.

en streamingtjeneste.explanation: "En streamingtjeneste" means "a streaming service", built from streaming and en tjeneste (a service). Tjeneste also means a favor: Kan du gøre mig en tjeneste? (Can you do me a favor?)

sentence.da: Vi betaler for en **streamingtjeneste** hver måned.
sentence.en: We pay for a streaming service every month.

en streg.explanation: "En streg" means "a line" or "a stroke" drawn with a pen. It also appears in the saying en streg i regningen (a wrench in the works), an unwelcome surprise that ruins a plan.

sentence.da: Tegn en **streg** på papiret med en lineal.
sentence.en: Draw a line on the paper with a ruler.

en strejke.explanation: "En strejke" means "a strike", when workers stop working to demand better pay or conditions. To go on strike, say at strejke: De vil strejke (They will go on strike).

sentence.da: Toget kører ikke, fordi lokomotivførerne er i **strejke**.
sentence.en: The train is not running because the train drivers are on strike.

en strid.explanation: "En strid" means "a dispute" or "a conflict", a serious disagreement between people, groups or countries. I strid med (in conflict with) is a common way to say that something goes against a rule: i strid med reglerne (against the rules).

sentence.da: Der er en lang **strid** mellem naboerne om et hegn.
sentence.en: There is a long dispute between the neighbors about a fence.

en strikhue.explanation: "En strikhue" means "a knitted hat", a warm woolen hat for cold weather, usually pulled down over the ears.

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **strikhue** på, fordi det er koldt.
sentence.en: I put on a knitted hat because it is cold.

en strofe.explanation: "En strofe" means "a stanza", a group of lines in a poem or song that belong together and are set apart by a blank line. In a song, the stanzas take turns with the chorus.

sentence.da: Hver **strofe** i digtet har fire linjer og rimer.
sentence.en: Each stanza in the poem has four lines and rhymes.

en strube.explanation: "En strube" means "a throat", the passage in your neck that air and food go through. In everyday talk, Danes more often say hals (throat / neck).

sentence.da: Der sidder noget fast i min **strube**.
sentence.en: Something is stuck in my throat.

en struktur.explanation: "En struktur" means "a structure", the way the parts of something are arranged, for example in a text, an organization or a building.

sentence.da: Teksten har en tydelig **struktur** med en indledning og en afslutning.
sentence.en: The text has a clear structure with an introduction and an ending.

en strygning.explanation: "En strygning" means "an ironing", the household job of making clothes smooth and flat with heat.

sentence.da: Efter **strygning** ser skjorten pæn og glat ud.
sentence.en: After ironing the shirt looks neat and smooth.

en strømpe.explanation: "En strømpe" means "a stocking" or "a sock", a soft piece of clothing that covers your foot. You wear strømper inside your shoes: Jeg har strømper på (I am wearing socks).

sentence.da: Man har en **strømpe** på hver fod.
sentence.en: You wear a sock on each foot.

en studentereksamen.explanation: "En studentereksamen" means "a high school diploma", the exam you pass after three years at a Danish school for ages 16 to 19. It lets you apply to university.

sentence.da: Med en **studentereksamen** kan man søge ind på universitetet.
sentence.en: With a high school diploma you can apply to the university.

en studenterfest.explanation: "En studenterfest" means "a graduation party", the party held when a young person has passed the final school exams. Families often invite friends and relatives home.

sentence.da: Min familie holder en stor **studenterfest**, når jeg bliver student.
sentence.en: My family is holding a big graduation party when I graduate.

en studenterhue.explanation: "En studenterhue" means "a graduation cap", the white cap with a colored band that young Danes put on after passing their final school exams.

sentence.da: Hun har sin **studenterhue** på, fordi hun lige har bestået eksamen.
sentence.en: She has her graduation cap on because she just passed her exam.

en studerende.explanation: "En studerende" means "a student", especially at a university: Der er mange studerende i byen (There are many students in town). The plural is studerende too. For a school child, use en elev (a pupil).

sentence.da: Hun er **studerende** på universitetet.
sentence.en: She is a student at the university.

en studiegruppe.explanation: "En studiegruppe" means "a study group", a small team of people who study the same subject and meet to work together.

sentence.da: Vi mødes i vores **studiegruppe** hver torsdag og læser sammen.
sentence.en: We meet in our study group every Thursday and read together.

en studiekammerat.explanation: "En studiekammerat" means "a fellow student", someone you study with at the same school or university.

sentence.da: Jeg låner noter af min **studiekammerat**, når jeg har været syg.
sentence.en: I borrow notes from my fellow student when I have been sick.

en studieplan.explanation: "En studieplan" means "a study plan", a list showing what you will study and when, for a course or for your own reading.

sentence.da: I min **studieplan** står der, hvad jeg skal læse hver uge.
sentence.en: My study plan says what I must read each week.

en studieretning.explanation: "En studieretning" means "a field of study", the line you choose at a Danish gymnasium, such as languages or science, which decides which classes take up most of your time.

sentence.da: På min **studieretning** har vi meget matematik og fysik.
sentence.en: In my field of study we have a lot of math and physics.

en studietur.explanation: "En studietur" means "a study trip", a trip with a school or a group to see a place connected to what they are learning.

sentence.da: Klassen tager på **studietur** til Berlin og besøger flere museer.
sentence.en: The class is going on a study trip to Berlin and visiting several museums.

en stue.explanation: "En stue" means "a living room", the room where you sit, relax and have guests. It also gives the ground floor its name: stueetagen (the ground floor).

sentence.da: Vi har en sofa i vores **stue**.
sentence.en: We have a sofa in our living room.

en stund.explanation: "En stund" means "a while", a stretch of time that is not exactly measured: Vi ventede en stund (We waited for a while). It can also describe a short spell of a certain kind: en rolig stund (a calm spell).

sentence.da: Det varer kun en **stund**, og så er det forbi.
sentence.en: It only lasts a while, and then it is over.

en styrelse.explanation: "En styrelse" means "an agency", a public body that handles one area of society for the state. Its name usually names the area: Sundhedsstyrelsen (the Danish Health Authority).

sentence.da: Ansøgningen skal sendes til en **styrelse** under ministeriet.
sentence.en: The application must be sent to an agency under the ministry.

en styrke.explanation: "En styrke" means "a strength", a thing you are good at: Min styrke er at lytte (My strength is listening). It also means physical power: Han har stor styrke i armene (He has great strength in his arms).

sentence.da: Matematik er min **styrke**, men sprog er svært.
sentence.en: Math is my strength, but languages are hard.

en størrelse.explanation: "En størrelse" means "a size", for clothes, shoes or anything else. It comes from stor (big), so en større størrelse is a bigger size.

sentence.da: Har I en større **størrelse** i kjolen?
sentence.en: Do you have a bigger size in the dress?

en støtte.explanation: "En støtte" means "a support", something or someone that holds you up. It can be money too: en støtte fra staten (support from the state).

sentence.da: Min familie er en stor **støtte**.
sentence.en: My family is a great support.

en støvle.explanation: "En støvle" means "a boot". Boots come in pairs, so you often hear et par støvler (a pair of boots). Rubber boots are gummistøvler, built on the same word.

sentence.da: Min venstre **støvle** er våd i regnen.
sentence.en: My left boot is wet in the rain.

en støvsuger.explanation: "En støvsuger" means "a vacuum cleaner". It is built from støv (dust) and suger (sucker), which comes from at suge (to suck). Suge also gives et sugerør (a straw).

sentence.da: Jeg henter en **støvsuger** og gør stuen ren.
sentence.en: I get a vacuum cleaner and clean the living room.

en støvsugning.explanation: "En støvsugning" means "a vacuuming", the job of cleaning floors and carpets with a machine that sucks up dirt.

sentence.da: Efter en grundig **støvsugning** er hele gulvet rent.
sentence.en: After a thorough vacuuming the whole floor is clean.

en succes.explanation: "En succes" means "a success", something that went well: Festen blev en succes (The party was a success). Without en, it means success in general: Han har succes som forfatter (He is successful as an author).

sentence.da: Middagen blev en stor **succes**.
sentence.en: The dinner was a big success.

en suite.explanation: "En suite" means "a suite", a large, fine hotel room, often with a separate living area.

sentence.da: Vi har booket en **suite** med to soveværelser.
sentence.en: We have booked a suite with two bedrooms.

en sukkerskål.explanation: "En sukkerskål" means "a sugar bowl", the small bowl for sugar on the table.

sentence.da: Sukkeret ligger i en lille **sukkerskål**.
sentence.en: The sugar is in a small sugar bowl.

en sum.explanation: "En sum" means "a sum", an amount of money or the result of adding numbers. In math, summen af to og tre er fem (the sum of two and three is five).

sentence.da: Han betalte en stor **sum** for huset.
sentence.en: He paid a large sum for the house.

en sundhedsplejerske.explanation: "En sundhedsplejerske" means "a health visitor", built from sundhed (health) and pleje (care). She visits families to check on babies and small children.

sentence.da: Vi har en tid hos en **sundhedsplejerske** med babyen.
sentence.en: We have an appointment with a health visitor for the baby.

en suppe.explanation: "En suppe" means "a soup", as in tomatsuppe (tomato soup). The verb to use is at spise (to eat), not at drikke (to drink).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **suppe** med en ske.
sentence.en: I eat hot soup with a spoon.

en sut.explanation: "En sut" means "a pacifier", the rubber tip a baby sucks on.

sentence.da: Babyen falder i søvn med sin **sut** i munden.
sentence.en: The baby falls asleep with its pacifier in its mouth.

en sutteflaske.explanation: "En sutteflaske" means "a baby bottle", used to give a baby milk through a rubber tip.

sentence.da: Babyen drikker mælk af en **sutteflaske**.
sentence.en: The baby drinks milk from a baby bottle.

en svaghed.explanation: "En svaghed" means "a weakness", something you are not good at or find hard to resist. It can also mean a lack of strength in the body: svaghed i benene (weakness in the legs).

sentence.da: Min største **svaghed** er, at jeg aldrig siger nej til kage.
sentence.en: My biggest weakness is that I never say no to cake.

en svamp.explanation: "En svamp" means "a mushroom", and also "a sponge" for washing: Jeg samler svampe om efteråret (I pick mushrooms in the fall). Jeg vasker op med en svamp (I wash up with a sponge).

sentence.da: Han fandt en stor **svamp** i skoven.
sentence.en: He found a big mushroom in the forest.

en svane.explanation: "En svane" means "a swan", a large white bird with a long neck that swims on lakes. A baby swan is en svaneunge (a cygnet).

sentence.da: En hvid **svane** svømmer på søen.
sentence.en: A white swan swims on the lake.

en svans.explanation: "En svans" means "a tail", the long part at the back of an animal's body, such as a squirrel's or a horse's. The word hale (tail) means the same and is also common.

sentence.da: Ræven har en lang og tyk **svans**.
sentence.en: The fox has a long, thick tail.

en svensker.explanation: "En svensker" means "a Swede", a person from Sweden: Min kollega er svensker (My colleague is Swedish). The country is Sverige, and the language is svensk (Swedish).

sentence.da: Han er **svensker** og kommer fra Malmø.
sentence.en: He is Swedish and comes from Malmö.

en svigerdatter.explanation: "En svigerdatter" means "a daughter-in-law", your son's wife.

sentence.da: Min søns kone er min **svigerdatter**.
sentence.en: My son's wife is my daughter-in-law.

en svigerfar.explanation: "En svigerfar" means "a father-in-law", the father of your husband or wife. It is built from sviger- (in-law) and far (father).

sentence.da: Min **svigerfar** er pensioneret.
sentence.en: My father-in-law is retired.

en svigerinde.explanation: "En svigerinde" means "a sister-in-law", your brother's wife or your spouse's sister.

sentence.da: Min **svigerinde** er gift med min bror.
sentence.en: My sister-in-law is married to my brother.

en svigermor.explanation: "En svigermor" means "a mother-in-law", the mother of your husband or wife. It is built from sviger- (in-law) and mor (mother).

sentence.da: Min **svigermor** kommer til middag i aften.
sentence.en: My mother-in-law is coming to dinner tonight.

en svigersøn.explanation: "En svigersøn" means "a son-in-law", your daughter's husband.

sentence.da: Min datters mand er min **svigersøn**.
sentence.en: My daughter's husband is my son-in-law.

en svindler.explanation: "En svindler" means "a swindler", a person who cheats others out of money by pretending to be someone else or offering something that does not exist. It belongs to at svindle (to cheat).

sentence.da: En **svindler** ringede og ville have mine bankoplysninger.
sentence.en: A swindler called and wanted my bank details.

en svinestald.explanation: "En svinestald" means "a pigsty", the building where pigs live on a farm. It is built from svin (pig) and stald (a shed for farm animals).

sentence.da: Grisene bor i en varm **svinestald** på gården.
sentence.en: The pigs live in a warm pigsty on the farm.

en svoger.explanation: "En svoger" means "a brother-in-law", your sister's husband or your spouse's brother.

sentence.da: Min **svoger** er gift med min søster.
sentence.en: My brother-in-law is married to my sister.

en sværm.explanation: "En sværm" means "a swarm", a big group of insects moving together. It can also be a crowd of people pushing around someone: en sværm af fans (a swarm of fans).

sentence.da: Der fløj en **sværm** af myg rundt om lampen.
sentence.en: A swarm of mosquitoes flew around the lamp.

en svømmebane.explanation: "En svømmebane" means "a swimming lane", one of the long strips of water in a pool that are marked off with ropes, so each person has their own.

sentence.da: I konkurrencen har hver deltager sin egen **svømmebane**.
sentence.en: In the competition each participant has their own lane.

en svømmehal.explanation: "En svømmehal" means "an indoor swimming pool", a public building where you can swim all year. It is built from at svømme (to swim) and en hal (a hall).

sentence.da: Vi går i **svømmehal** hver lørdag, og børnene elsker det.
sentence.en: We go to the swimming pool every Saturday, and the children love it.

en svømmetur.explanation: "En svømmetur" means "a swim", a trip to swim for fun or exercise. It is built from svømme (to swim) and tur (trip).

sentence.da: Efter arbejde tager jeg en **svømmetur** i poolen.
sentence.en: After work I go for a swim in the pool.

en sweater.explanation: "En sweater" means "a sweater", a warm top you pull over your head. To say you are wearing one, use have ... på (literally have ... on): Jeg har en sweater på (I am wearing a sweater).

sentence.da: Du kan holde varmen i en **sweater**.
sentence.en: You can stay warm in a sweater.

en sygdom.explanation: "En sygdom" means "a disease" or "an illness". It comes from syg (sick). You say Jeg er syg (I am sick) about yourself, and en sygdom for the illness itself.

sentence.da: Han er syg og har en alvorlig **sygdom**.
sentence.en: He is sick and has a serious illness.

en sygemelding.explanation: "En sygemelding" means "a sick note / sick leave", telling your workplace that you are ill and cannot come in, or the time off that follows. To call in sick, Danes say at melde sig syg.

sentence.da: Jeg har sendt min **sygemelding** til chefen i morges.
sentence.en: I sent my sick note to the boss this morning.

en sygeplejerske.explanation: "En sygeplejerske" means "a nurse". It comes from sygepleje (nursing). Male nurses are also called sygeplejerske, so the word is not only for women.

sentence.da: Min søster er **sygeplejerske** på et hospital.
sentence.en: My sister is a nurse at a hospital.

en synagoge.explanation: "En synagoge" means "a synagogue", a building where Jewish people pray and meet for services.

sentence.da: Jøder samles i en **synagoge**, når de skal bede.
sentence.en: Jews gather in a synagogue when they are going to pray.

en synd.explanation: "En synd" means "a sin", an act that is wrong according to religion. In everyday speech, synd is also a way to say you feel sorry for someone, with no religion involved: Det er synd for ham (I feel sorry for him).

sentence.da: I mange religioner er det en **synd** at stjæle.
sentence.en: In many religions it is a sin to steal.

en synder.explanation: "En synder" means "a sinner", a person who has done wrong in the eyes of religion. It also means the one to blame for something small, such as a missing cake: Hvem er synderen? (Who is the culprit?)

sentence.da: I kirken kan hver **synder** få tilgivelse.
sentence.en: In the church, every sinner can receive forgiveness.

en synkronisering.explanation: "En synkronisering" means "a sync", when two devices or accounts are made to hold the same information. It is also used when things are timed to happen together, such as sound and picture in a film.

sentence.da: Efter **synkronisering** har telefonen og computeren de samme filer.
sentence.en: After syncing, the phone and the computer have the same files.

en synsvinkel.explanation: "En synsvinkel" means "a point of view / angle", the way someone looks at a question, based on their own situation. It can also be the real angle from which you see something, such as in a photo.

sentence.da: Fra hans **synsvinkel** ser problemet helt anderledes ud.
sentence.en: From his point of view the problem looks completely different.

en syre.explanation: "En syre" means "an acid", a chemical that tastes sharp and can burn or eat into things.

sentence.da: Citron smager surt, fordi den indeholder en **syre**.
sentence.en: Lemon tastes sour because it contains an acid.

en sæk.explanation: "En sæk" means "a sack", a big bag of cloth or paper that holds heavy things like potatoes or flour. A small shopping bag is not a sæk.

sentence.da: Kartoflerne ligger i en **sæk** i kælderen.
sentence.en: The potatoes are in a sack in the cellar.

en sæl.explanation: "En sæl" means "a seal", the animal that swims in the sea and rests on rocks. A seal on a document is a different word: et segl (a stamp seal).

sentence.da: En **sæl** fanger fisk i havet.
sentence.en: A seal catches fish in the sea.

en sælger.explanation: "En sælger" means "a salesperson", someone who sells things for a living. It comes from at sælge (to sell).

sentence.da: En **sælger** hjælper kunderne i butikken.
sentence.en: A salesperson helps the customers in the store.

en sælgerske.explanation: "En sælgerske" means "a saleswoman". The word sounds old-fashioned today, and people usually say en sælger (a salesperson) for both men and women.

sentence.da: Den venlige **sælgerske** hjalp mig med skoene.
sentence.en: The friendly saleswoman helped me with the shoes.

en sæson.explanation: "En sæson" means "a season" for sports, TV shows and fruit: Jordbærsæsonen starter i juni (The strawberry season starts in June). For spring, summer, fall and winter, use en årstid.

sentence.da: Tv-serien har ti afsnit i hver **sæson**.
sentence.en: The TV series has ten episodes in each season.

en sæsonbillet.explanation: "En sæsonbillet" means "a season ticket", a ticket that lets you attend a whole series of matches or performances. Et sæsonkort (a season pass) is another common word for it.

sentence.da: Med en **sæsonbillet** kan jeg se alle klubbens hjemmekampe.
sentence.en: With a season ticket I can see all the club's home games.

en sætning.explanation: "En sætning" means "a sentence", words that make a full thought. For a prison sentence, use en dom (a verdict) or en straf (a punishment) instead.

sentence.da: En **sætning** slutter med et punktum.
sentence.en: A sentence ends with a period.

en sø.explanation: "En sø" means "a lake", a body of fresh water with land all around it. Do not mix it up with et hav (a sea), which is much bigger and salty.

sentence.da: Man kan bade og fiske i en **sø**.
sentence.en: You can swim and fish in a lake.

en søgemaskine.explanation: "En søgemaskine" means "a search engine", a website where you look for things online.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger ofte en **søgemaskine** til at finde opskrifter.
sentence.en: I often use a search engine to find recipes.

en sølvfisk.explanation: "En sølvfisk" means "a silverfish", a small silver-colored insect without wings that sometimes shows up in houses. Despite fisk (fish) in the name, it is not a fish.

sentence.da: En **sølvfisk** bor helst på mørke og fugtige steder.
sentence.en: A silverfish prefers to live in dark and damp places.

en søn.explanation: "En søn" means "a son". It is used for a son of any age, even a grown-up one: Hendes søn er tredive (Her son is thirty).

sentence.da: Min bror har en **søn** og en datter.
sentence.en: My brother has a son and a daughter.

en søndagsmiddag.explanation: "En søndagsmiddag" means "a Sunday dinner", a special meal that families eat together on Sunday.

sentence.da: Hele familien spiser sammen til **søndagsmiddag**.
sentence.en: The whole family eats together at Sunday dinner.

en søster.explanation: "En søster" means "a sister". For a sister who shares only one parent, say en halvsøster (a half sister).

sentence.da: Min **søster** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My sister and I have the same mother.

en søstjerne.explanation: "En søstjerne" means "a starfish", a flat animal of the sea with a star shape. The word is built from sø (sea) and stjerne (star).

sentence.da: En **søstjerne** har som regel fem arme og lever i havet.
sentence.en: A starfish usually has five arms and lives in the sea.

et s-tog.explanation: "Et S-tog" means "an S-train", the commuter train around Copenhagen. It runs often and stops close to many neighborhoods.

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **S-tog** ind til byen.
sentence.en: I take an S-train into the city.

et salg.explanation: "Et salg" means "a sale", the act of selling something. For a discount sale, use et udsalg (a clearance sale).

sentence.da: Han tjener penge på **salg** af brugte biler.
sentence.en: He makes money from the sale of used cars.

et samarbejde.explanation: "Et samarbejde" means "a collaboration", people or groups working together toward the same goal. For the partner, say i samarbejde med (in cooperation with): Vi laver det i samarbejde med kommunen (We are doing it in cooperation with the city).

sentence.da: Vi har et godt **samarbejde** med skolen.
sentence.en: We have a good collaboration with the school.

et samfund.explanation: "Et samfund" means "a society", the whole group of people living together under shared rules and habits.

sentence.da: Hvert **samfund** har sine egne regler.
sentence.en: Every society has its own rules.

et samfundsproblem.explanation: "Et samfundsproblem" means "a social problem", a problem that affects many people in a country, such as unemployment or pollution. The first part, samfunds-, comes from samfund (society).

sentence.da: Ensomhed blandt ældre er et stort **samfundsproblem**.
sentence.en: Loneliness among older people is a big social problem.

et samliv.explanation: "Et samliv" means "a life together", two people living as partners and sharing a home and a daily life. It covers the whole shared life, and Danes use it for couples with or without a wedding.

sentence.da: Deres **samliv** er roligt, og de skændes næsten aldrig.
sentence.en: Their life together is calm, and they almost never argue.

et sammenskudsgilde.explanation: "Et sammenskudsgilde" means "a potluck", a party where every guest brings a dish and everyone shares. The first part comes from at skyde sammen (to chip in together), and gilde means a feast.

sentence.da: Alle tager noget med til et **sammenskudsgilde**, så der er mad nok.
sentence.en: Everyone brings something to a potluck, so there is enough food.

et sammenstød.explanation: "Et sammenstød" means "a clash" and "a collision", when two things or two groups hit each other, or when two opinions cannot agree. It can be physical, like two cars: et sammenstød mellem to biler (a collision between two cars).

sentence.da: Der var et **sammenstød** mellem politiet og demonstranterne.
sentence.en: There was a clash between the police and the demonstrators.

et sammentræf.explanation: "Et sammentræf" means "a coincidence", when two things happen at the same time or in the same place by accident. It is surprising because nobody planned it: Sikke et sammentræf! (What a coincidence!)

sentence.da: Det var et **sammentræf**, at vi begge besøgte Rom samme dag.
sentence.en: It was a coincidence that we both visited Rome on the same day.

et samtaleemne.explanation: "Et samtaleemne" means "a topic of conversation", what you pick to talk about, for example with someone you have just met. It is built from samtale (conversation) and emne (topic).

sentence.da: Vejret er altid et godt **samtaleemne**.
sentence.en: The weather is always a good topic of conversation.

et samvær.explanation: "Et samvær" means "a time together", the time you spend with someone. In family matters, it has a special meaning: the time a child spends with the parent they do not live with, for example after the parents live apart.

sentence.da: Børnene har **samvær** med deres far hver anden weekend.
sentence.en: The children spend time with their father every other weekend.

et sankthansbål.explanation: "Et sankthansbål" means "a Midsummer bonfire", a big fire lit on the evening of June 23, when Danes meet outdoors and sing. A straw witch (en heks) is often put on top.

sentence.da: Mange tænder et stort **sankthansbål** ved vandet og synger sammen.
sentence.en: Many people light a big Midsummer bonfire by the water and sing together.

et sejl.explanation: "Et sejl" means "a sail", a large piece of strong cloth on a boat that catches the wind. At sejle (to sail) is wider: it means to travel by any boat, even without a sail, as in Færgen sejler til Sverige (The ferry sails to Sweden).

sentence.da: Båden har et hvidt **sejl**, som vinden blæser i.
sentence.en: The boat has a white sail that the wind blows into.

et sekund.explanation: "Et sekund" means "a second". Do not mix it up with second meaning number two: that is anden. Et øjeblik (a moment) is a similar short wait: Et øjeblik, tak (One moment, please).

sentence.da: Det tager kun et **sekund**.
sentence.en: It only takes a second.

et selskab.explanation: "Et selskab" means "a company" in business, and also "a party" or "a social gathering": Vi var til et selskab hos naboerne (We were at a party at the neighbors'). For a business, firma (company) is also common.

sentence.da: Vi holder et **selskab** for vores venner i morgen.
sentence.en: We are throwing a party for our friends tomorrow.

et semester.explanation: "Et semester" means "a semester", half of a year of study at a school or university.

sentence.da: Vi har eksamen i slutningen af hvert **semester**.
sentence.en: We have exams at the end of each semester.

et senat.explanation: "Et senat" means "a senate", the upper house in countries that have two, such as the United States. Denmark has only one house, called Folketinget.

sentence.da: USA har et **senat** med hundrede senatorer, to fra hver delstat.
sentence.en: The USA has a senate with a hundred senators, two from each state.

et shot.explanation: "Et shot" means "a shot", a small strong drink or a small amount of coffee: et shot espresso (a shot of espresso), et shot vodka (a shot of vodka).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **shot** espresso om morgenen.
sentence.en: I have a shot of espresso in the morning.

et show.explanation: "Et show" means "a show", an event where people sing, dance or tell jokes for an audience.

sentence.da: Vi så et fedt **show** med sang og dans i går.
sentence.en: We saw a cool show with singing and dancing yesterday.

et sidespor.explanation: "Et sidespor" means "a digression" and "a sidetrack", a part of a conversation that leads away from the main point. Literally it is a side track on a railway line, and Danes use it the same way for talk.

sentence.da: Vi kom ind på et **sidespor** og glemte, hvad mødet handlede om.
sentence.en: We got onto a sidetrack and forgot what the meeting was about.

et signal.explanation: "Et signal" means "a signal", a sign, sound or light that gives a message. It is also what your phone needs to work: Jeg har intet signal her (I have no signal here).

sentence.da: Når lyset skifter til grønt, er det et **signal** til at køre.
sentence.en: When the light changes to green, it is a signal to drive.

et sind.explanation: "Et sind" means "a mind", but it is about feelings and attitude more than about thinking: et åbent sind (an open mind). It describes the way a person is on the inside.

sentence.da: Hun har et roligt **sind** og bliver aldrig vred.
sentence.en: She has a calm mind and never gets angry.

et siv.explanation: "Et siv" means "a rush", a thin, tall, reed-like plant that grows on wet ground and at the edge of water, with many standing close together.

sentence.da: Ænderne bygger rede i det høje **siv** ved søen.
sentence.en: The ducks build nests in the tall rushes by the lake.

et skab.explanation: "Et skab" means "a cupboard", and also a cabinet, a closet or a locker: any closed space for storing things. Words are added to say which kind, for example et køleskab (a refrigerator, literally a cooling cupboard).

sentence.da: Tallerkenerne står i et **skab**.
sentence.en: The plates are in a cupboard.

et skattekort.explanation: "Et skattekort" means "a tax card", the record that tells your employer how much tax to take out of your pay. In Denmark it is digital, not a real card, and your employer gets it from the tax authorities.

sentence.da: Uden et **skattekort** kan arbejdsgiveren ikke trække den rigtige skat.
sentence.en: Without a tax card, the employer cannot withhold the right tax.

et skelet.explanation: "Et skelet" means "a skeleton", all the bones that hold a body up. It is also the bare frame of a building: Skelettet af huset er færdigt (The frame of the house is finished).

sentence.da: Når kødet er væk, er der kun et **skelet** tilbage.
sentence.en: When the flesh is gone, only a skeleton is left.

et skema.explanation: "Et skema" means "a schedule", such as the list of lessons for the week: Hvad står der på skemaet i dag? (What is on the schedule today?) It can also mean a form to fill in: Udfyld skemaet (Fill in the form).

sentence.da: Der er gymnastik på mit **skema** hver torsdag.
sentence.en: There is gym on my schedule every Thursday.

et skib.explanation: "Et skib" means "a ship". A smaller one is en båd (a boat). A cruise ship is et krydstogtskib.

sentence.da: Et stort **skib** sejler over havet til Norge.
sentence.en: A big ship sails across the sea to Norway.

et skift.explanation: "Et skift" means "a change": et skift i planen (a change in the plan). It also means "a work shift", like a day or night shift: et natskift (a night shift).

sentence.da: Han tager et ekstra **skift** i morgen.
sentence.en: He is taking an extra shift tomorrow.

et skilt.explanation: "Et skilt" means "a sign", a board with words or a picture. Watch out: Hun er skilt (She is divorced) uses the same word in another way.

sentence.da: Et **skilt** viser vej til stationen.
sentence.en: A sign shows the way to the station.

et skind.explanation: "Et skind" means "a skin" or "a hide", the skin of an animal, often with the fur on, used for rugs and clothes: et fåreskind (a sheepskin). For a person's skin, use en hud (skin) instead.

sentence.da: Et **skind** fra et får kan holde dig varm om vinteren.
sentence.en: A hide from a sheep can keep you warm in the winter.

et skjold.explanation: "Et skjold" means "a shield", a flat piece carried on the arm by soldiers and knights to block blows. The same word is in et våbenskjold (a coat of arms), a shield with the picture of a family or country.

sentence.da: Soldaten holdt sit **skjold** op for at stoppe pilene.
sentence.en: The soldier held up his shield to stop the arrows.

et skohorn.explanation: "Et skohorn" means "a shoehorn", a curved piece that helps your heel slide into a shoe. The name is sko (shoe) plus horn (horn).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **skohorn**, fordi skoene er stramme.
sentence.en: I use a shoehorn because the shoes are tight.

et skolefag.explanation: "Et skolefag" means "a school subject", like math, history or English. It is built from en skole (a school) and et fag (a subject).

sentence.da: Hvilket **skolefag** kan du bedst lide?
sentence.en: Which school subject do you like best?

et skoleår.explanation: "Et skoleår" means "a school year", from the end of one summer vacation to the next.

sentence.da: Efter sommerferien begynder et nyt **skoleår**.
sentence.en: After the summer vacation a new school year begins.

et skridt.explanation: "Et skridt" means "a step", one movement of the foot. It can also be a move in a plan: Det er et vigtigt skridt (It is an important step). A step on a stairway is et trin (a step).

sentence.da: Hun tog et **skridt** frem og smilede.
sentence.en: She took a step forward and smiled.

et skrig.explanation: "Et skrig" means "a scream", a loud cry from fear or pain. For the quiet opposite, use the verb at hviske (to whisper).

sentence.da: Vi hørte et **skrig** fra gaden.
sentence.en: We heard a scream from the street.

et skrivebord.explanation: "Et skrivebord" means "a desk". It is built from skrive (write) and bord (table), and skrive also appears in en skrivemaskine (a typewriter).

sentence.da: Hun sidder ved sit **skrivebord** og arbejder.
sentence.en: She sits at her desk and works.

et skud.explanation: "Et skud" means "a shot", from a gun or a kick in sports: Vi hørte et skud (We heard a shot). For a small strong drink, use et shot (a shot).

sentence.da: Hans **skud** gik forbi målet.
sentence.en: His shot missed the goal.

et skudsår.explanation: "Et skudsår" means "a gunshot wound", an injury from a bullet. It is built from skud (a shot) and sår (a wound), and the same ending appears in et knivsår (a stab wound).

sentence.da: Den sårede mand havde et **skudsår** i benet og blødte meget.
sentence.en: The wounded man had a gunshot wound in his leg and bled a lot.

et skudår.explanation: "Et skudår" means "a leap year", a year with 366 days instead of 365, which comes every four years. The extra day is called en skuddag (a leap day).

sentence.da: Februar har 29 dage i et **skudår**.
sentence.en: February has 29 days in a leap year.

et skuespil.explanation: "Et skuespil" means "a play", a story written to be acted out in a theater. Do not mix it up with en skuespiller (an actor), the person who acts in it.

sentence.da: I et **skuespil** taler skuespillerne med hinanden foran publikum.
sentence.en: In a play, the actors talk to each other in front of an audience.

et skur.explanation: "Et skur" means "a shed", a small building for tools, bikes or wood. It can also mean a rain shower, as in et regnskur (a rain shower).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **skur** bag huset.
sentence.en: We have a small shed behind the house.

et skybrud.explanation: "Et skybrud" means "a cloudburst", a sudden, extremely heavy rain that can fill the streets with water. It is built from sky (cloud) and brud (break), so it is literally a cloud breaking open.

sentence.da: Efter et **skybrud** stod gaderne under vand.
sentence.en: After a cloudburst, the streets were under water.

et skydevåben.explanation: "Et skydevåben" means "a firearm", a weapon that fires bullets. It is the general word for any gun, whatever its size.

sentence.da: Man må ikke have et **skydevåben** uden tilladelse.
sentence.en: You must not have a firearm without a permit.

et skæg.explanation: "Et skæg" means "a beard". A mustache is et overskæg, literally an over-beard.

sentence.da: Min far har et langt **skæg**.
sentence.en: My father has a long beard.

et skænderi.explanation: "Et skænderi" means "an argument", an angry quarrel with raised voices. A calm talk about different views is not a skænderi.

sentence.da: Det var et højlydt **skænderi**, og naboerne kunne høre det.
sentence.en: It was a loud argument, and the neighbors could hear it.

et skærebræt.explanation: "Et skærebræt" means "a cutting board". It is built from at skære (to cut) and bræt (board), and bræt also appears in et strygebræt (an ironing board).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer tomaterne på et **skærebræt** af træ.
sentence.en: I cut the tomatoes on a wooden cutting board.

et skærmbillede.explanation: "Et skærmbillede" means "a screenshot", a picture of what is on your phone or computer. It is built from skærm (screen) and billede (picture).

sentence.da: Jeg tog et **skærmbillede** af beskeden.
sentence.en: I took a screenshot of the message.

et skøn.explanation: "Et skøn" means "an estimate" and "a judgment": what someone thinks is right when exact numbers are missing. It is used in the phrase efter mit skøn (by my estimate). Do not mix it up with skøn (lovely), as in en skøn dag (a lovely day), which is a different word.

sentence.da: Det er kun et **skøn**, så den rigtige pris kan være højere.
sentence.en: It is only an estimate, so the real price may be higher.

et slag.explanation: "Et slag" means "a blow", a hit with a hand or an object, and also "a battle" in a war. It is also the beat in et hjerteslag (a heartbeat).

sentence.da: En hær kan vinde et **slag**, men tabe krigen.
sentence.en: An army can win a battle but lose the war.

et slagord.explanation: "Et slagord" means "a slogan", a short, catchy phrase that a company, a party or a demonstration uses to get attention.

sentence.da: Partiets **slagord** er kort, og mange kan huske det.
sentence.en: The party's slogan is short, and many people can remember it.

et slagsmål.explanation: "Et slagsmål" means "a fight" with fists. For a fight with words, use et skænderi (an argument).

sentence.da: Drengene kom i **slagsmål** efter skole.
sentence.en: The boys got into a fight after school.

et slagtilfælde.explanation: "Et slagtilfælde" means "a stroke", when the blood supply to part of the brain is suddenly cut off. A common cause is en blodprop (a blood clot).

sentence.da: Efter et **slagtilfælde** kunne han ikke bevæge sin højre arm.
sentence.en: After a stroke, he could not move his right arm.

et slips.explanation: "Et slips" means "a tie", the cloth you wear around your neck with a shirt: Han tager slips på (He puts on a tie). For a tied game, use uafgjort (tied).

sentence.da: Min far har **slips** på til mødet.
sentence.en: My father is wearing a tie to the meeting.

et slot.explanation: "Et slot" means "a castle" and also "a palace". Danish uses the same word for both.

sentence.da: Kongen bor på et stort **slot**.
sentence.en: The king lives in a big castle.

et smagsløg.explanation: "Et smagsløg" means "a taste bud", one of the tiny parts on the tongue that pick up sweet, sour, salty and bitter. A tasty dish is said to pirre smagsløgene (excite the taste buds).

sentence.da: Tungen har tusindvis af **smagsløg**, som kan mærke sødt og surt.
sentence.en: The tongue has thousands of taste buds that can feel sweet and sour.

et smil.explanation: "Et smil" means "a smile", the friendly look you make with your mouth, without any sound.

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **smil** og sagde hej.
sentence.en: She gave me a smile and said hi.

et smykke.explanation: "Et smykke" means "a piece of jewelry", one item you wear for decoration.

sentence.da: Hun har et smukt **smykke** om halsen.
sentence.en: She has a beautiful piece of jewelry around her neck.

et småbarn.explanation: "Et småbarn" means "a toddler", a child of about one to three years. It is built from små (small) and barn (child).

sentence.da: Et **småbarn** er for lille til at gå i skole.
sentence.en: A toddler is too little to go to school.

et smørrebrød.explanation: "Et smørrebrød" means "an open sandwich", rye bread with toppings and no top slice. It is built from smør (butter) and brød (bread).

sentence.da: Til frokost bestiller vi **smørrebrød** med fisk.
sentence.en: For lunch we order open sandwiches with fish.

et snefnug.explanation: "Et snefnug" means "a snowflake", one tiny flake of falling snow. It is built from sne (snow) and fnug (a bit of fluff).

sentence.da: Det første **snefnug** smelter i min hånd.
sentence.en: The first snowflake melts in my hand.

et snit.explanation: "Et snit" means "a cut", for example in cloth or skin, and also "an average", especially a grade average at school. The longer word for an average is et gennemsnit.

sentence.da: Hendes **snit** fra gymnasiet er højt nok til lægestudiet.
sentence.en: Her average from high school is high enough for medical school.

et snørebånd.explanation: "Et snørebånd" means "a shoelace", the cord that you tie to keep a shoe on your foot. It is built from at snøre (to lace up) and et bånd (a band).

sentence.da: Jeg skal binde mit **snørebånd**, før vi går.
sentence.en: I have to tie my shoelace before we go.

et sofabord.explanation: "Et sofabord" means "a coffee table". It is built from sofa (sofa) and bord (table), so it is the low table in front of the sofa.

sentence.da: Kopperne står på et lille **sofabord**.
sentence.en: The cups are on a small coffee table.

et solbær.explanation: "Et solbær" means "a blackcurrant", a small dark berry. Do not mix it up with et ribs (a redcurrant): Solbær er sorte, og ribs er røde (Blackcurrants are black, and redcurrants are red).

sentence.da: Jeg laver saft af **solbær** og vand.
sentence.en: I make juice from blackcurrants and water.

et solcenter.explanation: "Et solcenter" means "a tanning salon", where you pay to lie in a sunbed. It is built from sol (sun) and center (center).

sentence.da: Hun tager i **solcenter**, fordi hun vil være brun.
sentence.en: She goes to a tanning salon because she wants to be tan.

et solhverv.explanation: "Et solhverv" means "a solstice", one of the two days of the year when daylight is longest or shortest. Sommersolhverv (the summer solstice) is the longest day, and vintersolhverv (the winter solstice) is the shortest.

sentence.da: Ved **solhverv** i juni bliver det næsten aldrig helt mørkt.
sentence.en: At the solstice in June it almost never gets completely dark.

et solpanel.explanation: "Et solpanel" means "a solar panel", a flat plate, usually on a roof, that turns sunlight into electricity.

sentence.da: Vi har et **solpanel** på taget, og det giver strøm.
sentence.en: We have a solar panel on the roof, and it produces electricity.

et solstik.explanation: "Et solstik" means "a sunstroke", an illness from too much sun on your head and body, with headache, dizziness and nausea. Say fik solstik (got sunstroke) without et.

sentence.da: Hun fik **solstik** af at ligge i solen hele dagen.
sentence.en: She got sunstroke from lying in the sun all day.

et sommerhus.explanation: "Et sommerhus" means "a summer house" or "a cottage", a vacation home for weekends and summers. It is built from sommer (summer) and hus (house).

sentence.da: Vi tager i **sommerhus** hver sommer.
sentence.en: We go to the summer house every summer.

et sommerhusområde.explanation: "Et sommerhusområde" means "a summer house area", a zone with many vacation cottages, often near the sea. It is built from sommerhus (summer house) and område (area).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der stille i vores **sommerhusområde**.
sentence.en: In the winter, it is quiet in our summer house area.

et sommerjob.explanation: "Et sommerjob" means "a summer job", work you do during the summer vacation, often as a student. It is built from sommer (summer) and et job (a job).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have et **sommerjob** i en café.
sentence.en: I would like a summer job in a café.

et sortiment.explanation: "Et sortiment" means "an assortment", all the different goods that a shop or a company offers. Typical phrases are et bredt sortiment (a wide range) and et lille sortiment (a small range).

sentence.da: Butikken har et stort **sortiment** af ost fra hele Europa.
sentence.en: The shop has a large assortment of cheese from all over Europe.

et soundtrack.explanation: "Et soundtrack" means "a soundtrack", the music of a film, show or game.

sentence.da: Filmen har et flot **soundtrack**.
sentence.en: The movie has a nice soundtrack.

et soveværelse.explanation: "Et soveværelse" means "a bedroom". It is built from sove (to sleep) and værelse (room), and sove also appears in en sovepose (a sleeping bag).

sentence.da: Jeg sover i min seng i mit **soveværelse**.
sentence.en: I sleep in my bed in my bedroom.

et speciale.explanation: "Et speciale" means "a specialty" and "a master's thesis". As a specialty, it is what a person or a restaurant is best at: husets speciale (the house specialty). At a university, it is the large final project at the end of a master's degree.

sentence.da: Hun skriver **speciale** om børns sprog på universitetet.
sentence.en: She is writing her thesis about children's language at the university.

et spejl.explanation: "Et spejl" means "a mirror", a flat piece of glass that shows you your own face.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se mit ansigt i et **spejl**.
sentence.en: I can see my face in a mirror.

et spejlæg.explanation: "Et spejlæg" means "a fried egg" with a whole yolk, sunny side up. It is built from et spejl (a mirror) and et æg (an egg).

sentence.da: Han steger et **spejlæg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: He fries a sunny-side-up egg for breakfast.

et spil.explanation: "Et spil" means "a game", such as a board game, card game or computer game. It comes from at spille (to play), which is used for both games and music: at spille skak (to play chess), at spille guitar (to play guitar).

sentence.da: Skak er et **spil** for to personer.
sentence.en: Chess is a game for two people.

et spindelvæv.explanation: "Et spindelvæv" means "a spiderweb", the thin web of threads that spiders make to catch insects.

sentence.da: Edderkoppen fanger fluer i sit **spindelvæv**.
sentence.en: The spider catches flies in its spiderweb.

et spisebord.explanation: "Et spisebord" means "a dining table". It is built from at spise (to eat) and bord (table), and spise also appears in en spiseske (a tablespoon).

sentence.da: Vi har et stort **spisebord**, så der er plads til alle.
sentence.en: We have a big dining table, so there is room for everyone.

et spisekammer.explanation: "Et spisekammer" means "a pantry", a small room or cupboard for storing food.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger pasta og ris i vores **spisekammer**.
sentence.en: I put pasta and rice in our pantry.

et spisested.explanation: "Et spisested" means "an eatery", a general word for any place where you can sit down and eat, from a small diner to a fancy dining room. It does not say what kind of place it is.

sentence.da: Der er et billigt **spisested** lige ved stationen.
sentence.en: There is a cheap eatery right by the station.

et spor.explanation: "Et spor" means "a track" and "a trace": Der er spor i sneen (There are tracks in the snow). At a train station, it is the track number: Toget afgår fra spor 3 (The train leaves from track 3).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt et **spor** efter tyven.
sentence.en: The police found a trace of the thief.

et springvand.explanation: "Et springvand" means "a fountain", water that shoots up in a square or a park. It is built from springe (jump) and vand (water).

sentence.da: Der er et smukt **springvand** midt i parken.
sentence.en: There is a beautiful fountain in the middle of the park.

et sprog.explanation: "Et sprog" means "a language", such as English or Spanish.

sentence.da: Dansk og engelsk er to **sprog**.
sentence.en: Danish and English are two languages.

et sprogcenter.explanation: "Et sprogcenter" means "a language center", a school where adults learn a language. It is built from et sprog (a language) and et center (a center).

sentence.da: Jeg lærer dansk på et **sprogcenter** hver dag.
sentence.en: I learn Danish at a language center every day.

et spyd.explanation: "Et spyd" means "a spear", a long pole with a sharp point, thrown or pushed at an animal or an enemy. Danes use the same word for the javelin in athletics: at kaste spyd (to throw the javelin).

sentence.da: Vikingerne brugte et **spyd** til at jage og kæmpe.
sentence.en: The Vikings used a spear to hunt and fight.

et spædbarn.explanation: "Et spædbarn" means "an infant", a baby in its first months. A more everyday word is en baby (a baby).

sentence.da: Et **spædbarn** sover det meste af dagen.
sentence.en: An infant sleeps most of the day.

et spøgelse.explanation: "Et spøgelse" means "a ghost", the spirit of a dead person.

sentence.da: Der er et **spøgelse** i det gamle hus.
sentence.en: There is a ghost in the old house.

et spørgeskema.explanation: "Et spørgeskema" means "a questionnaire", a list of questions that many people fill in, often to collect opinions for a poll.

sentence.da: Alle studerende skal udfylde et **spørgeskema** om kurset.
sentence.en: All students must fill in a questionnaire about the course.

et spørgsmål.explanation: "Et spørgsmål" means "a question". A polite way to start is Må jeg stille et spørgsmål? (May I ask a question?). Literally, it says "put a question".

sentence.da: Læreren svarer på mit **spørgsmål**.
sentence.en: The teacher answers my question.

et spørgsmålstegn.explanation: "Et spørgsmålstegn" means "a question mark", built from spørgsmål (question) and tegn (sign). Tegn also means a sign in general: et tegn på forår (a sign of spring).

sentence.da: Sætningen slutter med et **spørgsmålstegn**, fordi den er et spørgsmål.
sentence.en: The sentence ends with a question mark because it is a question.

et stadie.explanation: "Et stadie" means "a stage", one part along the way in a process, such as an illness or a child growing up. A stage for a performance is en scene (a stage), not et stadie.

sentence.da: Sygdommen er i et tidligt **stadie**, og lægen er positiv.
sentence.en: The illness is at an early stage, and the doctor is optimistic.

et stadion.explanation: "Et stadion" means "a stadium", where big matches and concerts are held.

sentence.da: Der er mange mennesker på **stadion** i dag.
sentence.en: There are many people at the stadium today.

et standpunkt.explanation: "Et standpunkt" means "a point of view", a position that you have taken and can defend. Det er mit standpunkt (That is my position) sounds firm, as if you have thought it through.

sentence.da: Politikeren holder fast i sit **standpunkt**, selv når andre er uenige.
sentence.en: The politician sticks to his position, even when others disagree.

et statsborgerskab.explanation: "Et statsborgerskab" means "a citizenship", the legal status of belonging to a country, with duties and rights that foreigners do not have. To apply for it, say at ansøge om: ansøge om dansk statsborgerskab (to apply for Danish citizenship).

sentence.da: Hun fik dansk **statsborgerskab**, efter hun havde boet her i ni år.
sentence.en: She got Danish citizenship after she had lived here for nine years.

et stearinlys.explanation: "Et stearinlys" means "a candle", a stick of wax that you light on the table or in the window.

sentence.da: Hun tænder et **stearinlys**, når det bliver mørkt.
sentence.en: She lights a candle when it gets dark.

et sted.explanation: "Et sted" means "a place" or "a spot", and also "somewhere": Jeg har set det et sted means "I have seen it somewhere".

sentence.da: Er der et **sted** at spise her?
sentence.en: Is there a place to eat here?

et stedord.explanation: "Et stedord" means "a pronoun", a small word like han (he) or den (it) that stands in for a name or a thing.

sentence.da: Et **stedord** som han eller hun står i stedet for et navn.
sentence.en: A pronoun like he or she stands in place of a name.

et stik.explanation: "Et stik" means "a plug" and also "a sting" or "a prick", such as from an insect or a needle. Et stik fra en bi gør ondt (A sting from a bee hurts).

sentence.da: Sæt dit **stik** i væggen, så virker lampen.
sentence.en: Put your plug in the wall and the lamp works.

et stillads.explanation: "Et stillads" means "scaffolding", the temporary frame of metal poles and platforms that workers stand on when they build or repair the outside of a house.

sentence.da: Malerne står på et **stillads**, når de maler husets facade.
sentence.en: The painters stand on scaffolding when they paint the front of the house.

et sting.explanation: "Et sting" means "a stitch", one loop of thread in sewing, or one of the small stitches that close a cut. A sudden sharp pain in your side from running is et sidestik (a side stitch), not et sting.

sentence.da: Lægen lukkede såret med fem **sting**.
sentence.en: The doctor closed the wound with five stitches.

et stipendium.explanation: "Et stipendium" means "a scholarship", money given to a student or researcher to support their studies, which you do not have to pay back.

sentence.da: Hun fik et **stipendium** og kunne studere i udlandet.
sentence.en: She got a scholarship and could study abroad.

et stof.explanation: "Et stof" means "a fabric", and also "a drug" or "a substance": Stoffet er blødt (The fabric is soft). Det er et farligt stof (It is a dangerous drug).

sentence.da: Jeg vil sy en kjole af dette **stof**.
sentence.en: I want to sew a dress from this fabric.

et stoppested.explanation: "Et stoppested" means "a stop". It is built from stoppe (to stop) and sted (place). For a bus, say et busstoppested (a bus stop).

sentence.da: Næste **stoppested** er banegården.
sentence.en: The next stop is the railway station.

et storindkøb.explanation: "Et storindkøb" means "a big grocery shop", buying lots of food at once.

sentence.da: Vi laver et **storindkøb** i supermarkedet hver lørdag.
sentence.en: We do a big grocery shop at the supermarket every Saturday.

et stormagasin.explanation: "Et stormagasin" means "a department store", a large store with many departments under one roof, such as clothes, shoes and kitchenware. Magasin du Nord in Copenhagen is a well-known one.

sentence.da: I et **stormagasin** kan man købe tøj, sko og køkkenudstyr.
sentence.en: In a department store, you can buy clothes, shoes and kitchenware.

et straffespark.explanation: "Et straffespark" means "a penalty kick" in soccer. The referee gives one when a player breaks the rules inside the penalty area, and the kicker shoots alone against the player in goal.

sentence.da: Dommeren gav et **straffespark**, fordi forsvareren trak i trøjen.
sentence.en: The referee gave a penalty kick because the defender pulled the shirt.

et strygebræt.explanation: "Et strygebræt" means "an ironing board". It is built from at stryge (to iron) and et bræt (a board), the same bræt as in et skærebræt (a cutting board).

sentence.da: Hun stryger skjorten på et **strygebræt**.
sentence.en: She irons the shirt on an ironing board.

et strygejern.explanation: "Et strygejern" means "an iron" for clothes. It is built from at stryge (to iron) and jern (iron). The metal alone is just jern: et rør af jern (a pipe made of iron).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **strygejern** til skjorten.
sentence.en: I use an iron on the shirt.

et strømstik.explanation: "Et strømstik" means "a power plug", the part on the end of a cord that goes into the wall.

sentence.da: Der sidder et **strømstik** for enden af ledningen.
sentence.en: There is a power plug at the end of the cord.

et studie.explanation: "Et studie" means "a study", a piece of research that tests or measures something. For the time spent at a university, Danes say et studium (a study program).

sentence.da: Et nyt **studie** viser, at søvn er vigtig for hukommelsen.
sentence.en: A new study shows that sleep is important for memory.

et studiejob.explanation: "Et studiejob" means "a student job", a job that a student has next to their studies, often in a field related to what they study.

sentence.da: Han har et **studiejob** på et advokatkontor to dage om ugen.
sentence.en: He has a student job at a law office two days a week.

et studiekort.explanation: "Et studiekort" means "a student card", the card that proves you are enrolled at a school or university. In Denmark it gives you discounts, for example on trains and at museums.

sentence.da: Med dit **studiekort** får du rabat på toget.
sentence.en: With your student card, you get a discount on the train.

et studielån.explanation: "Et studielån" means "a student loan", money that you borrow from the state while you study and pay back later. In Denmark it comes on top of SU, the monthly support that students get.

sentence.da: Mange unge optager et **studielån** for at betale husleje.
sentence.en: Many young people take out a student loan to pay rent.

et studieår.explanation: "Et studieår" means "an academic year", the period from the start of classes in late summer to the exams in early summer. It is different from a calendar year, which starts in January.

sentence.da: Det første **studieår** er ofte det sværeste.
sentence.en: The first academic year is often the hardest.

et studium.explanation: "Et studium" means "a study program", the whole program that you take at a university, for example medicine or history. The form studiet (the study program) is the same as for et studie (a study), so the context tells which one is meant.

sentence.da: Hendes **studium** tager fem år og slutter med en kandidatgrad.
sentence.en: Her study program takes five years and ends with a master's degree.

et stykke.explanation: "Et stykke" means "a piece", as in et stykke kage (a piece of cake). In stores it also means "each": ti kroner stykket means "ten kroner each".

sentence.da: Må jeg få et **stykke** kage?
sentence.en: May I have a piece of cake?

et stød.explanation: "Et stød" means "a shock" or "a jolt", a sudden push or hit, such as from a bump in the road or from electricity. Danes also use it for a sudden emotional shock: Nyheden var et stød (The news was a shock).

sentence.da: Jeg fik et **stød**, da jeg rørte ved ledningen.
sentence.en: I got a shock when I touched the wire.

et støtteparti.explanation: "Et støtteparti" means "a supporting party", a party that is not part of the government but agrees to vote with it. Governments in Denmark often need one because they do not have enough seats on their own.

sentence.da: Regeringen har brug for et **støtteparti**, fordi den ikke har flertal.
sentence.en: The government needs a supporting party because it does not have a majority.

et sugerør.explanation: "Et sugerør" means "a drinking straw", the thin tube you drink through.

sentence.da: Hun drikker sin juice med **sugerør**.
sentence.en: She drinks her juice with a straw.

et suk.explanation: "Et suk" means "a sigh", a long breath out that shows tiredness, relief or sadness. It also exists as a verb, at sukke (to sigh).

sentence.da: Hun udstødte et **suk** af lettelse, da eksamen var slut.
sentence.en: She let out a sigh of relief when the exam was over.

et sundhedskort.explanation: "Et sundhedskort" means "a health insurance card", the card you show at the doctor or the hospital.

sentence.da: Du skal vise dit **sundhedskort** hos lægen.
sentence.en: You have to show your health insurance card at the doctor.

et supermarked.explanation: "Et supermarked" means "a supermarket". It is built from super (super) and marked (market). Marked also means a market or fair: et julemarked (a Christmas market).

sentence.da: Et **supermarked** sælger mad og mange andre ting.
sentence.en: A supermarket sells food and many other things.

et svar.explanation: "Et svar" means "an answer" or "a reply", what you give to a question or a message. Tak for svaret means "thanks for the reply".

sentence.da: Hun giver et **svar** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: She gives an answer to the question.

et svigt.explanation: "Et svigt" means "a betrayal" or "a letdown", when someone you trusted fails you or breaks a promise. It also appears in hjertesvigt (heart failure), where something stops working as it should.

sentence.da: Det var et stort **svigt**, at han ikke holdt sit løfte.
sentence.en: It was a big letdown that he did not keep his promise.

et svin.explanation: "Et svin" means "a pig". Calling a person et svin is rude: Han er et svin means "He is a swine". For the meat, Danes say svinekød (pork).

sentence.da: Bonden har mange **svin** på gården.
sentence.en: The farmer has many pigs on the farm.

et sving.explanation: "Et sving" means "a turn" or "a curve", for example in a road.

sentence.da: Pas på, der er et skarpt **sving** forude.
sentence.en: Be careful, there is a sharp curve ahead.

et sværd.explanation: "Et sværd" means "a sword", a long metal blade with a handle, used as a weapon in the past. Today you mostly see swords in museums, in films and in the sport of fencing.

sentence.da: Ridderen trak sit **sværd** og stillede sig foran slottet.
sentence.en: The knight drew his sword and stood in front of the castle.

et sygehus.explanation: "Et sygehus" means "a hospital". It is built from syg (sick) and hus (house). Et hospital (a hospital) means the same.

sentence.da: Lægen og sygeplejerskerne arbejder på et **sygehus**.
sentence.en: The doctor and the nurses work at a hospital.

et symbol.explanation: "Et symbol" means "a symbol", a sign that stands for an idea.

sentence.da: Hjertet er et **symbol** på kærlighed.
sentence.en: The heart is a symbol of love.

et symptom.explanation: "Et symptom" means "a symptom", a sign that you are ill, such as fever or a cough. It can also be a sign of a problem in general: Støjen er et symptom på noget større (The noise is a symptom of something bigger).

sentence.da: Feber er et almindeligt **symptom** på influenza.
sentence.en: A fever is a common symptom of the flu.

et syn.explanation: "Et syn" means "a sight" and also "vision", your ability to see: Det var et smukt syn (It was a beautiful sight). Hun har godt syn (She has good eyesight).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar har dårligt **syn** og bruger briller.
sentence.en: My grandfather has bad eyesight and wears glasses.

et synonym.explanation: "Et synonym" means "a synonym", a word that says the same, or almost the same, as another word. The opposite is et antonym (an antonym).

sentence.da: Et **synonym** for glad er lykkelig.
sentence.en: A synonym for happy is joyful.

et synspunkt.explanation: "Et synspunkt" means "a viewpoint", the way you see a question, based on your own experience or interests. It is close to et standpunkt (a position), but a standpunkt is one you have settled on, while a synspunkt is more a way of looking at things.

sentence.da: Det er et interessant **synspunkt**, men jeg er uenig.
sentence.en: That is an interesting viewpoint, but I disagree.

et system.explanation: "Et system" means "a system", a set of parts or rules that work together.

sentence.da: Et **system** hjælper os med at holde orden.
sentence.en: A system helps us keep things in order.

et sår.explanation: "Et sår" means "a wound" or "a sore", such as a cut or a scrape. Et sår i munden means "a sore in the mouth".

sentence.da: Jeg har et **sår** på mit knæ.
sentence.en: I have a wound on my knee.

et sæde.explanation: "Et sæde" means "a seat" in a car, plane or train. A chair is en stol, not et sæde.

sentence.da: Der er et ledigt **sæde** ved vinduet.
sentence.en: There is a free seat by the window.

et sølvbryllup.explanation: "Et sølvbryllup" means "a silver wedding anniversary", the celebration when a couple has been married for 25 years. Danes also celebrate et guldbryllup (a golden wedding) after 50 years.

sentence.da: Mine forældre holder **sølvbryllup**, fordi de har været gift i 25 år.
sentence.en: My parents are celebrating their silver wedding because they have been married for 25 years.

et søm.explanation: "Et søm" means "a nail", the thin metal pin you hit into wood. Do not mix it up with en skrue (a screw), which you turn in.

sentence.da: Jeg hænger billedet op med et **søm**.
sentence.en: I hang the picture up with a nail.

saft.explanation: "Saft" means "cordial" or "squash", a sweet fruit syrup that you mix with water. It is not the same as en juice (a juice): Jeg blander saft med koldt vand (I mix cordial with cold water).

sentence.da: **Saft** laves af frugt og er meget sød.
sentence.en: Cordial is made from fruit and is very sweet.

saftevand.explanation: "Saftevand" means "diluted cordial", fruit syrup mixed with water. It is built from saft (cordial) and vand (water): saft is the syrup before you add the water.

sentence.da: **Saftevand** er saft blandet med vand.
sentence.en: Diluted cordial is cordial mixed with water.

sagtens.explanation: "Sagtens" means "easily" or "surely", and shows that something is perfectly possible or no problem. Most often it goes with kan or kunne (can, could).

forms.da: Det kan sagtens lade sig gøre

sentence.da: Du kan **sagtens** nå toget, hvis du skynder dig.
sentence.en: You can easily catch the train if you hurry.

salt.explanation: "Salt" means "salt". You do not count it, so you say noget salt (some salt) rather than a salt. The same word also describes taste: det er for salt means "it is too salty".

sentence.da: Der er meget **salt** i havet.
sentence.en: There is a lot of salt in the sea.

saltet.explanation: "Saltet" means "salted" and comes from at salte (to salt). Do not mix it up with salt, the word for "salty", which describes a taste.

sentence.da: Fisken er **saltet** og smager af salt.
sentence.en: The fish is salted and tastes of salt.

samfundsfag.explanation: "Et samfundsfag" means "social studies", the school subject about how society works: politics, the economy and the rules we live by. It is built from et samfund (a society) and et fag (a subject).

sentence.da: I **samfundsfag** lærer vi, hvordan et valg fungerer.
sentence.en: In social studies we learn how an election works.

samme.explanation: "Samme" means "same". It usually follows den, det or de (all three mean "the"), but it can also stand alone, as in samme dag (the same day). Det samme! is also a reply meaning "the same to you": God weekend! - Det samme! (Have a good weekend! - You too!)

sentence.da: Vi har den **samme** bil.
sentence.en: We have the same car.

sammen.explanation: "Sammen" means "together". Compare Vi spiser sammen (We eat together) with Jeg spiser alene (I eat alone). Alle sammen means "everyone together", as in Hej alle sammen! (Hello everyone!).

sentence.da: Min ven og jeg bor **sammen**.
sentence.en: My friend and I live together.

sammenhold.explanation: "Et sammenhold" means "togetherness", the feeling that a group sticks together and helps each other, in a team, a family or a village. It comes from at holde sammen (to stick together).

sentence.da: I vores klasse er der et stærkt **sammenhold**, og alle hjælper hinanden.
sentence.en: In our class there is strong togetherness, and everyone helps each other.

sammenhængende.explanation: "Sammenhængende" means "coherent": the parts fit together into one whole, or form one continuous piece. It is used for a text, a story or an area, and it comes from at hænge sammen (to hang together). The opposite is usammenhængende (disconnected).

sentence.da: Hendes fortælling var **sammenhængende**, så alle kunne følge med.
sentence.en: Her story was coherent, so everyone could follow.

sammenhængskraft.explanation: "En sammenhængskraft" means "social cohesion": the glue that makes people in a country feel connected and willing to help each other. It is built from sammenhæng (connection) and kraft (strength). You mostly hear it in political talk.

sentence.da: Fælles regler og værdier styrker samfundets **sammenhængskraft**.
sentence.en: Shared rules and values strengthen society's social cohesion.

sammenlignelig.explanation: "Sammenlignelig" means "comparable", close enough in kind that you can put two things side by side and judge them fairly. It is usually followed by med (with): Hans løn er sammenlignelig med min (His pay is comparable to mine).

sentence.da: Prisen er **sammenlignelig** med prisen i de andre butikker.
sentence.en: The price is comparable to the price in the other stores.

sammensat.explanation: "Sammensat" means "composite", made up of several parts put together. It is also used for a problem or reason with many parts, which is why it can mean "complex". It is not the same as kompliceret (complicated): sammensat only says there are several parts, while kompliceret says it is hard.

sentence.da: Håndklæde er et **sammensat** ord af hånd og klæde.
sentence.en: Håndklæde (towel) is a compound word made of hand and cloth.

samt.explanation: "Samt" means "as well as", and joins the last item to a list. It is mostly written, as on menus and forms: Kaffe, te samt kage (Coffee, tea and cake). In speech, Danes use og (and).

sentence.da: Husk at tage pas **samt** billet med til lufthavnen.
sentence.en: Remember to take your passport as well as your ticket to the airport.

samtidig.explanation: "Samtidig" means "simultaneously", or "at the same time": Vi gik samtidig (We left at the same time). Add med to say with what: samtidig med mødet (at the same time as the meeting).

forms.en: They arrived at the same time.
She laughed and cried at the same time.
At the same time, it is cheap.

sentence.da: Han taler og spiser **samtidig**.
sentence.en: He talks and eats at the same time.

samtlige.explanation: "Samtlige" means "all", and stresses that none are left out. It is stronger than alle (all) and is typical of writing and announcements: samtlige elever (every single student).

sentence.da: **Samtlige** elever skal aflevere opgaven inden fredag.
sentence.en: All the students must hand in the assignment before Friday.

sand.explanation: "Sand" means "sand". Do not mix it up with sand meaning "true", as in Det er sandt (That is true).

sentence.da: På stranden er der meget **sand**.
sentence.en: There is a lot of sand on the beach.

sandaler.explanation: "Sandaler" means "sandals", open shoes with straps that you wear in warm weather. One sandal is en sandal, but shoes come in pairs, so you mostly hear sandaler.

sentence.da: Om sommeren går jeg i **sandaler**.
sentence.en: In summer I wear sandals.

sandelig.explanation: "Sandelig" means "indeed" or "truly": it adds strong emphasis, often with surprise or irritation: Det var sandelig noget rod! (That was truly a mess!) It sounds a bit old-fashioned, and in everyday talk people usually say virkelig (really).

forms.da: Det er jeg sandelig ikke enig i.
forms.en: I truly do not agree with that.

sentence.da: Det var **sandelig** en lang dag, men vi klarede den.
sentence.en: It was indeed a long day, but we made it.

sandsynlig.explanation: "Sandsynlig" means "likely" or "probable" and says that something will probably happen: Det er sandsynligt, at han kommer (It is likely that he is coming).

sentence.da: Regn er **sandsynlig**, fordi himlen er mørk.
sentence.en: Rain is likely because the sky is dark.

sandsynligvis.explanation: "Sandsynligvis" means "probably" and is built from sandsynlig (likely): Hun kommer sandsynligvis for sent (She is probably coming too late). It is more sure than muligvis (possibly).

sentence.da: Det bliver **sandsynligvis** koldt i morgen.
sentence.en: It will probably be cold tomorrow.

sankthans.explanation: "Sankthans" means "Midsummer", the evening of 23 June, when Danes light bonfires near the sea and lakes and sing together. It is named after St. John (Sankt Hans), whose day is 24 June.

sentence.da: Til **sankthans** tænder vi et stort bål ved stranden.
sentence.en: At Midsummer we light a big fire on the beach.

sarkastisk.explanation: "Sarkastisk" means "sarcastic", saying the opposite of what you mean to make fun of something or hurt someone. For example, Dejligt, det regner igen! (Lovely, it is raining again!) said in a flat voice.

sentence.da: Han svarede **sarkastisk**, at det var en fantastisk idé.
sentence.en: He answered sarcastically that it was a fantastic idea.

sej.explanation: "Sej" means "tough" or "cool". For a person, it is a compliment: Hun er sej (She is cool). For food, it means chewy or tough: sejt kød (tough meat).

sentence.da: Han er **sej** og giver aldrig op.
sentence.en: He is tough and never gives up.

sejlads.explanation: "En sejlads" means "a sailing trip", a journey or outing on the water by boat. Its verb at sejle (to sail) is used for any trip by ship or boat, including a ferry, not only a boat with a sail.

sentence.da: På en lang **sejlads** over havet kan man ikke se land.
sentence.en: On a long sailing trip across the sea you cannot see land.

sentence.da: To gange tre er **seks**.
sentence.en: Two times three is six.

seksten.explanation: "Seksten" means "sixteen". Do not mix it up with seks (six): seks børn (six children), seksten børn (sixteen children).

sentence.da: Ti plus seks er **seksten**.
sentence.en: Ten plus six is sixteen.

seksuel.explanation: "Seksuel" means "sexual", the neutral word used in health, law and school texts for anything to do with sex. It does not mean "sexy": that is the word sexet.

sentence.da: Skolen har undervisning om **seksuel** sundhed og beskyttelse.
sentence.en: The school has teaching about sexual health and protection.

selleri.explanation: "Selleri" means "celery". Stangselleri (celery stalks) is the green stalk, and knoldselleri (celeriac) is the round root.

sentence.da: Jeg skærer **selleri** og gulerod til suppen.
sentence.en: I cut celery and carrot for the soup.

selv.explanation: "Selv" means "myself", yourself, herself and so on, with nobody helping: Jeg gør det selv (I do it myself). At the start of a sentence it means "even": Selv børn kan det (Even children can do it).

sentence.da: Jeg laver maden **selv**.
sentence.en: I make the food myself.

selv tak.explanation: "Selv tak" means "you're welcome". It literally means "thanks yourself", which is why it also returns thanks: Tak for i aftes. Selv tak. (Thanks for last night. Thanks to you too.)

forms.en: Thanks for the help. - You're welcome.

forms.da: Tak for i aftes. - Selv tak.
forms.en: Thanks for last night. - Thanks to you too.

sentence.da: "Tak for hjælpen!" - "**Selv tak**!"
sentence.en: "Thanks for the help!" - "You're welcome!"

selvforsvar.explanation: "Et selvforsvar" means "self-defense", protecting yourself when you are attacked, and also the classes that teach it. In law, the word is nødværge (legal self-defense).

sentence.da: I **selvforsvar** lærer man at slippe fri, hvis nogen griber fat i en.
sentence.en: In self-defense you learn to get free if someone grabs hold of you.

selvfølgelig.explanation: "Selvfølgelig" means "of course". It can also sit inside a sentence to say that something is no surprise: Hun kommer selvfølgelig for sent (Of course she is going to be late).

sentence.da: "Må jeg låne din bog?" - "**Selvfølgelig**!"
sentence.en: "May I borrow your book?" - "Of course!"

selvglad.explanation: "Selvglad" means "smug" or "conceited", pleased with yourself in a way that annoys others. It is literally "happy with oneself", but always negative. To say you are happy with your own effort, use tilfreds (satisfied).

sentence.da: Han er så **selvglad**, at han aldrig lytter til andre.
sentence.en: He is so smug that he never listens to others.

selvmodsigende.explanation: "Selvmodsigende" means "contradictory": it says one thing and the opposite at the same time. It is built from selv (self) and at modsige (to contradict), so it contradicts itself.

sentence.da: Reglen er **selvmodsigende**, fordi den både tillader og forbyder det.
sentence.en: The rule is contradictory, because it both allows and forbids it.
