selvom.explanation: "Selvom" means "even though" and introduces something you would not expect: Jeg går en tur, selvom det regner (I am going for a walk even though it is raining). After it comes a full sentence, unlike på trods af (despite), which is followed by a thing: på trods af regnen (despite the rain).

forms.en: even though he does not know

sentence.da: Jeg løber, **selvom** jeg er meget træt.
sentence.en: I am running even though I am very tired.

selvsikker.explanation: "Selvsikker" means "confident" and describes someone who believes in themselves. It is built from selv (self) and sikker (sure). Selv also starts other words, such as selvstændig (independent).

sentence.da: Hun er **selvsikker** og taler højt foran alle.
sentence.en: She is confident and speaks loudly in front of everyone.

selvstændig.explanation: "Selvstændig" means "independent" and "self-employed". For a person, it means able to decide and manage without help. About work, it means running your own business: Min søster er selvstændig (My sister is self-employed).

sentence.da: Hun vil være **selvstændig** og åbne sin egen frisørsalon.
sentence.en: She wants to be self-employed and open her own hair salon.

selvstændighed.explanation: "Selvstændighed" means "independence", being able to decide and manage things on your own. It fits a person who manages alone and a country that rules itself.

sentence.da: Mange unge flytter hjemmefra for at få **selvstændighed**.
sentence.en: Many young people move out to gain independence.

selvtillid.explanation: "Selvtillid" means "self-confidence", the belief that you can do things well.

sentence.da: Hun har stor **selvtillid** og er aldrig bange.
sentence.en: She has great self-confidence and is never afraid.

senere.explanation: "Senere" means "later", as in senere i dag (later today). Do not mix it up with sent, which means "late": Det er sent (It is late).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig **senere**.
sentence.en: I will call you later.

seneste.explanation: "Seneste" means "latest" or "most recent": Har du set hans seneste film? (Have you seen his latest movie?) It also works for a stretch of time: de seneste uger (the last few weeks). For the final one, use sidste (last).

sentence.da: Har du hørt den **seneste** nyhed?
sentence.en: Have you heard the latest news?

sengetid.explanation: "Sengetid" means "bedtime", the time to go to sleep. It is built from seng (bed) and tid (time). Tid also ends other words for set times, such as spisetid (mealtime).

sentence.da: Nu er det **sengetid**, og børnene er trætte.
sentence.en: Now it is bedtime, and the kids are tired.

sennep.explanation: "Sennep" means "mustard". You do not count it, so you say noget sennep (some mustard).

sentence.da: Pølsen smager godt med ketchup og **sennep**.
sentence.en: The sausage tastes good with ketchup and mustard.

sensitiv.explanation: "Sensitiv" means "sensitive", easily affected by touch, substances or feelings. For a person who feels things strongly, Danes more often say følsom (sensitive): Han er meget følsom (He is very sensitive).

sentence.da: Hun bruger en mild creme, fordi hendes hud er **sensitiv**.
sentence.en: She uses a mild cream because her skin is sensitive.

sent.explanation: "Sent" means "late", as in not early. Do not mix it up with senere, which means "later". To say you are running late, say Jeg kommer for sent (I am coming too late) or Jeg er forsinket (I am delayed).

sentence.da: Vi kommer **sent** hjem i dag.
sentence.en: We come home late today.

september.explanation: "September" means "September", the ninth month. Month names are not capitalized in Danish, unlike in English: Vi rejser i september (We travel in September).

sentence.da: Børnene starter i skole igen i **september**.
sentence.en: The children start school again in September.

seriøs.explanation: "Seriøs" means "serious" and describes someone who is earnest or a thing that is meant for real. Ask Er du seriøs? (Are you serious?) to check that someone means it.

sentence.da: Han er meget **seriøs** og laver aldrig sjov.
sentence.en: He is very serious and never jokes.

ses i morgen.explanation: "Ses i morgen" means "see you tomorrow". Swap i morgen for another time: ses i aften (see you tonight).

forms.en: Will we see each other tomorrow?

sentence.da: Jeg skal hjem nu. **Ses i morgen**!
sentence.en: I am going home now. See you tomorrow!

sexet.explanation: "Sexet" means "sexy", for someone or something that draws the eye. In casual talk it can also mean "cool and appealing": Det er et sexet design (That is a sexy design).

sentence.da: Hun har en **sexet** kjole på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a sexy dress.

shampoo.explanation: "Shampoo" means "shampoo" and is spelled the same as in English. You do not count it, so you say noget shampoo (some shampoo).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mit hår med **shampoo**.
sentence.en: I wash my hair with shampoo.

shorts.explanation: "Shorts" means "shorts". It is always used for more than one: Mine shorts er nye (My shorts are new).

sentence.da: Jeg har **shorts** og T-shirt på.
sentence.en: I am wearing shorts and a T-shirt.

siddende.explanation: "Siddende" means "sitting" or "seated" and describes someone who is in a sitting position. To say what someone is doing right now, use at sidde (to sit): Han sidder (He is sitting).

sentence.da: Den **siddende** mand ved vinduet læste en bog.
sentence.en: The seated man by the window was reading a book.

siden.explanation: "Siden" means "since" and also "ago". Since: siden i går (since yesterday). Ago: for to år siden (two years ago), where siden comes last.

sentence.da: Jeg har boet her **siden** 2020.
sentence.en: I have lived here since 2020.

sidenhen.explanation: "Sidenhen" means "since then" or "later on", and it looks back from a moment in the past to what came afterwards. It usually starts from a moment you have already mentioned.

forms.en: and later on he became a doctor

sentence.da: Vi mødtes i 2010, og **sidenhen** har vi været venner.
sentence.en: We met in 2010, and since then we have been friends.

sidst.explanation: "Sidst" means "last" in the sense of coming after everyone else or at the end. Before a thing, use sidste, as in sidste gang (the last time).

sentence.da: Han kom **sidst** til festen.
sentence.en: He came last to the party.

sidste.explanation: "Sidste" means "last" before a thing: den sidste bus (the last bus), sidste uge (last week), sidste år (last year). Compare Jeg kom sidst (I came last), where sidst stands alone with nothing after it.

sentence.da: Det er den **sidste** bus i dag.
sentence.en: It is the last bus today.

sig.explanation: "Sig" means "himself", "herself", "itself" or "themselves". Compare Han vasker ham (He washes him, someone else) with Han vasker sig (He washes himself). Some verbs always take sig: at skynde sig (to hurry), at glæde sig (to look forward to).

forms.en: She is looking forward to it.

sentence.da: Han vasker **sig** hver morgen.
sentence.en: He washes himself every morning.

sikke.explanation: "Sikke" means "what a ..." and starts an exclamation. It is followed by en or et to match the word: Sikke en overraskelse! (What a surprise!) and Sikke et vejr! (What weather!).

sentence.da: Åh, **sikke** en flot hund du har!
sentence.en: Oh, what a nice dog you have!

sikke en dag.explanation: "Sikke en dag" means "what a day" and reacts to a day that was great, hard or surprising. Sikke en goes with en-words. With et-words, use sikke et: Sikke et vejr! (What weather!).

forms.da: Sikke en dag, alt gik galt!
forms.en: What a day, everything went wrong!

sentence.da: **Sikke en dag**, vi vandt hele turneringen!
sentence.en: What a day, we won the whole tournament!

sikke noget.explanation: "Sikke noget" means "what a thing" or "wow", said when something surprises you: Sikke noget vejr! (What weather!). It can show amazement or annoyance, and the tone of voice tells which: a happy one is delight, a sighing one is a complaint.

sentence.da: **Sikke noget** rod, der er mel overalt!
sentence.en: What a mess, there is flour everywhere!

sikker.explanation: "Sikker" means "sure" and "safe". It says that someone has no doubt, or that something cannot hurt you. Er du sikker? (Are you sure?) is the usual way to check a fact.

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **sikker** på det.
sentence.en: I am completely sure about it.

sikkerhed.explanation: "Sikkerhed" means "security" and "safety", being protected from harm. It can also mean "being sure": Jeg ved det med sikkerhed (I know it for sure).

sentence.da: Bilbælter giver **sikkerhed** i trafikken.
sentence.en: Seat belts give safety in traffic.

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi **sild** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat herring on rye bread.

silke.explanation: "Silke" means "silk", a soft, shiny, light cloth used for scarves, ties and fine clothes. It is the material itself, so it takes no en or et: Jeg elsker silke (I love silk).

sentence.da: Hendes kjole er lavet af **silke**.
sentence.en: Her dress is made of silk.

simpel.explanation: "Simpel" means "simple", easy to understand or do. It can also mean plain, with nothing extra: et simpelt hus (a plain house).

sentence.da: Det er en **simpel** opgave, og børn kan klare den.
sentence.en: It is a simple task, and children can handle it.

simpelthen.explanation: "Simpelthen" means "simply" and adds force to what you feel: Jeg kan simpelthen ikke mere (I simply can't take any more).

forms.en: I simply do not understand it

sentence.da: Det er **simpelthen** den bedste kage.
sentence.en: It is simply the best cake.

sin.explanation: "Sin" means "his own", "her own" or "its own" before an en-word. Compare Peter ser sin bror (Peter sees his own brother) with Peter ser Jens og hans bror (Peter sees Jens and Jens's brother). For "I" and "you" use min (my) and din (your): Jeg ser min bror (I see my brother).

sentence.da: Hun elsker **sin** hund.
sentence.en: She loves her (own) dog.

sindssyg.explanation: "Sindssyg" means "insane", and in casual talk it can also mean "wild" or "extreme": Det er sindssygt godt (It is insanely good). It is stronger than gal (crazy).

sentence.da: Det er en **sindssyg** idé, og den er farlig.
sentence.en: That is an insane idea, and it is dangerous.

sine.explanation: "Sine" means "his own" or "her own" for more than one thing. Compare Peter ser sine venner (Peter sees his own friends) with Peter ser Jens og hans venner (Peter sees Jens and Jens's friends). For one thing, use sin (en-word) or sit (et-word): sin bror (his own brother).

sentence.da: Hun ringer til **sine** forældre.
sentence.en: She calls her (own) parents.

single.explanation: "Single" means "single" in the sense of not being in a relationship. For just one, use enkelt: en enkelt dag (a single day).

sentence.da: Jeg er **single** og har tid til venner.
sentence.en: I am single and have time for friends.

sirup.explanation: "En sirup" means "a syrup", a thick, sweet liquid made from sugar and water, used for example in baking. Danes use saft (fruit cordial) for the fruity drink you mix with water, which is a different thing.

sentence.da: **Sirup** er tyk og sød, og den passer til pandekager.
sentence.en: Syrup is thick and sweet, and it goes well with pancakes.

sit.explanation: "Sit" means "his own", "her own" or "its own" before an et-word. Compare Peter elsker sit hus (Peter loves his own house) with Peter ser Jens og hans hus (Peter sees Jens and Jens's house). For an en-word, use sin: sin bil (his own car).

sentence.da: Han passer på **sit** barn.
sentence.en: He looks after his (own) child.

sjette.explanation: "Sjette" means "sixth". It is used for dates too: den sjette maj (the sixth of May). It is not spelled sekste, even though seks (six) is the number it comes from.

sentence.da: Efter femte sal kommer **sjette** sal.
sentence.en: After the fifth floor comes the sixth floor.

sjov.explanation: "Sjov" means "fun" and also "funny": a party and a joke can both be sjov. Det var sjovt means "That was fun", and for sjov means "for fun" or "as a joke".

sentence.da: Klovnen er **sjov** og alle ler.
sentence.en: The clown is funny and everyone laughs.

sjusket.explanation: "Sjusket" means "sloppy": done too fast and without attention, so it has mistakes or looks untidy. It describes the result, such as a badly painted wall, and can also be used for untidy clothes.

sentence.da: Rapporten er **sjusket**, og der er mange stavefejl i den.
sentence.en: The report is sloppy, and there are many spelling mistakes in it.

sjælden.explanation: "Sjælden" means "rare", for things that are hard to find. Sjældent means "rarely": Jeg ser ham sjældent (I rarely see him).

sentence.da: Det er en **sjælden** fugl i Danmark.
sentence.en: It is a rare bird in Denmark.

sjældent.explanation: "Sjældent" means "rarely": Han kommer sjældent for sent (He is rarely late). For something hard to find, use sjælden: en sjælden bog (a rare book).

sentence.da: Jeg ser **sjældent** min bror, fordi han bor langt væk.
sentence.en: I rarely see my brother because he lives far away.

skadelig.explanation: "Skadelig" means "harmful", describing something that can hurt your health or damage things. The word for the harm itself is en skade (an injury, damage).

sentence.da: Rygning er **skadelig** for både lungerne og hjertet.
sentence.en: Smoking is harmful to both the lungs and the heart.

skak.explanation: "Skak" means "chess" and is used without en or et: Han er god til skak (He is good at chess). In the game, Skak! (Check!) means the king is under attack, and skak mat (checkmate) ends the game.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar spiller **skak** hver søndag.
sentence.en: My grandfather plays chess every Sunday.

skal vi ikke bare...?.explanation: "Skal vi ikke bare...?" means "shall we just...?" and suggests the simple choice. The dots stand for the action you suggest. Although it contains ikke (not), it is a gentle suggestion, not a refusal: Skal vi ikke bare tage hjem? (Shall we just go home?)

forms.da: Skal vi ikke bare bestille pizza?

sentence.da: **Skal vi ikke bare** tage bussen i dag?
sentence.en: Shall we just take the bus today?

skaldet.explanation: "Skaldet" means "bald", with a bare head, either completely or in part. To say it is happening now, use ved at blive: Han er ved at blive skaldet (He is going bald).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er **skaldet**, men han har et pænt skæg.
sentence.en: My grandfather is bald, but he has a nice beard.

skaldyr.explanation: "Skaldyr" means "shellfish". It is built from en skal (a shell) and et dyr (an animal), and it is one word for crabs, lobsters, mussels and more.

forms.en: Is there shellfish in the dish?

sentence.da: Krabber og hummere er **skaldyr**.
sentence.en: Crabs and lobsters are shellfish.

skam.explanation: "Skam" means "shame", the uncomfortable feeling after something embarrassing: Der er ingen skam i at spørge (There is no shame in asking). Det er en skam (That is a pity) uses it for something sad.

sentence.da: Hun følte **skam**, fordi alle grinede af hende.
sentence.en: She felt shame because everyone laughed at her.

skamfuld.explanation: "Skamfuld" means "ashamed", the heavy feeling after you did something wrong or embarrassing. It is not the same as being shy: shyness is about meeting people, while this is about something you did.

sentence.da: Han følte sig **skamfuld**, fordi han havde løjet for sin mor.
sentence.en: He felt ashamed because he had lied to his mother.

skandinavien.explanation: "Skandinavien" means "Scandinavia". Place names start with a capital letter in Danish, but skandinavisk (Scandinavian) does not. To include Finland and Iceland too, Danes say Norden (the Nordic countries).

sentence.da: Danmark ligger i **Skandinavien**.
sentence.en: Denmark is in Scandinavia.

skarp.explanation: "Skarp" means "sharp" and is used for knives and edges. It also describes a quick mind: Hun er meget skarp (She is very sharp).

sentence.da: Saksen er **skarp** og klipper papiret let.
sentence.en: The scissors are sharp and cut the paper easily.

skarpt.explanation: "Skarpt" means "sharply" and says how something is done: clearly and strictly, or with an edge, like a voice that cuts or a sudden turn. To say a thing itself is sharp, use skarp (sharp): en skarp kniv (a sharp knife).

forms.en: to turn sharply to the right

sentence.da: Læreren talte **skarpt** til drengen, fordi han larmede.
sentence.en: The teacher spoke sharply to the boy because he was noisy.

skeptisk.explanation: "Skeptisk" means "skeptical", not ready to believe something or trust it until you see proof. It is often followed by over for (about): Jeg er skeptisk over for planen (I am skeptical about the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg er **skeptisk**, fordi tilbuddet virker for godt til at være sandt.
sentence.en: I am skeptical because the offer seems too good to be true.

skidt.explanation: "Skidt" means "bad" in casual phrases: Det gik ikke så skidt (It did not go so badly). It also means "dirt".

forms.en: There is dirt on the floor.

sentence.da: Maden var ikke **skidt**, men den var kold.
sentence.en: The food was not bad, but it was cold.

skiløb.explanation: "Skiløb" means "skiing", the sport. It is built from en ski (a ski) and et løb (a run). You can also say at stå på ski (to ski, literally to stand on skis).

sentence.da: Han elsker **skiløb** og tager til Norge hver vinter.
sentence.en: He loves skiing and goes to Norway every winter.

skinnende.explanation: "Skinnende" means "shiny", giving back light from a smooth, clean surface, like en skinnende ring (a shiny ring). To say the sun is out, use at skinne (to shine): Solen skinner (The sun is shining).

sentence.da: Efter rengøring er gulvet rent og **skinnende**.
sentence.en: After cleaning, the floor is clean and shiny.

sko.explanation: "Sko" means "shoes". It looks the same for one shoe and many: en sko (one shoe), mine sko (my shoes). Danish often says the where English says my: Jeg tager skoene på (I put my shoes on).

sentence.da: Vi har **sko** på fødderne.
sentence.en: We have shoes on our feet.

skrald.explanation: "Skrald" means "garbage", the things you throw away: Jeg tager skraldet ud (I take out the garbage). The container for it is en skraldespand (a garbage can).

sentence.da: Der ligger **skrald** på gaden.
sentence.en: There is garbage lying in the street.

skriftlig.explanation: "Skriftlig" means "written", for things done in writing rather than out loud. The opposite is mundtlig (oral): en mundtlig prøve (an oral test).

sentence.da: Der er både en mundtlig og en **skriftlig** prøve.
sentence.en: There is both an oral and a written test.

skråt.explanation: "Skråt" means "diagonally" or "at an angle", neither upright nor flat. In directions, skråt over for means "diagonally across from": Caféen ligger skråt over for stationen (The cafe is diagonally across from the station).

sentence.da: Solen skinner **skråt** ind ad vinduet om morgenen.
sentence.en: The sun shines in at an angle through the window in the morning.

skræk.explanation: "Skræk" means "fright" or "terror", a sudden strong fear: Hun skreg af skræk (She screamed in terror). It is a sudden shock, not a lasting worry like bekymring (worry).

sentence.da: Han fik en **skræk**, da lyset gik ud.
sentence.en: He got a fright when the light went out.

skræmmende.explanation: "Skræmmende" means "frightening" and describes the thing that scares you. To say how you feel, use bange (scared): Jeg er bange (I am scared).

sentence.da: Mørket kan være **skræmmende** for børn.
sentence.en: The dark can be frightening for children.

skræmt.explanation: "Skræmt" means "scared", frightened by something that happened. To say you fear something in general, use bange: Jeg er bange for edderkopper (I am afraid of spiders).

sentence.da: Barnet så **skræmt** ud efter tordenen.
sentence.en: The child looked scared after the thunder.

skrøbelig.explanation: "Skrøbelig" means "fragile": easily broken. It is also used for poor health, especially in old people, and for things that can fall apart easily: en skrøbelig fred (a fragile peace).

sentence.da: Pas på, vasen er meget **skrøbelig**.
sentence.en: Careful, the vase is very fragile.

skuffende.explanation: "Skuffende" means "disappointing", describing a thing that turned out worse than you hoped. To say how a person feels, use skuffet (disappointed): Jeg er skuffet (I am disappointed).

sentence.da: Vi trænede hårdt, men resultatet var **skuffende**.
sentence.en: We trained hard, but the result was disappointing.

skuffet.explanation: "Skuffet" means "disappointed". Use over (about) for the cause: Jeg er skuffet over resultatet (I am disappointed with the result). Han så skuffet ud (He looked disappointed).

sentence.da: Hun var **skuffet** over sin karakter.
sentence.en: She was disappointed with her grade.

skummetmælk.explanation: "Skummetmælk" means "skim milk". It is skummet (skimmed) and mælk (milk) joined together: milk with the cream taken off.

sentence.da: **Skummetmælk** har næsten intet fedt.
sentence.en: Skim milk has almost no fat.

sky.explanation: "Sky" means "shy", nervous or quiet around people you do not know well. Watch the look-alike en sky (a cloud), spelled the same: Hun er sky (She is shy), but Der er en sky på himlen (There is a cloud in the sky).

forms.en: He was shy as a child

sentence.da: Han er **sky** og siger næsten ikke noget til fremmede.
sentence.en: He is shy and hardly says anything to strangers.

skyet.explanation: "Skyet" means "cloudy". It comes from en sky (a cloud). In weather forecasts, you also hear overskyet (overcast), when clouds cover the whole sky.

sentence.da: Himlen er grå og **skyet** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is gray and cloudy today.

skyld.explanation: "Skyld" means "guilt" or "fault": Det er ikke din skyld (It is not your fault). To ask who is to blame, say Hvem har skylden? (Who is to blame?).

sentence.da: Jeg følte **skyld**, fordi jeg glemte hendes fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I felt guilt because I forgot her birthday.

skyldfølelse.explanation: "En skyldfølelse" means "a feeling of guilt", the uneasy feeling that you did something wrong or failed to do something you should have. In everyday talk, Danes often say Jeg har dårlig samvittighed (I feel bad about it), literally "I have a bad conscience".

sentence.da: Hun fik en **skyldfølelse**, fordi hun glemte sin mors fødselsdag.
sentence.en: She felt a sense of guilt because she forgot her mother's birthday.

skyldig.explanation: "Skyldig" means "guilty" and also "owing": Jeg er dig 50 kroner skyldig (I owe you 50 kroner).

sentence.da: Retten finder ham **skyldig**.
sentence.en: The court finds him guilty.

skynd dig.explanation: "Skynd dig" means "hurry up" and is said to one person. To several people, say skynd jer. The little words dig and jer mean yourself (one person) and yourselves (several people).

forms.da: Skynd dig, vi er sent på den.

sentence.da: **Skynd dig**, toget går nu!
sentence.en: Hurry up, the train is leaving now!

skyr.explanation: "En skyr" means "skyr", a thick, tart dairy food that people eat plain or with fruit or oats, much like yogurt.

sentence.da: **Skyr** er tyk, syrlig og kommer oprindeligt fra Island.
sentence.en: Skyr is thick, tart and originally comes from Iceland.

skål.explanation: "Skål" means "cheers". Add for and a name or dig (you) to toast someone: Skål for dig! (Cheers to you!). It is the same word as en skål (a bowl).

sentence.da: Vi løfter glassene og siger **skål**!
sentence.en: We raise the glasses and say cheers!

skærtorsdag.explanation: "Skærtorsdag" means "Maundy Thursday", the Thursday just before langfredag (Good Friday). It is a public holiday in Denmark.

sentence.da: Mange danskere holder fri på **skærtorsdag** og tager på ferie.
sentence.en: Many Danes take the day off on Maundy Thursday and go on vacation.

skæv.explanation: "Skæv" means "crooked", not straight or level: et skævt billede (a crooked picture). It also describes something odd or quirky, as in en skæv humor (a quirky sense of humor).

sentence.da: Stolen er **skæv**, fordi det ene ben er for kort.
sentence.en: The chair is crooked because one leg is too short.

skødesløs.explanation: "Skødesløs" means "careless", not paying attention to what you do or to your things, often because you do not care enough. It is said about a person or about a mistake.

sentence.da: Han var **skødesløs** og glemte at låse døren.
sentence.en: He was careless and forgot to lock the door.

skøjteløb.explanation: "Skøjteløb" means "ice skating". It is built from en skøjte (an ice skate) and et løb (a run). The verb is at løbe på skøjter (to ice skate, literally to run on skates).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker **skøjteløb** om vinteren.
sentence.en: The children love ice skating in the winter.

skønt.explanation: "Skønt" means "although" and joins two parts of a sentence: Jeg gik, skønt det regnede (I went although it rained). It sounds more like writing than selvom (even though), which people use in everyday speech. Do not mix it up with skønt meaning "lovely": Det er skønt! (That is lovely!)

sentence.da: Hun blev hjemme, **skønt** hun gerne ville med.
sentence.en: She stayed home although she really wanted to go along.

skør.explanation: "Skør" means "crazy" in a mild, playful way. For food it means "crisp": Kiksene er skøre (The crackers are crisp).

sentence.da: Min onkel er lidt **skør**, men han er sjov.
sentence.en: My uncle is a bit crazy, but he is funny.

sladder.explanation: "Sladder" means "gossip": talk about other people's private lives, often unkind or untrue. It is the talk itself, not the person. Someone who tells on others is en sladrehank (tattletale).

sentence.da: Det er bare **sladder**, og det er ikke sandt.
sentence.en: It is just gossip, and it is not true.

sladrevorn.explanation: "Sladrevorn" means "gossipy": always ready to tell others what you know about people. It is built on the idea of at sladre (to gossip) and is said about a person or a small community.

sentence.da: Min nabo er **sladrevorn** og ved alt om alle i gaden.
sentence.en: My neighbor is gossipy and knows everything about everyone on the street.

slank.explanation: "Slank" means "slim", with a light, well-shaped build: en slank figur (a slim figure). It also works for things, like en slank mobil (a slim phone).

sentence.da: Hun er høj og **slank**, og hun løber hver morgen.
sentence.en: She is tall and slim, and she runs every morning.

slet ikke.explanation: "Slet ikke" means "not at all" and makes a no stronger: Jeg er slet ikke træt (I am not tired at all). Compare Jeg er ikke træt (I am not tired).

forms.en: It is not expensive at all.
I do not understand at all.

sentence.da: Jeg er **slet ikke** sulten i dag.
sentence.en: I am not hungry at all today.

slidt.explanation: "Slidt" means "worn": old and used up from much use, as in en slidt sofa (a worn sofa). It is also used about people: Jeg er helt slidt means "I am completely worn out".

sentence.da: Dækket er **slidt**, så vi skal have et nyt.
sentence.en: The tire is worn, so we need a new one.

slik.explanation: "Slik" means "candy" (sweets). You do not count it and normally use it without en or et: Jeg spiser for meget slik (I eat too much candy).

sentence.da: Børn elsker **slik** og kage.
sentence.en: Children love candy and cake.

slud.explanation: "Slud" means "sleet", a wet, heavy mix of rain and snow that falls when the air is near freezing. It differs from hagl (hail), which comes as hard little pellets.

sentence.da: I dag falder der **slud**, og alle har våde sko.
sentence.en: Today sleet is falling and everyone has wet shoes.

slut.explanation: "Slut" means "over" or "finished", used after er (is). It also means something has run out: Mælken er slut (The milk has run out).

sentence.da: Skoledagen er **slut** nu.
sentence.en: The school day is over now.

sløret.explanation: "Sløret" means "blurred": not sharp or clear, like a photo, or eyes after crying or too little sleep. It can also mean "veiled", unclear on purpose, though tilsløret (concealed) is the usual word for that.

sentence.da: Billedet er **sløret**, fordi kameraet rystede.
sentence.en: The picture is blurred because the camera shook.

smagløs.explanation: "Smagløs" means "tasteless" in two ways: food with no flavor, and behavior or jokes in bad taste. It is built from smag (taste) and -løs (without).

sentence.da: Suppen var **smagløs** uden salt og peber.
sentence.en: The soup was tasteless without salt and pepper.

smal.explanation: "Smal" means "narrow", for streets, paths, doors and windows. It is about width, not about being thin like paper; for that use tynd (thin).

sentence.da: Den lille gade er meget **smal**.
sentence.en: The little street is very narrow.

smart.explanation: "Smart" means "smart" in the sense of clever or handy, and also "stylish". For an intelligent person, klog (smart) fits better: Hun er klog (She is smart).

sentence.da: Det er en **smart** måde at spare tid på.
sentence.en: It is a clever way to save time.

smertefuld.explanation: "Smertefuld" means "painful", causing pain, either in the body or in your feelings. For a body part that hurts right now, Danes use at gøre ondt (to hurt): Det gør ondt (It hurts).

sentence.da: Det var en **smertefuld** operation, men han blev rask.
sentence.en: It was a painful operation, but he got well.

smertelig.explanation: "Smertelig" means "painful" for things that hurt in your feelings, like a loss, a memory or a hard fact. For the body, the more common word is smertefuld (painful).

sentence.da: Tabet af hendes bror var en **smertelig** oplevelse.
sentence.en: The loss of her brother was a painful experience.

smertestillende.explanation: "Smertestillende" means "painkillers", medicine that takes away or lessens pain. It is short for smertestillende midler (pain-relieving medicines) and covers the whole group, from mild tablets to strong ones.

sentence.da: Hun tog **smertestillende**, fordi hendes tand gjorde ondt.
sentence.en: She took painkillers because her tooth hurt.

smigret.explanation: "Smigret" means "flattered", pleased because someone said something nice about you. You usually say føle sig smigret (to feel flattered).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **smigret**, da min chef roste mit arbejde.
sentence.en: I was flattered when my boss praised my work.

smitsom.explanation: "Smitsom" means "contagious", able to spread from one person to another: en smitsom sygdom (a contagious disease). It also works for feelings: smitsom latter (contagious laughter).

sentence.da: Influenza er **smitsom**, og syge børn bør blive hjemme.
sentence.en: Influenza is contagious, and sick children should stay home.

smuk.explanation: "Smuk" means "beautiful", for people, places, views and things. It is a bit stronger than pæn (nice-looking). Hvor er det smukt! means "How beautiful it is!"

sentence.da: Hun har en **smuk** kjole på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a beautiful dress.

småpenge.explanation: "Småpenge" means "small change", coins of little value, and it only exists in the plural. It is also used for a small price: Det er småpenge (It is peanuts).

sentence.da: Har du nogle **småpenge** til automaten?
sentence.en: Do you have some small change for the machine?

småting.explanation: "Småting" means "small things" or "trifles", and it is almost always plural. It is built from små (small) and ting (things).

forms.en: I am buying some small things.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bare købe nogle **småting** i byen.
sentence.en: I just have to buy a few small things in town.

smør.explanation: "Smør" means "butter". The word for spreading it is at smøre (to spread), which looks almost the same. Smørrebrød is literally butter-bread, a slice of bread with toppings.

sentence.da: Vil du have **smør** på dit brød?
sentence.en: Do you want butter on your bread?

smøreost.explanation: "Smøreost" means "spreadable cheese", a soft cheese you spread instead of slicing. It is smøre (to spread) and ost (cheese) joined together.

sentence.da: Jeg smører **smøreost** på mit rugbrød.
sentence.en: I spread spreadable cheese on my rye bread.

snakkesalig.explanation: "Snakkesalig" means "chatty", someone who likes to talk and always has something to say, like a child after school. It is mild and often friendly, and it comes from at snakke (to talk).

sentence.da: Han er **snakkesalig** og fortæller gerne om hele sin dag.
sentence.en: He is chatty and likes to tell about his whole day.

snarere.explanation: "Snarere" means "rather" when you correct or sharpen what you just said: Han er ikke doven, snarere træt (He is not lazy, rather tired). To say you prefer something, use hellere: Jeg vil hellere gå (I would rather walk).

sentence.da: Det var ikke en fejl, men **snarere** en dårlig plan.
sentence.en: It was not a mistake, but rather a bad plan.

snart.explanation: "Snart" means "soon": Vi ses snart (See you soon). With a clock time it means "almost": Klokken er snart ti (It is almost ten o'clock). Så snart means "as soon as": Så snart jeg kommer hjem, ringer jeg (As soon as I get home, I will call).

sentence.da: Maden er **snart** klar.
sentence.en: The food will be ready soon.

snavs.explanation: "Snavs" means "dirt", the dirty stuff on clothes, floors and hands. It is not soil in the ground: that is jord, as in Planterne vokser i jord (The plants grow in soil).

sentence.da: Der er meget **snavs** på mine sko.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dirt on my shoes.

snavset.explanation: "Snavset" means "dirty", covered with snavs (dirt) and in need of a wash.

sentence.da: Tøjet er **snavset** og skal vaskes.
sentence.en: The clothes are dirty and need washing.

sne.explanation: "Sne" means "snow". It is also the start of other snow words: en snebold (a snowball) and en snestorm (a snowstorm).

sentence.da: Børnene laver en snemand af **sne**.
sentence.en: The children make a snowman out of snow.

snu.explanation: "Snu" means "cunning": clever at getting what you want, often by a trick or by thinking ahead. It never changes form. It is spelled like at snu (to turn), but it is a different word.

sentence.da: Ræven er **snu** og stjæler æg fra hønsegården.
sentence.en: The fox is cunning and steals eggs from the henhouse.

snue.explanation: "Snue" means "a head cold", the runny-nose kind, and you say it with no en in front. For the flu, say influenza (flu).

sentence.da: Jeg har **snue**, og min næse løber.
sentence.en: I have a head cold, and my nose is running.

social.explanation: "Social" means "social", about people who like company or things done with others. It can also be about how people live together: sociale problemer (social problems).

sentence.da: Min søster er meget **social** og elsker fester.
sentence.en: My sister is very social and loves parties.

sociale medier.explanation: "Sociale medier" means "social media" and is normally used in the plural: Sociale medier er populære (Social media are popular).

sentence.da: Facebook og Instagram er **sociale medier**.
sentence.en: Facebook and Instagram are social media.

socialistisk.explanation: "Socialistisk" means "socialist", linked to socialism, the political idea that wealth and key services should be shared or owned together. In Danish politics it fits parties on the left, such as Socialistisk Folkeparti (the Socialist People's Party).

sentence.da: Et **socialistisk** parti vil have, at staten ejer mere.
sentence.en: A socialist party wants the state to own more.

software.explanation: "Software" means "software", the instructions that make a computer or phone work. The physical parts are called hardware, and Danish uses both English words as they are.

sentence.da: Vi bruger gratis **software** til at redigere billeder.
sentence.en: We use free software to edit pictures.

sojamælk.explanation: "Sojamælk" means "soy milk", a plant drink made from soybeans. It is soja (soy) and mælk (milk) joined together.

sentence.da: Hun drikker **sojamælk**, fordi hun er veganer.
sentence.en: She drinks soy milk because she is vegan.

sokker.explanation: "Sokker" means "socks". Danish often joins two words into one, so wool socks are uldsokker, from uld (wool) and sokker.

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sokker** og sko på.
sentence.en: I put on socks and shoes.

solbriller.explanation: "Solbriller" means "sunglasses", from sol (sun) and briller (glasses). It is always used for more than one, even for a single pair. Briller on its own means glasses you see with.

sentence.da: Jeg tager **solbriller** på i solen.
sentence.en: I put on sunglasses in the sun.

solbrændt.explanation: "Solbrændt" means "sunburned" or "tanned". It can be red and sore after too much sun, or just brown and healthy after a vacation, so the rest of the sentence shows which.

sentence.da: Efter en uge på stranden var han rød og **solbrændt**.
sentence.en: After a week on the beach he was red and sunburned.

solcreme.explanation: "Solcreme" means "sunscreen", from sol (sun) and creme (cream). When you talk about it in general, you leave out en, as in the last form above.

sentence.da: Husk at tage **solcreme** med på stranden.
sentence.en: Remember to bring sunscreen to the beach.

solenergi.explanation: "Solenergi" means "solar power", energy that comes from the sun. It is usually collected with solceller (solar cells) and turned into electricity, or used to heat water.

sentence.da: Med **solenergi** kan huset lave strøm af solens lys.
sentence.en: With solar power the house can make electricity from sunlight.

solid.explanation: "Solid" means "solid", well made and strong, so it does not break easily. It can also mean "reliable": en solid mand (a reliable man).

sentence.da: Vi byggede en **solid** hytte af sten.
sentence.en: We built a solid cabin made of stone.

solrig.explanation: "Solrig" means "sunny". When you just say what the weather is like, use solrigt: Det er solrigt i dag (It is sunny today).

sentence.da: Det er en varm og **solrig** dag.
sentence.en: It is a warm and sunny day.

solrigt.explanation: "Solrigt" means "sunny". You use it with vejr (weather), as in solrigt vejr (sunny weather), and after det er, as in Det er solrigt (It is sunny).

sentence.da: I dag er det **solrigt** og varmt.
sentence.en: Today it is sunny and warm.

solskin.explanation: "Solskin" means "sunshine", made of sol (sun) and skin (shine). The verb is at skinne (to shine): Solen skinner (The sun is shining).

sentence.da: Efter regnen kommer **solskin**.
sentence.en: After the rain comes sunshine.

solskinsvejr.explanation: "Solskinsvejr" means "sunny weather", from solskin (sunshine) and vejr (weather). It means a clear sky and bright sun: Hvis det er solskinsvejr, tager vi på stranden (If it is sunny, we go to the beach).

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at gå tur i **solskinsvejr**.
sentence.en: It is lovely to go for a walk in sunny weather.

solsystemet.explanation: "Solsystemet" means "the solar system", the sun and everything that circles it, including Earth and the other planets. Any star with planets can be called et solsystem (a solar system), but solsystemet means our own.

sentence.da: Jorden er en af otte planeter i **solsystemet**.
sentence.en: Earth is one of eight planets in the solar system.

som.explanation: "Som" means "who", "that" or "which" when it joins two parts of a sentence: manden, som bor her (the man who lives here), bogen, som jeg læser (the book that I read). It also means "like" or "as": Han er som sin far (He is like his father), Jeg arbejder som lærer (I work as a teacher).

sentence.da: Det er den bog, **som** jeg læser.
sentence.en: That is the book that I am reading.

som følge af.explanation: "Som følge af" means "as a result of" and names the reason for something that follows. It is typical of news and official writing. In daily speech people more often say på grund af (because of): Toget var forsinket på grund af sne (The train was delayed because of snow).

forms.en: as a result of the accident
as a result of the rain

sentence.da: Flere fly blev aflyst **som følge af** den kraftige storm.
sentence.en: Several flights were canceled as a result of the strong storm.

som helst.explanation: "Som helst" means "any" or "whatever" and is added to a question word: hvad som helst (anything), hvem som helst (anyone). After ikke (not), it means "at all": ikke noget som helst (nothing at all).

forms.da: Det kan være hvad som helst

sentence.da: Du kan spørge mig om hvad **som helst**.
sentence.en: You can ask me about anything.

som om.explanation: "Som om" means "as if" and compares with something that is not true or not sure: Han opfører sig, som om han ejer stedet (He acts as if he owns the place). Det ser ud, som om det regner (It looks as if it is raining).

forms.en: as if we know each other

sentence.da: Det føles **som om** vi har kendt hinanden længe.
sentence.en: It feels as if we have known each other for a long time.

som regel.explanation: "Som regel" means "as a rule", or "usually", and says what normally happens: Om søndagen sover vi som regel længe (On Sundays we usually sleep in).

forms.da: Jeg står som regel op klokken syv.
forms.en: I usually get up at seven o'clock.
As a rule we eat late.

sentence.da: Jeg drikker **som regel** kaffe om morgenen.
sentence.en: I usually drink coffee in the morning.

somme tider.explanation: "Somme tider" means "sometimes", for things that happen now and then, not every day.

sentence.da: Jeg er **somme tider** træt om morgenen.
sentence.en: I am sometimes tired in the morning.

sommertid.explanation: "Sommertid" means "daylight saving time", when the clocks go forward one hour: Med sommertid er det lyst om aftenen (With daylight saving time it is light in the evening). In the fall, the clocks go back again.

forms.da: Der er sommertid fra marts til oktober
forms.en: Daylight saving time runs from March to October
Daylight saving time starts in March
It is daylight saving time now

sentence.da: Vi skifter til **sommertid** i marts.
sentence.en: We switch to daylight saving time in March.

sommetider.explanation: "Sommetider" means "sometimes", for things that happen now and then, not every day.

forms.en: I sometimes go for a walk

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sommetider** cyklen på arbejde.
sentence.en: Sometimes I take the bike to work.

sorg.explanation: "Sorg" means "sorrow" and "grief", the deep sadness after losing someone. For ordinary sadness, say Jeg er ked af det (I am sad).

sentence.da: Hele byen delte familiens **sorg**.
sentence.en: The whole town shared the family's grief.

sort.explanation: "Sort" means "black", the darkest color, the opposite of white. It is also used for coffee with no milk: sort kaffe (black coffee).

sentence.da: Natten er mørk og **sort**.
sentence.en: The night is dark and black.

sov godt.explanation: "Sov godt" means "sleep well". Sov comes from at sove (to sleep) and godt means "well".

sentence.da: Godnat, **sov godt**!
sentence.en: Good night, sleep well!

spaghetti.explanation: "Spaghetti" means "spaghetti", spelled the same as in English. You do not count it: en tallerken spaghetti (a plate of spaghetti).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **spaghetti** med kødsovs.
sentence.en: We eat spaghetti with meat sauce.

spanien.explanation: "Spanien" means "Spain". Countries take i for being there and til for going there, as in the forms above.

sentence.da: Vi holder ferie i **Spanien**.
sentence.en: We are on vacation in Spain.

spansk.explanation: "Spansk" means "Spanish", for things from Spain and for the language. Danish writes it with a lowercase letter. For the language: Jeg taler spansk (I speak Spanish).

sentence.da: I Spanien taler man **spansk**.
sentence.en: In Spain, people speak Spanish.

spartansk.explanation: "Spartansk" means "spartan": very plain, without comfort or extras. It comes from Sparta, the ancient Greek city known for its hard way of life.

sentence.da: Værelset var **spartansk** og havde kun en seng og en stol.
sentence.en: The room was spartan and only had a bed and a chair.

speciel.explanation: "Speciel" means "special". It can also mean "odd" in a mild way: Han er lidt speciel (He is a bit odd).

sentence.da: I dag er en **speciel** dag for os.
sentence.en: Today is a special day for us.

specifik.explanation: "Specifik" means "specific", exact and clearly pointed out instead of general. It is the opposite of generel (general): Kan du give et specifikt eksempel? (Can you give a specific example?)

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter en **specifik** bog, ikke bare en krimi.
sentence.en: I am looking for a specific book, not just a crime novel.

specifikt.explanation: "Specifikt" means "specifically" and narrows what you say down to one exact thing. To describe a thing itself as exact, use specifik (specific): en specifik grund (a specific reason).

forms.en: What are you looking for specifically?

sentence.da: Jeg vil **specifikt** have den røde jakke, ikke den blå.
sentence.en: I specifically want the red jacket, not the blue one.

spegepølse.explanation: "En spegepølse" means "a salami", a dry, cured sausage that is sliced thin and eaten cold.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en tynd skive **spegepølse** på rugbrødet.
sentence.en: I put a thin slice of salami on the rye bread.

spids.explanation: "Spids" means "pointed" or "sharp", narrowing to a thin end, like a pencil. For a blade that cuts, use skarp (sharp): en skarp kniv (a sharp knife).

sentence.da: Nålen er **spids**, og den kan stikke dig.
sentence.en: The needle is pointed, and it can prick you.

spinat.explanation: "Spinat" means "spinach". For spinach in general, you leave out en: Jeg elsker spinat (I love spinach).

sentence.da: **Spinat** er grøn og sund.
sentence.en: Spinach is green and healthy.

spinkel.explanation: "Spinkel" means "slender" or "frail": slight and delicate, about a body or a branch. It can also be used for a basis that is too flimsy to rely on: et spinkelt grundlag (a flimsy basis).

sentence.da: Pigen er **spinkel**, men stærk og hurtig.
sentence.en: The girl is slender, but strong and fast.

spirituel.explanation: "Spirituel" means "witty": clever with words, so that remarks are amusing and sharp. For something religious or of the soul, åndelig (spiritual) is the safest word.

sentence.da: Hun er **spirituel** og har altid et skarpt svar klar.
sentence.en: She is witty and always has a sharp answer ready.

spiselig.explanation: "Spiselig" means "edible", safe to eat. It says nothing about taste: a thing can be spiselig and still not be lækker (delicious).

sentence.da: Denne svamp er **spiselig**, men den anden er giftig.
sentence.en: This mushroom is edible, but the other one is poisonous.

spontan.explanation: "Spontan" means "spontaneous" and describes something done without planning.

sentence.da: Vi tog en **spontan** tur til stranden i går.
sentence.en: We took a spontaneous trip to the beach yesterday.

sport.explanation: "Sport" means "sport". For sport in general, you leave out en. At dyrke sport means "to do sports": Han dyrker meget sport (He does a lot of sports).

sentence.da: Fodbold og tennis er **sport**.
sentence.en: Soccer and tennis are sports.

sportslig.explanation: "Sportslig" means "sporty" or "athletic" and is about competing and training, not about looks. For clothes or a casual look, Danes use the loan word sporty: en sporty jakke (a sporty jacket).

sentence.da: Holdet havde en stor **sportslig** succes i år.
sentence.en: The team had a big athletic success this year.

sporty.explanation: "Sporty" means "sporty", borrowed from English, and it describes a casual, active style, mostly in clothes. It never changes, so it looks the same with en-words, et-words and plurals. It is about looks, while sportslig (athletic) is about sport itself.

sentence.da: Hun kommer altid i **sporty** sko og en let jakke.
sentence.en: She always comes in sporty shoes and a light jacket.

sprogkundskaber.explanation: "Sprogkundskaber" means "language skills", what you know and can do in one or more languages. It is common in job ads, where employers list the languages they want.

sentence.da: Jobbet kræver **sprogkundskaber** i både engelsk og tysk.
sentence.en: The job requires language skills in both English and German.

sprængstof.explanation: "Et sprængstof" means "an explosive": a substance that blows up with great force, used in mines and for demolition. It is built from at sprænge (to blow up) and stof (substance). Stof also means fabric, so the meaning depends on the word before it.

sentence.da: Arbejderne bruger **sprængstof** til at lave tunneler i fjeldet.
sentence.en: The workers use explosives to make tunnels in the rock.

sprød.explanation: "Sprød" means "crispy" or "crunchy", for food that breaks with a snap. Fresh vegetables can be sprød too: sprøde gulerødder (crunchy carrots).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **sprød** bacon.
sentence.en: I like crispy bacon.

spændende.explanation: "Spændende" means "exciting" or "interesting". Det lyder spændende means "That sounds exciting". Interessant (interesting) is milder and fits less thrilling things.

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **spændende** bog.
sentence.en: I am reading an exciting book.

spænding.explanation: "Spænding" means "excitement" and also "tension": Børnene taler med spænding om turen (The kids talk with excitement about the trip). Der var spænding mellem dem (There was tension between them). A film that keeps you hooked is spændende (exciting).

sentence.da: Vi ventede med **spænding** på resultatet.
sentence.en: We waited with excitement for the result.

spærret.explanation: "Spærret" means "blocked" or "closed", for a way you cannot pass, such as a road or an entrance. Something has shut it on purpose, such as police or a fence.

sentence.da: Broen er **spærret**, fordi der er vejarbejde i dag.
sentence.en: The bridge is closed because there are roadworks today.

stabil.explanation: "Stabil" means "stable", for things that do not wobble or change: Hans helbred er stabilt (His health is stable).

sentence.da: Den nye stige er meget **stabil**, så den er sikker.
sentence.en: The new ladder is very stable, so it is safe.

stadig.explanation: "Stadig" means "still", for something that is continuing: Jeg er stadig træt (I am still tired). Endnu (yet) is used for something that has not happened: ikke endnu means "not yet".

sentence.da: Barnet sover **stadig** klokken ti.
sentence.en: The child is still sleeping at ten o'clock.

stadigvæk.explanation: "Stadigvæk" means "still", for something that keeps going: Det regner stadigvæk (It is still raining). It means the same as stadig (still). Endnu (yet) is different: ikke endnu means "not yet".

sentence.da: Han bor **stadigvæk** hos sin mor.
sentence.en: He still lives with his mother.

stakkels.explanation: "Stakkels" means "poor" in the sense of pitiful, when you feel sorry for someone: Stakkels dig! (Poor you!). For someone with no money, use fattig (poor).

sentence.da: Den **stakkels** hund er våd og kold.
sentence.en: The poor dog is wet and cold.

standard.explanation: "Standard" means "standard", the plain, regular version of something with no extras. It also means a level of quality: Danes say høj standard (high standard) for something that is of good quality.

sentence.da: Bilen har varme i sæderne som **standard**.
sentence.en: The car has heated seats as standard.

standhaftig.explanation: "Standhaftig" means "steadfast": staying firm in your views or promises even under pressure. It is a positive word. Stædig (stubborn) is the one you use when the firmness annoys others.

sentence.da: Hun forblev **standhaftig** og gav ikke efter for presset.
sentence.en: She remained steadfast and did not give in to the pressure.

stavning.explanation: "En stavning" means "a spelling", the way a word is written out. The action behind it is at stave (to spell): Kan du stave dit navn? (Can you spell your name?)

sentence.da: Ordbogen viser den rigtige **stavning** af hvert ord.
sentence.en: The dictionary shows the correct spelling of each word.

stegt.explanation: "Stegt" means "fried" or "roasted", food cooked in fat or in an oven, depending on the food: stegt flæsk (fried pork) and stegt kylling (roast chicken).

sentence.da: Fisken er **stegt** i panden.
sentence.en: The fish is fried in the pan.

stegt flæsk.explanation: "Stegt flæsk" means "fried pork belly", thick slices fried until crisp. It is traditionally eaten with potatoes and a white sauce, and many Danes call it the national dish.

forms.en: two slices of fried pork belly
We are eating fried pork belly

sentence.da: **Stegt flæsk** med persillesovs er en klassisk dansk ret.
sentence.en: Fried pork belly with parsley sauce is a classic Danish dish.

stemmeret.explanation: "En stemmeret" means "a right to vote", the legal right to cast your vote when the country chooses its government. A group can win it: Kvinder fik stemmeret i 1915 (Women got the right to vote in 1915).

sentence.da: I Danmark får man **stemmeret**, når man fylder atten år.
sentence.en: In Denmark you get the right to vote when you turn eighteen.

stemningsfuld.explanation: "Stemningsfuld" means "atmospheric": having a strong, pleasant mood, like an old street at dusk. It is built from en stemning (a mood) and -fuld (full of).

sentence.da: Caféen er **stemningsfuld**, med levende lys og blød musik.
sentence.en: The café is atmospheric, with candles and soft music.

stilhed.explanation: "Stilhed" means "silence", when nobody speaks and there is no sound: Der var stilhed i klassen (There was silence in the class). For peace and quiet, Danes say ro: Jeg vil have ro (I want peace and quiet).

sentence.da: Efter skriget var der **stilhed** i huset.
sentence.en: After the scream there was silence in the house.

stille.explanation: "Stille" means "quiet", "silent" or "calm": Vær stille means "Be quiet". For a calm, relaxed person, rolig (calm) also fits. Do not mix it up with at stille (to put or place), as in at stille et spørgsmål (to ask a question).

sentence.da: Det er meget **stille** i huset.
sentence.en: It is very quiet in the house.

stillehavet.explanation: "Stillehavet" means "the Pacific Ocean". The name is built from stille (calm) and hav (ocean), and you say i Stillehavet (in the Pacific) with no extra word for "the".

sentence.da: **Stillehavet** er det største hav på Jorden og ligger mellem Asien og Amerika.
sentence.en: The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean on Earth and lies between Asia and America.

stinkende.explanation: "Stinkende" means "stinking", with a very bad smell. It is also used to strengthen another word, as in stinkende rig (stinking rich).

sentence.da: Der er **stinkende** fisk i skraldespanden, og alle kan lugte det.
sentence.en: There is stinking fish in the trash can, and everyone can smell it.

stiv.explanation: "Stiv" means "stiff" and describes something that does not bend, or a body that is sore and tight: Mine ben er stive efter turen (My legs are stiff after the trip).

sentence.da: Jeg er **stiv** i nakken i dag.
sentence.en: My neck is stiff today.

stolt af.explanation: "Stolt af" means "proud of": Jeg er stolt af dig (I am proud of you). Before an action, use af at: stolt af at have klaret det (proud of having managed it).

forms.da: Jeg er stolt af min datter.
forms.en: I am proud of my daughter.

forms.da: Hun er stolt af sit hus.
forms.en: She is proud of her house.
We are proud of the team.

sentence.da: Jeg er **stolt af** min lille bror.
sentence.en: I am proud of my little brother.

stolthed.explanation: "Stolthed" means "pride", the warm feeling when you or someone close did something well. The person who feels it is stolt (proud).

sentence.da: Hans mor græd af **stolthed**, fordi han vandt.
sentence.en: His mother cried with pride because he won.

stop.explanation: "Stop" means "stop". Adding lige (just) makes it softer: Stop lige! (Hold on a second!).

sentence.da: **Stop**! Der kommer en bil!
sentence.en: Stop! A car is coming!

stor.explanation: "Stor" means "big" or "large". It can also mean "grown-up": Hvor er du blevet stor! means "How big you have grown!"

sentence.da: Elefanten er meget **stor**.
sentence.en: The elephant is very big.

storartet.explanation: "Storartet" means "magnificent", a warm, strong word of praise for something very good, such as a result, a performance or a meal. For a grand view or building, use storslået (grand).

sentence.da: Det var en **storartet** forestilling, og publikum klappede længe.
sentence.en: It was a magnificent performance, and the audience clapped for a long time.

storbritannien.explanation: "Storbritannien" means "Great Britain". It is built from stor (big) and Britannien (Britain). Stor also starts other words, such as en storby (a big city).

sentence.da: London ligger i **Storbritannien**.
sentence.en: London is in Great Britain.

stormfuld.explanation: "Stormfuld" means "stormy", full of strong wind and rough weather. It is also used for troubled times in life, so a bumpy relationship can be stormfuld too.

sentence.da: Natten var **stormfuld**, og vinden ruskede i træerne.
sentence.en: The night was stormy, and the wind shook the trees.

storslået.explanation: "Storslået" means "grand" or "magnificent", large and so beautiful or impressive that it makes people stop and look. It is mostly used for nature, buildings and big events.

sentence.da: Fra toppen af bjerget har man en **storslået** udsigt.
sentence.en: From the top of the mountain you have a magnificent view.

stort set.explanation: "Stort set" means "basically" and "more or less". It says that something is nearly true, with only a small part missing.

sentence.da: Vi er **stort set** enige om det.
sentence.en: We basically agree about it.

straks.explanation: "Straks" means "right away", and often "in just a moment". It says the thing will happen almost at once, and is common when you answer someone: Vent lidt, jeg er der straks (Wait a bit, I'll be there in a moment).

sentence.da: Sæt dig ned, maden er **straks** klar.
sentence.en: Sit down, the food will be ready in a moment.

stram.explanation: "Stram" means "tight", fitting closely or pulled hard: en stram knude (a tight knot). It can also mean strict, as in en stram regel (a strict rule).

sentence.da: Jakken er for **stram** over skuldrene, og jeg vil bytte den.
sentence.en: The jacket is too tight over the shoulders, and I want to exchange it.

stramt.explanation: "Stramt" means "tightly", describing how something is tied, pulled or fitted.

sentence.da: Hun bandt sækken **stramt** til.
sentence.en: She tied the sack tightly.

streaming.explanation: "Streaming" means "streaming", watching or listening online without saving the file first.

sentence.da: Vi bruger **streaming** i stedet for dvd'er.
sentence.en: We use streaming instead of DVDs.

streng.explanation: "Streng" means "strict" and describes people and rules that allow little freedom. It also fits a very cold winter: en streng vinter (a harsh winter).

sentence.da: Vores lærer er **streng**, men retfærdig.
sentence.en: Our teacher is strict but fair.

stress.explanation: "Stress" means "stress", the strained feeling of having too much to handle. Danes use it for everyday pressure and for long overload that makes people take time off work: Han er sygemeldt med stress (He is on sick leave with stress).

sentence.da: Meget arbejde og lidt søvn kan give **stress**.
sentence.en: A lot of work and little sleep can cause stress.

stresset.explanation: "Stresset" means "stressed", feeling that there is too much to do. To describe the thing that causes it, use stressende (stressful): Det er stressende (It is stressful).

sentence.da: Hun er **stresset**, fordi hun har for meget arbejde.
sentence.en: She is stressed because she has too much work.

stribet.explanation: "Stribet" means "striped", with lines of different colors running side by side. It comes from en stribe (a stripe).

sentence.da: Zebraens pels er **stribet** i sort og hvid.
sentence.en: The zebra's coat is striped in black and white.

strikning.explanation: "Strikning" means "knitting", the activity or hobby as a whole. To say what you are doing, use the verb at strikke (to knit): Jeg strikker en trøje (I am knitting a sweater).

sentence.da: Min mormor elsker **strikning** og laver mange trøjer.
sentence.en: My grandmother loves knitting and makes many sweaters.

strålende.explanation: "Strålende" means "brilliant" or "radiant", for something that shines or is wonderful. It comes from en stråle (a ray of light). It is also a strong way to say great: Det går strålende (It is going great).

sentence.da: Vi havde **strålende** vejr hele ugen.
sentence.en: We had brilliant weather all week.

stråling.explanation: "Stråling" means "radiation": energy that travels as rays, such as heat and light. It comes from en stråle (a ray).

sentence.da: For meget **stråling** fra solen kan skade huden.
sentence.en: Too much radiation from the sun can damage the skin.

strøm.explanation: "Strøm" means "electricity", the power that runs your home. It also means a "current" in water: en stærk strøm i floden (a strong current in the river).

sentence.da: Lamper og computere bruger **strøm**.
sentence.en: Lamps and computers use electricity.

strømpebukser.explanation: "Strømpebukser" means "tights", the thin legwear worn under skirts and dresses. It is always plural: et par strømpebukser (a pair of tights).

sentence.da: Hun har sorte **strømpebukser** på til kjolen.
sentence.en: She is wearing black tights with the dress.

styrketræning.explanation: "Styrketræning" means "strength training", exercise that makes muscles stronger, such as lifting weights. Exercise for stamina, like running, is called konditionstræning (cardio training).

sentence.da: Med **styrketræning** bliver musklerne større og stærkere.
sentence.en: With strength training, the muscles get bigger and stronger.

stål.explanation: "Stål" means "steel", the hard, strong metal made from iron. You say stål with no en or et in front when you mean the material.

sentence.da: Broen er lavet af **stål** og er meget stærk.
sentence.en: The bridge is made of steel and is very strong.

stædig.explanation: "Stædig" means "stubborn" and describes someone who will not change their mind. It is often said about children and animals.

sentence.da: Han er **stædig** og vil aldrig lytte til andre.
sentence.en: He is stubborn and never wants to listen to others.

stærk.explanation: "Stærk" means "strong", for people, coffee, tea, wind and feelings: stærk kaffe is strong coffee. For food it also means "hot" or "spicy": en stærk sovs (a spicy sauce).

sentence.da: Han er **stærk** og kan løfte tunge ting.
sentence.en: He is strong and can lift heavy things.

støj.explanation: "Støj" means "noise", the unwanted kind such as traffic or loud neighbors. A sound you like is lyd (sound), not støj: en dejlig lyd (a lovely sound).

sentence.da: Naboerne laver meget **støj** om natten.
sentence.en: The neighbors make a lot of noise at night.

støjende.explanation: "Støjende" means "noisy", for a person or place that is loud all the time. For a single loud sound, use høj (loud): høj musik (loud music).

sentence.da: Vores naboer er meget **støjende** om natten.
sentence.en: Our neighbors are very noisy at night.

størst.explanation: "Størst" means "biggest" or "largest", the one that nothing else beats. Compare Hun er større (She is bigger) with Han er størst (He is the biggest).

sentence.da: Hvalen er **størst** af dyrene.
sentence.en: The whale is the biggest of the animals.

støv.explanation: "Støv" means "dust", the fine dry kind that settles on shelves and floors. To clean it, use at tørre støv af (to wipe dust off).

sentence.da: Der er meget **støv** under sofaen.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dust under the sofa.

støvler.explanation: "Støvler" means "boots", sturdy footwear that covers the ankle or more, worn in wet or cold weather. A pair is et par støvler (a pair of boots).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **støvler** på i regnen.
sentence.en: I put on boots in the rain.

støvregn.explanation: "Støvregn" means "drizzle", very fine rain that feels almost like mist. It is built from støv (dust) and regn (rain): drops as small as dust.

sentence.da: I **støvregn** bliver man næsten ikke våd.
sentence.en: In drizzle you hardly get wet.

su.explanation: "SU" means "Danish student grant", the monthly money the state pays to people who study at a university or college. The letters stand for statens uddannelsesstøtte (the state's study support).

sentence.da: Studerende på universitetet får **SU** hver måned.
sentence.en: Students at the university get SU every month.

subjektiv.explanation: "Subjektiv" means "subjective", based on personal taste and views instead of facts. That is why two people can both be right about something subjective.

sentence.da: Smag er **subjektiv**.
sentence.en: Taste is subjective.

succesfuld.explanation: "Succesfuld" means "successful", for a person, a plan or a business that reaches its goal.

sentence.da: Hun er en **succesfuld** læge.
sentence.en: She is a successful doctor.

sukker.explanation: "Sukker" means "sugar", the white powder used in baking and drinks.

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **sukker** i kaffen.
sentence.en: I want sugar in my coffee.

sult.explanation: "Sult" means "hunger", mostly as a big or general problem: Der er sult i verden (There is hunger in the world). To say you are hungry, use sulten: Jeg er sulten (I am hungry), not Jeg har sult.

sentence.da: Mange mennesker i verden lider af **sult** og har ikke mad.
sentence.en: Many people in the world suffer from hunger and have no food.

sulten.explanation: "Sulten" means "hungry", the feeling that your body wants food. It describes a person or animal.

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **sulten** og vil spise.
sentence.en: I am very hungry and want to eat.

sund.explanation: "Sund" means "healthy", good for your body, like fruit, sleep and exercise. Do not mix it up with rask (well, not sick): Jeg er rask igen (I am well again).

sentence.da: Æbler og gulerødder er **sund** mad.
sentence.en: Apples and carrots are healthy food.

sundhed.explanation: "Sundhed" means "health" in a general sense, such as how healthy a lifestyle or a country is. For a person's own condition, Danes usually say helbred (health): Han har dårligt helbred (He is in poor health).

forms.en: It is good for your health.

sentence.da: Frugt og søvn er gode for din **sundhed**.
sentence.en: Fruit and sleep are good for your health.

sundhedsvæsenet.explanation: "Sundhedsvæsenet" means "the healthcare system", all the hospitals, family doctors and other care that a country offers its people.

sentence.da: I Danmark er **sundhedsvæsenet** betalt over skatten.
sentence.en: In Denmark the healthcare system is paid for through taxes.

super.explanation: "Super" means "great". It can stand alone: Super! (Great!). Before another word, it makes that word stronger: super god (really good).

sentence.da: Vi vandt kampen. Det var **super**!
sentence.en: We won the game. It was great!

sur.explanation: "Sur" means "sour" and also "grumpy": Citronen er sur (The lemon is sour) and Han er sur i dag (He is grumpy today).

sentence.da: Min bror er altid **sur** om morgenen.
sentence.en: My brother is always grumpy in the morning.

sur på.explanation: "Sur på" means "mad at". The person you are mad at comes after på (at). On its own, sur also means "sour": en sur citron (a sour lemon).

forms.da: Jeg er sur på min bror.
forms.en: I am mad at my brother.

sentence.da: Min mor er **sur på** mig i dag.
sentence.en: My mom is mad at me today.

suspenderet.explanation: "Suspenderet" means "suspended", sent away from a job, school or team for a while, for example while a case is investigated. It comes from at suspendere (to suspend).

sentence.da: Spilleren blev **suspenderet** i to kampe.
sentence.en: The player was suspended for two games.

svag.explanation: "Svag" means "weak" for people and things. It also means "faint" for a sound or a light: en svag lyd (a faint sound).

sentence.da: Han er stadig **svag** efter sygdommen.
sentence.en: He is still weak after the illness.

sved.explanation: "Sved" means "sweat", the salty water your skin makes when you are hot or working hard. A sudden sweat from fear is called koldsved (cold sweat).

sentence.da: Efter løbeturen havde han **sved** på panden.
sentence.en: After the run he had sweat on his forehead.

svensk.explanation: "Svensk" means "Swedish". It is also the name of the language: Jeg taler svensk (I speak Swedish).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Sverige og er **svensk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Sweden and is Swedish.

sverige.explanation: "Sverige" means "Sweden". Do not mix it up with Schweiz (Switzerland), which is a different country.

sentence.da: **Sverige** er et land ved siden af Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is a country next to Denmark.

svigerforældre.explanation: "Svigerforældre" means "parents-in-law", the parents of your husband, wife or partner. To talk about just one of them, use en svigermor (mother-in-law) or en svigerfar (father-in-law).

sentence.da: Min mands forældre er mine **svigerforældre**.
sentence.en: My husband's parents are my parents-in-law.

svimmel.explanation: "Svimmel" means "dizzy", the feeling that the room is spinning. You say Jeg er svimmel (I am dizzy) or Jeg bliver svimmel (I am getting dizzy).

sentence.da: Jeg er **svimmel** og skal sidde ned.
sentence.en: I am dizzy and need to sit down.

svimmelhed.explanation: "Svimmelhed" means "dizziness", the feeling that the room is spinning. To say you feel it right now, use svimmel: Jeg er svimmel (I am dizzy).

sentence.da: **Svimmelhed** kan være et tegn på for lavt blodtryk.
sentence.en: Dizziness can be a sign of low blood pressure.

svindel.explanation: "Svindel" means "fraud", tricking people to get their money, for example with fake emails or phone calls.

sentence.da: Politiet advarer mod **svindel** på nettet.
sentence.en: The police warn against fraud online.

svinekød.explanation: "Svinekød" means "pork". It is built from svin (pig) and kød (meat), so it is literally pig meat. It is the meat in flæskesteg (roast pork with crackling), a classic Danish dinner.

sentence.da: **Svinekød** er kød fra en gris.
sentence.en: Pork is meat from a pig.

svær.explanation: "Svær" means "difficult" or "hard to do". Det er svært means "It is hard", and Det er svært at lære dansk means "It is hard to learn Danish".

sentence.da: Opgaven er meget **svær** for mig.
sentence.en: The task is very difficult for me.

svømning.explanation: "Svømning" means "swimming" as an activity or class. Compare Jeg kan svømme (I can swim) with Jeg har svømning (I have a swimming class).

sentence.da: Børnene har **svømning** i svømmehallen i dag.
sentence.en: The children have swim class at the pool today.

syd.explanation: "Syd" means "south". Use i syd for a place and mod syd for a direction: Det er varmt i syd (It is warm in the south).

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver mod **syd** om vinteren.
sentence.en: The birds fly south in the winter.

sydamerika.explanation: "Sydamerika" means "South America". It is made from syd (south) and Amerika (America). Syd also works in other words, such as sydpå (to the south).

sentence.da: Brasilien og Argentina ligger i **Sydamerika**.
sentence.en: Brazil and Argentina are in South America.

sydlig.explanation: "Sydlig" means "southern" and also "from the south". For a part of a country, say: Sønderborg ligger i det sydlige Danmark (Sønderborg is in southern Denmark).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **sydlig** vind i aften.
sentence.en: A southerly wind is coming tonight.

sydpå.explanation: "Sydpå" means "southward", toward the south, for movement. For a place, use syd for (south of): Odense ligger syd for Aarhus (Odense is south of Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi kører **sydpå** i morgen.
sentence.en: We are driving south tomorrow.

syg.explanation: "Syg" means "sick" or "ill". At melde sig syg means "to call in sick".

sentence.da: Min søn er **syg** og bliver hjemme.
sentence.en: My son is sick and stays home.

syltetøj.explanation: "Syltetøj" means "jam". Put the name of a fruit in front to say the kind: hindbærsyltetøj (raspberry jam), blommesyltetøj (plum jam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **syltetøj** på mit brød.
sentence.en: I want jam on my bread.

sympati.explanation: "Sympati" means "sympathy", kind feeling toward someone in a hard situation. It also means mild support for an idea: Jeg har sympati for forslaget (I am sympathetic to the proposal).

sentence.da: Vi sendte blomster som tegn på **sympati**.
sentence.en: We sent flowers as a sign of sympathy.

sympatisk.explanation: "Sympatisk" means "likeable" and is used for someone you like at first meeting: Han virker sympatisk (He seems likeable). It does not mean "sympathetic".

sentence.da: Din nye chef virker meget **sympatisk**.
sentence.en: Your new boss seems very likeable.

syning.explanation: "Syning" means "sewing", the activity or hobby as a whole. To say what you are doing, use the verb at sy (to sew): Jeg syr en kjole (I am sewing a dress).

sentence.da: Min mor elsker **syning**, og hun syr mange kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother loves sewing, and she sews many dresses.

synlig.explanation: "Synlig" means "visible", possible to see. It is used for things you can see with your eyes and for changes that people can notice.

sentence.da: Månen er **synlig** på himlen i aften.
sentence.en: The moon is visible in the sky tonight.

sytten.explanation: "Sytten" means "seventeen". Do not mix it up with syv (seven): syv børn (seven children), sytten børn (seventeen children).

sentence.da: Efter seksten kommer **sytten**.
sentence.en: After sixteen comes seventeen.

syv.explanation: "Syv" means "seven". Do not mix it up with sytten (seventeen): syv dage (seven days) but sytten dage (seventeen days).

sentence.da: Der er **syv** dage i en uge.
sentence.en: There are seven days in a week.

syvende.explanation: "Syvende" means "seventh". Compare syv æg (seven eggs) with det syvende æg (the seventh egg). It is used for dates too: den syvende juli (the seventh of July).

sentence.da: Søndag er den **syvende** dag i ugen.
sentence.en: Sunday is the seventh day of the week.

så.explanation: "Så" means "so" or "then". Compare Det regner, så vi bliver hjemme (It is raining, so we stay home) with Først spiser vi, og så går vi (First we eat, and then we go). Before a describing word, it adds strength: så stor (so big). Careful: så is also the past of at se (to see): Jeg så ham (I saw him).

sentence.da: Jeg er **så** glad i dag!
sentence.en: I am so happy today!

så at sige.explanation: "Så at sige" means "so to speak" or "in a way", used when what you say is not exactly true but very close.

forms.da: Han er så at sige min bror
forms.en: He is, so to speak, my brother

forms.da: Det er så at sige færdigt
forms.en: It is, so to speak, finished

forms.da: Vi bor så at sige i skoven
forms.en: We live, so to speak, in the forest

sentence.da: Vi har **så at sige** ingen penge tilbage.
sentence.en: We have, so to speak, no money left.

så længe.explanation: "Så længe" means "as long as". It is different from indtil (until): Jeg bliver, indtil du kommer (I stay until you come). On its own, it means "for now": Vent her så længe (Wait here for now).

forms.en: as long as there is time

sentence.da: Jeg er glad, **så længe** solen skinner.
sentence.en: I am happy as long as the sun shines.

så snart.explanation: "Så snart" means "as soon as" and names the moment when the next thing happens: Så snart han kom, gik vi (As soon as he came, we left).

forms.en: as soon as it is ready

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig, **så snart** jeg er hjemme.
sentence.en: I will call you as soon as I am home.

så vidt.explanation: "Så vidt" means "as far as", and limits what you say to what you know or what is possible. It can also mean "only just": Jeg nåede så vidt toget (I only just caught the train).

forms.en: as far as I can see

sentence.da: **Så vidt** jeg ved, åbner butikken klokken ni.
sentence.en: As far as I know, the store opens at nine o'clock.

sådan.explanation: "Sådan" means "like that" or "this way". Compare Gør det sådan (Do it like this) with sådan en bil (a car like that). Said on its own, Sådan! means "There you go!" or "That's it!"

sentence.da: Se, jeg gør det **sådan**.
sentence.en: Look, I do it like this.

sådan er det bare.explanation: "Sådan er det bare" means "that's just how it is" and you use it for something that cannot be changed: Der er ofte kø her, men sådan er det bare (There is often a line here, but that's just how it is). The word bare (just) makes it sound calm.

related.en: that's just the way it is

sentence.da: Det regner meget her, men **sådan er det bare**.
sentence.en: It rains a lot here, but that's just how it is.

sådanne.explanation: "Sådanne" means "such", used before more than one thing. For one thing Danes say sådan: sådan en regel (such a rule).

sentence.da: Vi køber aldrig **sådanne** dyre ting.
sentence.en: We never buy such expensive things.

sågar.explanation: "Sågar" means "even", adding something more surprising than what came before. It does not mean "even if": for that Danes say selv om (even if).

sentence.da: Det regnede hele dagen og sneede **sågar** om aftenen.
sentence.en: It rained all day and even snowed in the evening.

såkaldt.explanation: "Såkaldt" means "so-called", used for a name that others give something. It often shows doubt about whether the name fits: Den såkaldte chef tog fejl (The so-called boss was wrong).

sentence.da: Han er en **såkaldt** ekspert uden uddannelse.
sentence.en: He is a so-called expert without any training.

således.explanation: "Således" means "thus" and "like this". It shows how something is done, and it is formal and mostly written. In speech, people say sådan instead: Gør det sådan (Do it like this).

sentence.da: Du skal skrive det **således**.
sentence.en: You must write it like this.

sårbar.explanation: "Sårbar" means "vulnerable", easy to hurt or damage, in body, feelings or systems. It is built from et sår (a wound) and -bar, which works like -able in English, as in brugbar (usable).

sentence.da: En nyfødt fugl er meget **sårbar**.
sentence.en: A newborn bird is very vulnerable.

såret.explanation: "Såret" means "wounded" or "hurt", for a body or for feelings: Soldaten er såret (The soldier is wounded). Hun følte sig såret (She felt hurt).

sentence.da: Hunden er **såret** i benet og kan ikke gå.
sentence.en: The dog is wounded in the leg and cannot walk.

såsom.explanation: "Såsom" means "such as", introducing examples after a general word. It sounds more written than spoken; in everyday speech Danes often say som for eksempel (like for example).

forms.en: countries such as Norway and Sweden

sentence.da: Han spiser meget grønt, **såsom** broccoli og spinat.
sentence.en: He eats a lot of greens, such as broccoli and spinach.

sæbe.explanation: "Sæbe" means "soap". For an amount, you say noget sæbe (some soap) or et stykke sæbe (a piece of soap). Dish soap is a different word: opvaskemiddel (dishwashing liquid).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mine hænder med **sæbe** og vand.
sentence.en: I wash my hands with soap and water.

sædvanlig.explanation: "Sædvanlig" means "usual", what you would normally expect. The most common use is the set phrase som sædvanligt (as usual): Maden var god som sædvanligt (The food was good as usual).

sentence.da: Det er en helt **sædvanlig** tirsdag.
sentence.en: It is a completely usual Tuesday.

særegen.explanation: "Særegen" means "distinctive", used for something with a character of its own that sets it apart from others, such as a style, a smell or a voice.

sentence.da: Byen har en **særegen** lugt af tang og røg.
sentence.en: The city has a distinctive smell of seaweed and smoke.

særlig.explanation: "Særlig" means "special" or "particular". With ikke, it means "not very": Det er ikke særlig dyrt (It is not very expensive).

sentence.da: I dag er en **særlig** dag for os.
sentence.en: Today is a special day for us.

sød.explanation: "Sød" means "sweet" in taste (sød kage, sweet cake) and also "sweet" or "cute" for people, animals and small children. A common phrase is Det er sødt af dig (That is sweet of you).

sentence.da: Kagen er for **sød** for mig.
sentence.en: The cake is too sweet for me.

sødmælk.explanation: "Sødmælk" means "whole milk", the milk with the most fat. Despite sød (sweet) in the name, it is not sweet: Jeg bruger sødmælk i kaffen (I use whole milk in my coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vælger **sødmælk**, fordi den har mere fedt.
sentence.en: I choose whole milk because it has more fat.

sølle.explanation: "Sølle" means "measly", used for an amount or a thing that is too small or poor to be worth much. About a person it can mean "pathetic". The word never changes form.

sentence.da: Jeg fik kun en **sølle** halv time til at spise.
sentence.en: I only got a measly half hour to eat.

sølv.explanation: "Sølv" means "silver", both the metal and the color. In sports, it is also the second-place medal: Hun vandt sølv (She won silver).

sentence.da: Min ring er lavet af **sølv**.
sentence.en: My ring is made of silver.

sølvpapir.explanation: "Sølvpapir" means "aluminum foil", the shiny sheet you wrap food in. It is built from sølv (silver) and papir (paper). Despite the name, it is made of aluminum, not silver.

sentence.da: Jeg pakker kartoflerne ind i **sølvpapir**.
sentence.en: I wrap the potatoes in aluminum foil.

søndag.explanation: "Søndag" means "Sunday". Day names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish. Say på søndag (on Sunday) for this coming Sunday and om søndagen (on Sundays) for every Sunday.

sentence.da: Efter lørdag kommer **søndag**.
sentence.en: After Saturday comes Sunday.

sørgelig.explanation: "Sørgelig" means "sad" in the sense of a regrettable situation, not a feeling inside you. To say that you feel sad, use Jeg er ked af det (I am sad). It can also mean "pathetic" about a poor result: et sørgeligt resultat (a pathetic result).

sentence.da: Det var en **sørgelig** nyhed for hele familien.
sentence.en: That was a sad piece of news for the whole family.

sørgmodig.explanation: "Sørgmodig" means "sorrowful", a quiet sadness that shows in a face, a voice or a melody. You meet it mostly in writing and songs, while in everyday speech Danes say trist (sad).

sentence.da: Hendes stemme var **sørgmodig**, og alle i rummet blev stille.
sentence.en: Her voice was sorrowful, and everyone in the room went quiet.

søskende.explanation: "Søskende" means "siblings", brothers and sisters as a group. For one person, say en bror (a brother) or en søster (a sister).

sentence.da: Jeg har to **søskende**, en bror og en søster.
sentence.en: I have two siblings, a brother and a sister.

søvn.explanation: "Søvn" means "sleep", the rest your body gets at night. It is the thing itself, not the act of sleeping, so you get it or lack it: Jeg fik lidt søvn i nat (I got little sleep last night).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget træt og har brug for **søvn**.
sentence.en: I am very tired and need sleep.

søvnløshed.explanation: "Søvnløshed" means "insomnia", trouble falling asleep or staying asleep for many nights. It is built from søvn (sleep) and -løs (without), the same -løs as in hjemløs (homeless).

sentence.da: Efter flere nætter med **søvnløshed** var hun meget træt.
sentence.en: After several nights with insomnia she was very tired.
